title.zh: 卷八十九 列傳第七十七: 藝術上
title.raw: 卷八十九 列傳第七十七: 藝術上 Volume 89 Biographies 77: Diviners 1

sentences.zh: 藝術上

translations.literal: The Arts, Part One
translations.idiomatic: The Arts, Part One

sentences.zh: 列傳第七十七藝術上

translations.literal: Biography 77 — The Arts, Part One
translations.idiomatic: Biography 77: The Arts, Part One

sentences.zh: 晁崇張深殷紹王早耿玄劉靈助沙門靈遠李順興檀特師由吾道榮張遠遊顏惡頭王春信都芳宋景業許遵麹紹吳遵世趙輔和皇甫玉解法選魏甯綦母懷文張子信陸法和蔣升強練庾季才子質盧太翼耿詢來和蕭吉楊伯醜臨孝恭劉祐張胄玄

translations.literal: Chao Chong, Zhang Shen, Yin Shao, Wang Zao, Geng Xuan, Liu Lingzhu, the monk Lingyuan, Li Shunxing, Tante Shi, Youwu Daorong, Zhang Yuanyou, Yan Etou, Wang Chun, Xindu Fang, Song Jingye, Xu Zun, Qu Shao, Wu Zunshi, Zhao Fuhe, Huangfu Yu, Jiefa Xuan, Wei Ning, Qimou Huaiwen, Zhang Zixin, Lu Fahe, Jiang Sheng, Qiang Lian, Yu Jicai, Zi Zhi, Lu Taiyi, Geng Xun, Lai He, Xiao Ji, Yang Bochou, Lin Xiaogong, Liu You, Zhang Zhouxuan
translations.idiomatic: Chao Chong, Zhang Shen, Yin Shao, Wang Zao, Geng Xuan, Liu Lingzhu, the monk Lingyuan, Li Shunxing, Tante Shi, Youwu Daorong, Zhang Yuanyou, Yan Etou, Wang Chun, Xindu Fang, Song Jingye, Xu Zun, Qu Shao, Wu Zunshi, Zhao Fuhe, Huangfu Yu, Jiefa Xuan, Wei Ning, Qimou Huaiwen, Zhang Zixin, Lu Fahe, Jiang Sheng, Qiang Lian, Yu Jicai, Zi Zhi, Lu Taiyi, Geng Xun, Lai He, Xiao Ji, Yang Bochou, Lin Xiaogong, Liu You, and Zhang Zhouxuan

sentences.zh: 夫陰陽所以正時日，順氣序者也；

translations.literal: Now yin and yang are what set the days and months in order and align the sequence of the seasons;
translations.idiomatic: Yin and yang serve to regulate the calendar and harmonize the seasonal progression;

sentences.zh: 卜筮所以決嫌疑，定猶豫者也；

translations.literal: divination and milfoil stalk-casting are what resolve doubt and settle hesitation;
translations.idiomatic: divination resolves doubt and settles indecision;

sentences.zh: 醫巫所以禦妖邪，養性命者也；

translations.literal: physicians and shamans are what ward off demonic harm and nurture life;
translations.idiomatic: physicians and shamans ward off evil spirits and sustain life;

sentences.zh: 音律所以和人神，節哀樂者也；

translations.literal: pitch and rhythm are what harmonize human beings and spirits and regulate grief and joy;
translations.idiomatic: music harmonizes humanity with the divine and moderates sorrow and delight;

sentences.zh: 相術所以辨貴賤，明分理者也；

translations.literal: physiognomy is what distinguishes noble and base and clarifies proper distinctions;
translations.idiomatic: physiognomy distinguishes high and low station and clarifies what is fitting;

sentences.zh: 技巧所以利器用，濟艱難者也。

translations.literal: craft and ingenuity are what sharpen tools for use and relieve hardship.
translations.idiomatic: technical skill perfects instruments for use and helps overcome difficulty.

sentences.zh: 此皆聖人無心，因人設教，救恤災患，禁止淫邪，自三五哲王，其所由來久矣。

translations.literal: All these are matters in which the sages had no private intent: they established teachings according to people's needs, relieved disasters and afflictions, and forbade licentiousness and perversity — since the sage kings of the Three Dynasties, their origin has been long indeed.
translations.idiomatic: The sages pursued none of these arts for personal gain; they devised teachings to meet human need, to relieve calamity, and to restrain depravity. Their roots reach back to the sage rulers of antiquity.

sentences.zh: 昔之言陰陽者，則有箕子、裨灶、梓慎、子韋；

translations.literal: Of old those who spoke of yin and yang included Jizi, Pizao, Zishen, and Ziwei;
translations.idiomatic: Among the masters of yin and yang in antiquity were Jizi, Pizao, Zishen, and Ziwei;

sentences.zh: 曉音律者，則師曠、師摯、伯牙、杜夔；

translations.literal: those who understood pitch and rhythm included Shi Kuang, Shi Zhi, Boya, and Du Kui;
translations.idiomatic: those skilled in music included Shi Kuang, Shi Zhi, Boya, and Du Kui;

sentences.zh: 敘卜筮，則史扁、史蘇、嚴君平、司馬季主；

translations.literal: in recounting divination, there were Shi Bian, Shi Su, Yan Junping, and Sima Jizhu;
translations.idiomatic: in divination were Shi Bian, Shi Su, Yan Junping, and Sima Jizhu;

sentences.zh: 論相術，則內史叔服、姑布子卿、唐舉、許負；

translations.literal: in discussing physiognomy, there were Grand Clerk Shufu, Gubu Ziqing, Tang Ju, and Xu Fu;
translations.idiomatic: in physiognomy were Grand Clerk Shufu, Gubu Ziqing, Tang Ju, and Xu Fu;

sentences.zh: 語醫巫則文摯、扁鵲、季咸、華佗；

translations.literal: in speaking of physicians and shamans, there were Wen Zhi, Bian Que, Ji Xian, and Hua Tuo;
translations.idiomatic: among physicians and shamans were Wen Zhi, Bian Que, Ji Xian, and Hua Tuo;

sentences.zh: 其巧思，則奚仲、墨翟、張平子、馬德衡。

translations.literal: in ingenious craft, there were Xi Zhong, Mozi, Zhang Heng, and Ma Jun.
translations.idiomatic: in mechanical ingenuity were Xi Zhong, Mozi, Zhang Heng, and Ma Jun.

sentences.zh: 凡此諸君，莫不探靈入妙，理洞精微。

translations.literal: All these gentlemen, without exception, plumbed the numinous and entered the subtle; their grasp of principle penetrated the most refined.
translations.idiomatic: Every one of these masters penetrated the subtle and mysterious, with a command of principle that reached the finest depths.

sentences.zh: 或弘道以濟時，或隱身以利物，深不可測，固無得而稱矣。

translations.literal: Some spread the Way to aid the age; some hid themselves to benefit others — so deep as to be unfathomable, and truly beyond full praise.
translations.idiomatic: Some spread the Way to save their times; others withdrew from the world yet still served humanity. Their depths cannot be measured, and no praise can do them justice.

sentences.zh: 近古涉乎斯術者，鮮有存夫貞一，多肆其淫僻，厚誣天道。

translations.literal: In recent antiquity those who practiced these arts have rarely preserved integrity; most have indulged depravity and grossly slandered the Way of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: In later ages, few who took up these arts remained true to their purpose; most gave themselves to perversity and grossly misrepresented Heaven's will.

sentences.zh: 或變亂陰陽，曲成君欲；

translations.literal: some have distorted yin and yang and twisted them to satisfy a ruler's desires;
translations.idiomatic: Some have perverted yin and yang to gratify a ruler's whims;

sentences.zh: 或假託神怪，熒惑人心。

translations.literal: some have feigned spirits and prodigies and bewildered people's hearts.
translations.idiomatic: some have invoked false omens and spirits to delude the people.

sentences.zh: 遂令時俗妖訛，不獲返其真性，身罹災毒，莫得壽終而死。

translations.literal: Thus the customs of the age have grown demonic and confused, people cannot return to their true nature, their persons suffer calamity and poison, and they cannot die a full span of years.
translations.idiomatic: Custom has grown corrupt and deluded, people cannot recover their true selves, they suffer disaster and harm, and few die a natural death at the end of a full life.

sentences.zh: 藝成而下，意在茲乎！

translations.literal: "When the arts are complete, one descends" — the meaning lies here!
translations.idiomatic: The saying that the arts rank below the Way — its point is precisely this!

sentences.zh: 曆觀經史百家之言，無不存夫藝術。

translations.literal: Surveying the statements of the classics, histories, and the hundred schools, none fail to preserve material on these arts.
translations.idiomatic: A survey of the classics, histories, and masters shows that none omit these arts entirely.

sentences.zh: 或敘其玄妙，或記其迂誕，非徒用廣異聞，將以明乎勸戒。

translations.literal: Some narrate their profundity; some record their absurdity — not merely to broaden strange lore, but to make clear admonition and warning.
translations.idiomatic: Some relate their marvels, others their absurdities — not simply to entertain with wonders, but to teach by warning and example.

sentences.zh: 是以後來作者，咸相祖述。

translations.literal: Therefore later writers have all followed one another in the same tradition.
translations.idiomatic: Later historians have all followed this precedent.

sentences.zh: 自魏至隋，年移四代，至於遊心藝術，亦為多矣。

translations.literal: From Wei to Sui, years passed through four dynasties; those who devoted their hearts to these arts were also very numerous.
translations.idiomatic: From the Northern Wei through Sui, four dynasties passed, and many devoted themselves to these arts.

sentences.zh: 在魏，則敘晁崇、張深、殷紹、王早、耿玄、劉靈助、江式、周澹、李脩、徐謇、王顯、崔彧、蔣少遊，以為《術藝傳》；

translations.literal: In Wei, then, it narrates Chao Chong, Zhang Shen, Yin Shao, Wang Zao, Geng Xuan, Liu Lingzhu, Jiang Shi, Zhou Tan, Li Xiu, Xu Jian, Wang Xian, Cui Yu, and Jiang Shaoyou, making the 'Treatise on Arts and Skills';
translations.idiomatic: For Northern Wei, the work treats Chao Chong, Zhang Shen, Yin Shao, Wang Zao, Geng Xuan, Liu Lingzhu, Jiang Shi, Zhou Tan, Li Xiu, Xu Jian, Wang Xian, Cui Yu, and Jiang Shaoyou under the heading 'Treatise on Arts and Skills.'

sentences.zh: 在齊，則有由吾道榮、王春、信都芳、宋景業、許遵、吳遵世、趙輔和、皇甫玉、解法選、魏甯、綦母懷文、張子信、馬嗣明為《方伎傳》；

translations.literal: In Qi, then, there are Youwu Daorong, Wang Chun, Xindu Fang, Song Jingye, Xu Zun, Wu Zunshi, Zhao Fuhe, Huangfu Yu, Jiefa Xuan, Wei Ning, Qimou Huaiwen, Zhang Zixin, and Ma Siming as the 'Treatise on Occult Arts';
translations.idiomatic: For Northern Qi, Youwu Daorong, Wang Chun, Xindu Fang, Song Jingye, Xu Zun, Wu Zunshi, Zhao Fuhe, Huangfu Yu, Jiefa Xuan, Wei Ning, Qimou Huaiwen, Zhang Zixin, and Ma Siming appear in the 'Treatise on Occult Arts.'

sentences.zh: 在周，則有冀俊、蔣升、姚僧垣、黎景熙、趙文深、褚該、強練，以為《藝術傳》；

translations.literal: In Zhou, then, there are Ji Jun, Jiang Sheng, Yao Sengyuan, Li Jingxi, Zhao Wenshen, Chu Gai, and Qiang Lian, making the 'Treatise on Arts and Techniques';
translations.idiomatic: For Northern Zhou, Ji Jun, Jiang Sheng, Yao Sengyuan, Li Jingxi, Zhao Wenshen, Chu Gai, and Qiang Lian are gathered into the 'Treatise on Arts and Techniques.'

sentences.zh: 在隋，則有庾季才、盧太翼、耿詢、韋鼎、來和、蕭吉、張胄玄、許智藏、萬寶常為《藝術傳》。

translations.literal: In Sui, then, there are Yu Jicai, Lu Taiyi, Geng Xun, Wei Ding, Lai He, Xiao Ji, Zhang Zhouxuan, Xu Zhicang, and Wan Baochang as the 'Treatise on Arts and Techniques.'
translations.idiomatic: For Sui, Yu Jicai, Lu Taiyi, Geng Xun, Wei Ding, Lai He, Xiao Ji, Zhang Zhouxuan, Xu Zhicang, and Wan Baochang form the 'Treatise on Arts and Techniques.'

sentences.zh: 今檢江式、崔彧、冀俊、黎景熙、趙文深各編別傳。

translations.literal: Now, upon examination, Jiang Shi, Cui Yu, Ji Jun, Li Jingxi, and Zhao Wenshen are each compiled into separate biographies.
translations.idiomatic: On review, Jiang Shi, Cui Yu, Ji Jun, Li Jingxi, and Zhao Wenshen are each given their own separate biographies.

sentences.zh: 又檢得沙門靈遠、李順興、檀特師、顏惡頭，並以陸法和、徐之才、何稠附此篇，以備《藝術傳》。

translations.literal: Also found upon examination are the monks Lingyuan, Li Shunxing, Tante Shi, and Yan Etou; together with Lu Fahe, Xu Zhicai, and He Chou appended to this chapter, to complete the 'Treatise on Arts and Techniques.'
translations.idiomatic: Further examination also turned up the monks Lingyuan, Li Shunxing, Tante Shi, and Yan Etou, along with Lu Fahe, Xu Zhicai, and He Chou, all appended to this chapter to round out the 'Treatise on Arts and Techniques.'

sentences.zh: 前代著述，皆混而書之。

translations.literal: Writings of former ages all mixed them together in recording.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier dynasties, in their compilations, recorded such figures all together without distinction.

sentences.zh: 但道苟不同，則其流異。

translations.literal: But if the Way differs, then its streams diverge.
translations.idiomatic: Yet when the Way itself differs, the currents of learning diverge as well.

sentences.zh: 今各因其事，以類區分。

translations.literal: Now each is classified according to its matter, by category distinguished.
translations.idiomatic: Here, each subject is grouped by kind according to its proper field.

sentences.zh: 先載天文數術，次載醫方伎巧云。

translations.literal: First are recorded astronomy and numerology; next are recorded medical formulas, arts, and craft—thus.
translations.idiomatic: Astronomy and numerology come first; medical formulas, occult arts, and craftsmanship follow.

sentences.zh: 晁崇，字子業，遼東襄平人也。

translations.literal: Chao Chong, courtesy name Ziye, was a man of Xiangping in Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: Chao Chong, styled Ziye, was a native of Xiangping in Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 善天文術數，為慕容垂太史郎。

translations.literal: He was skilled in astronomy and numerology, and served as Grand Astrologer Gentleman to Murong Chui.
translations.idiomatic: Skilled in astronomy and the arts of calculation, he served Murong Chui as Grand Astrologer Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 從慕容寶敗於參合，為道武所獲。

translations.literal: Following Murong Bao's defeat at Canhe, he was captured by Emperor Daowu.
translations.idiomatic: When Murong Bao was defeated at Canhe, Chao Chong fell into the hands of Emperor Daowu.

sentences.zh: 從平中原，拜太史令。

translations.literal: Following the pacification of the Central Plains, he was appointed Grand Astrologer.
translations.idiomatic: After the Central Plains were brought to order, he was appointed Grand Astrologer.

sentences.zh: 詔崇造渾儀，遷中書侍郎，令如故。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Chong to construct an armillary sphere; he was promoted to Vice Director of the Secretariat, his original office retained as before.
translations.idiomatic: The throne commanded Chong to build an armillary sphere and promoted him to Vice Director of the Secretariat while leaving him in his former post.

sentences.zh: 天興五年，月暈左角，崇奏，占為角蟲將死。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Tianxing, the moon was haloed at its left horn; Chong memorialized that, by divination, horned creatures would soon die.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Tianxing, a halo appeared at the left horn of the moon. Chong submitted a memorial interpreting the omen: horned beasts were about to perish.

sentences.zh: 帝既克姚平于柴壁，以崇言之徵，遂命諸軍焚車而反。

translations.literal: The Emperor, having already conquered Yao Ping at Chaibi, took Chong's words as a verified sign and thereupon ordered the armies to burn their wagons and turn back.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor, fresh from his victory over Yao Ping at Chaibi, took Chong's prediction as confirmation and ordered the armies to burn their supply wagons and withdraw.

sentences.zh: 牛果大疫，輿駕所乘巨犗數百頭，亦同日斃于路側，自餘首尾相繼。

translations.literal: Cattle indeed suffered a great pestilence; several hundred great oxen drawing the imperial carriage died the same day by the roadside, and the rest followed one after another.
translations.idiomatic: Cattle did indeed fall victim to a great plague. Several hundred of the huge oxen that pulled the imperial train died that same day by the road, and countless others followed in succession.

sentences.zh: 是歲天下牛死者十七八，麋鹿亦多死。

translations.literal: That year, seven or eight tenths of the oxen in the realm died; elk and deer also died in great numbers.
translations.idiomatic: That year, seven or eight out of every ten oxen in the empire perished, and elk and deer died in great numbers as well.

sentences.zh: 崇弟懿，明辯而才不及崇。

translations.literal: Chong's younger brother Yi was sharp in debate, but his talent did not match Chong's.
translations.idiomatic: Chong's younger brother Yi was clever of tongue, though his gifts fell short of his brother's.

sentences.zh: 以善北人語，為黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: Because he was skilled in the languages of the northern peoples, he was made Vice Director of the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Skilled in the tongues of the northern peoples, he was appointed Vice Director of the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 懿好矜容儀，被服僭度，言音類帝，左右每聞其聲，莫不驚悚。

translations.literal: Yi loved to affect dignified bearing; his dress exceeded proper measure, and his speech sounded like the Emperor's—whenever those around him heard his voice, none failed to be startled and fearful.
translations.idiomatic: Yi was fond of striking a lordly pose. He dressed above his station, and his speech sounded so like the Emperor's that those who heard him nearby were invariably shaken with alarm.

sentences.zh: 帝知而惡之。

translations.literal: The Emperor learned of this and came to hate him.
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor learned of it, he came to loathe the man.

sentences.zh: 後其家奴告崇、懿叛，招引姚興。

translations.literal: Later a household slave of their family reported that Chong and Yi had rebelled and were inviting Yao Xing.
translations.idiomatic: Later a slave in their household accused Chong and Yi of treason, claiming they were summoning Yao Xing.

sentences.zh: 及興寇平陽，帝以奴言為實，執崇兄弟，並賜死。

translations.literal: When Xing raided Pingyang, the Emperor took the slave's words as true, seized the Chong brothers, and had them both executed by imperial command.
translations.idiomatic: When Yao Xing raided Pingyang, the Emperor accepted the slave's accusation as truth, seized the brothers, and had them both put to death by imperial decree.

sentences.zh: 張深，不知何許人也。

translations.literal: Zhang Shen—no one knows whence he came.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shen—of whose origins nothing is known.

sentences.zh: 明占候。

translations.literal: He was skilled in divination by celestial signs.
translations.idiomatic: He was accomplished in reading the heavens and forecasting events.

sentences.zh: 自雲，嘗事苻堅，堅欲征晉，深勸不行，堅不從，果敗。

translations.literal: He himself said that he had once served Fu Jian; when Jian wished to campaign against Jin, Shen urged against it, but Jian would not listen and was indeed defeated.
translations.idiomatic: He claimed to have served Fu Jian. When Jian planned an expedition against Jin, Shen urged him not to go; Jian refused, and was duly defeated.

sentences.zh: 又仕姚興為靈台令，姚泓滅，入赫連昌。

translations.literal: He also served Yao Xing as Director of the Spirit Tower; when Yao Hong was destroyed, he entered the service of Helian Chang.
translations.idiomatic: He later served Yao Xing as Director of the Spirit Tower. After Yao Hong's fall, he entered the service of Helian Chang.

sentences.zh: 昌復以深及徐辯對為太史令。

translations.literal: Chang again appointed Shen and Xu Bian as joint Grand Astrologers.
translations.idiomatic: Chang once more paired Shen with Xu Bian as Grand Astrologers.

sentences.zh: 統萬平，深、辯俱見獲，以深為太史令。

translations.literal: When Tongwan was pacified, Shen and Bian were both captured; Shen was made Grand Astrologer.
translations.idiomatic: When Tongwan fell, both Shen and Bian were taken captive, and Shen was appointed Grand Astrologer.

sentences.zh: 神抅二年，將討蠕蠕，深、辯皆謂不宜行，與崔浩爭于太武前。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shenqi, when a campaign against the Ruru was planned, both Shen and Bian said it should not be undertaken, and they disputed the matter before Emperor Taiwu with Cui Hao.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Shenqi, as an expedition against the Ruru was being prepared, Shen and Bian both argued that it should not be launched, and clashed with Cui Hao before Emperor Taiwu.

sentences.zh: 深專守常占，而不能鉤深賾遠，故不及浩。

translations.literal: Shen clung solely to routine divination and could not probe the deep and distant; therefore he did not match Hao.
translations.idiomatic: Shen adhered only to conventional readings of the heavens and could not reach into deeper, more distant meanings—hence he never equaled Hao.

sentences.zh: 後為驃騎軍謀祭酒，著《觀象賦》，其言星文甚備，文多不載。

translations.literal: Later he served as Libationer of Strategy for the Flying Cavalry Army and wrote 'Rhapsody on Observing the Heavens'; his words on the stars were very complete, though most of the text is not recorded here.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as Libationer of Strategy for the Flying Cavalry Army and composed the 'Rhapsody on Observing the Heavens,' a work rich in star lore, though much of it is not reproduced here.

sentences.zh: 又明元時，有容城令徐路，善占候，坐系冀州獄。

translations.literal: Also, in the time of Emperor Mingyuan, there was Xu Lu, magistrate of Rongcheng, skilled in divination by celestial signs; he was imprisoned in Ji Province.
translations.idiomatic: In Emperor Mingyuan's reign there was also Xu Lu, magistrate of Rongcheng, skilled in reading the heavens, who was imprisoned in Ji Province.

sentences.zh: 別駕崔隆宗就禁慰問之，路曰：「昨夜驛馬星流，計赦須臾應至。」

translations.literal: Vice Prefect Cui Longzong went to the prison to visit and comfort him; Lu said, 'Last night the Courier Star flowed—by my reckoning an amnesty should arrive in no time.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Prefect Cui Longzong visited him in prison to offer comfort. Lu said, 'Last night the Courier Star moved across the sky. By my reckoning, an amnesty should arrive at any moment.

sentences.zh: 隆宗先信之，遂遣人出城候焉，俄而赦至。

translations.literal: Longzong believed him beforehand and sent men out of the city to wait; before long the amnesty arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Longzong trusted him at once and sent men outside the city to watch for it—and soon the amnesty came.

sentences.zh: 又道武、明元時，太史令王亮、蘇垣，太武時，破和龍得馮弘太史令閔盛，孝文時，太史趙樊生，並知天文。

translations.literal: Also, in the times of Emperor Daowu and Emperor Mingyuan, Grand Astrologers Wang Liang and Su Yuan; in the time of Emperor Taiwu, Min Sheng, Grand Astrologer to Feng Hong, taken when Helong was captured; in the time of Emperor Xiaowen, Grand Astrologer Zhao Fansheng—all understood astronomy.
translations.idiomatic: In the reigns of Emperors Daowu and Mingyuan there were Grand Astrologers Wang Liang and Su Yuan; under Emperor Taiwu, Min Sheng, Feng Hong's Grand Astrologer, was taken when Helong fell; under Emperor Xiaowen, Grand Astrologer Zhao Fansheng—all were versed in astronomy.

sentences.zh: 後太史令趙勝、趙翼、趙洪慶、胡世榮、胡法通等二族，世業天文。

translations.literal: Later, among Grand Astrologers Zhao Sheng, Zhao Yi, Zhao Hongqing, Hu Shirong, Hu Fatong, and others, two clans carried on the profession of astronomy through the generations.
translations.idiomatic: Later, among Grand Astrologers Zhao Sheng, Zhao Yi, Zhao Hongqing, Hu Shirong, Hu Fatong, and others, two families maintained astronomy as a hereditary calling.

sentences.zh: 又永安中，詔以恆州人高崇祖善天文，每占吉凶有驗，特除中散大夫。

translations.literal: Also, in the Yong'an era, an edict noted that Gao Chongzu of Heng Province was skilled in astronomy and that his prognostications of fortune and misfortune had repeatedly proved true; he was specially appointed Palace Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yong'an era, an edict singled out Gao Chongzu of Heng Province, whose readings of fortune and misfortune had repeatedly come true, and specially appointed him Palace Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 永熙中，詔通直散騎常侍孫僧化與太史胡世榮、太史令張寵、趙洪慶及中書舍人孫子良等在門下外省，校比天文書，集甘、石二家星經，及漢、魏以來二十三家經占，集五十五卷。

translations.literal: In the Yongxi era, an edict ordered Attendant-in-Ordinary Sun Sengua, Grand Astrologer Hu Shirong, Grand Astrologer Zhang Chong, Zhao Hongqing, and Secretariat Gentleman Sun Ziliang and others, in the Outer Office of the Secretariat-Chancellery, to collate and compare books on astronomy, gathering the star classic of the Gan and Shi schools and the prognostic texts of twenty-three schools from Han and Wei down, in fifty-five volumes.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yongxi era, an edict directed Attendant-in-Ordinary Sun Sengua, Grand Astrologer Hu Shirong, Grand Astrologer Zhang Chong, Zhao Hongqing, and Secretariat Gentleman Sun Ziliang and others, working in the Outer Office of the Secretariat-Chancellery, to collate astronomical texts—collecting the star classic of the Gan and Shi schools and the prognostic writings of twenty-three traditions from Han and Wei onward into fifty-five volumes.

sentences.zh: 後集諸家撮要，前後所上雜占，以類相從，日月、五星、二十八宿、中外官及圖，合為七十五卷。

translations.literal: Later they gathered selected essentials from various schools and miscellaneous prognostications submitted earlier and later, arranged by category—sun and moon, the five planets, the twenty-eight lodges, inner and outer asterisms, and charts—altogether seventy-five volumes.
translations.idiomatic: They later compiled selected essentials from the various schools, together with miscellaneous prognostications submitted over the years, arranged by category—sun and moon, the five planets, the twenty-eight lodges, inner and outer asterisms, and charts—seventy-five volumes in all.

sentences.zh: 僧化，東莞人也。

translations.literal: Sengua was a man of Dongguan.
translations.idiomatic: Sengua was a native of Dongguan.

sentences.zh: 識星分，案文占以言災異，時有所中。

translations.literal: He knew the divisions of the stars and, consulting texts to prognosticate calamities and anomalies, sometimes hit the mark.
translations.idiomatic: He knew the divisions of the heavens and, drawing on written lore to foretell calamities and portents, sometimes proved right.

sentences.zh: 普泰中，爾硃兆惡其多言，遂系于廷尉，免官。

translations.literal: In the Putai era, Erzhu Rong hated his excessive talk and had him imprisoned by the Minister of Justice; he was dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: In the Putai era, Erzhu Rong, weary of his loose tongue, had him thrown into the Minister of Justice's prison and stripped of office.

sentences.zh: 永熙中，孝武帝召僧化與中散大夫孫安都共撰兵法，未就而帝入關，遂罷。

translations.literal: In the Yongxi era, Emperor Xiaowu summoned Sengua and Palace Gentleman Sun An'du to compile a treatise on military strategy together; before it was finished the Emperor entered the Passes, and the work was abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yongxi era, Emperor Xiaowu summoned Sengua and Palace Gentleman Sun An'du to draft a military treatise together, but before it was finished the Emperor withdrew into the Passes and the project was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 元象中，死于晉陽。

translations.literal: In the Yuanxiang era, he died at Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yuanxiang era he died at Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 殷紹，長樂人也。

translations.literal: Yin Shao was a man of Changle.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Shao was a native of Changle.

sentences.zh: 達《九章》、《七曜》。

translations.literal: He mastered the 'Nine Chapters' and the 'Seven Luminaries.'
translations.idiomatic: He had mastered the 'Nine Chapters' and the 'Seven Luminaries.'

sentences.zh: 太武時，為算生博士，給事東宮西曹。

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Taiwu, he served as Doctor of Calculators and Attendant in the Western Bureau of the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Taiwu he served as Doctor of Calculators and Attendant in the Western Bureau of the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 太安四年，上《四序堪輿》，表言：「以姚氏之時，行學伊川，遇游遁大儒成公興，從求《九章》要術。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Tai'an, he submitted 'The Four Seasons of Geomancy,' memorializing: 'During the time of the Yao clan, while studying on the Yichuan, I encountered the wandering recluse and great scholar Cheng Gongxing and sought from him the essential techniques of the 'Nine Chapters.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Tai'an he submitted 'The Four Seasons of Geomancy,' writing in his memorial: 'In the days of the Yao clan, while pursuing my studies on the Yichuan, I met the wandering recluse and great scholar Cheng Gongxing and sought from him the essential techniques of the 'Nine Chapters.

sentences.zh: 興字廣明，自雲膠東人也，山居隱跡，希在人間。

translations.literal: Xing's courtesy name was Guangming; he said himself that he was a man of Jiaodong, dwelling in the mountains in hidden seclusion, rarely appearing among men.
translations.idiomatic: Xing, styled Guangming, claimed to be from Jiaodong. He lived hidden in the mountains and seldom showed himself in the world of men.

sentences.zh: 興將臣到陽翟九崖岩沙門釋曇影間，興即北還。

translations.literal: When Xing was about to take your subject to the monk Shiying at Jiuyai Cliff in Yangdi, Xing turned north and returned.
translations.idiomatic: When Xing was about to bring your subject to the monk Shiying at Jiuyai Cliff in Yangdi, Xing turned north and went back.

sentences.zh: 臣獨留住，依止影所，求請《九章》。

translations.literal: Your subject alone remained, relying on Shiying's place, and requested the 'Nine Chapters.'
translations.idiomatic: Your subject alone remained, lodging with Shiying and begging instruction in the 'Nine Chapters.'

sentences.zh: 影復將臣向長廣東山，就道人法穆。

translations.literal: Shiying then led your subject east to Mount Dong in Changguang, to seek out the Daoist Famu.
translations.idiomatic: Shiying then led your subject to Mount Dong in Changguang to seek out the Daoist Famu.

sentences.zh: 法穆時共影為臣開述《九章》數家雜要。

translations.literal: Famu, together with Shiying, then expounded for your subject the assorted essentials of several schools of the 'Nine Chapters.'
translations.idiomatic: Famu, together with Shiying, then opened for your subject the assorted essentials of several schools of the 'Nine Chapters.'

sentences.zh: 復以先師和公所注黃帝《四序經》文三十六卷，合有三百二十四章，專說天地陰陽之本。

translations.literal: He also had the thirty-six volumes of text from the Yellow Emperor's 'Classic of the Four Seasons,' annotated by my former master Master He, altogether three hundred twenty-four chapters, devoted solely to the roots of yin and yang in Heaven and Earth.
translations.idiomatic: He also possessed thirty-six volumes of the Yellow Emperor's 'Classic of the Four Seasons,' as annotated by my former master Master He—three hundred twenty-four chapters in all, devoted entirely to the fundamental roots of yin and yang in Heaven and Earth.

sentences.zh: 其第一，孟序，九卷八十一章，說陰陽配合之原；

translations.literal: The first, the Sequence of the First Month, nine volumes and eighty-one chapters, explains the origin of the pairing of yin and yang;
translations.idiomatic: The first part, the Sequence of the First Month—nine volumes and eighty-one chapters—explains the origin of yin-yang pairing;

sentences.zh: 第二，仲序，九卷八十一章，解四時氣王，休殺吉凶；

translations.literal: the second, the Sequence of the Second Month, nine volumes and eighty-one chapters, explains the dominance and decline of the four seasons' qi, and the auspice and bane of rest and killing;
translations.idiomatic: the second, the Sequence of the Second Month—nine volumes and eighty-one chapters—explains how the qi of the four seasons wax and wane, and the fortune or misfortune of rest and killing;

sentences.zh: 第三，叔序，九卷八十一章，明日月辰宿，交會相生為表裏；

translations.literal: the third, the Sequence of the Third Month, nine volumes and eighty-one chapters, clarifies the sun, moon, stars, and lodges, their conjunctions and mutual generation as inner and outer;
translations.idiomatic: the third, the Sequence of the Third Month—nine volumes and eighty-one chapters—clarifies the sun, moon, stars, and lodges, their conjunctions and mutual generation as inner and outer counterparts;

sentences.zh: 第四，季序，九卷八十一章，具釋六甲，刑禍福德。

translations.literal: the fourth, the Sequence of the Fourth Month, nine volumes and eighty-one chapters, fully explains the six jia, punishment, calamity, and blessing.
translations.idiomatic: the fourth, the Sequence of the Fourth Month—nine volumes and eighty-one chapters—fully explains the six jia, punishment, calamity, and blessing.

sentences.zh: 以此經文，傳授於臣。

translations.literal: With this classic text, he transmitted it to your subject.
translations.idiomatic: With this scripture he passed the teaching on to your subject.

sentences.zh: 山神禁嚴，不得齎出。

translations.literal: The mountain spirits forbade it strictly; it could not be carried out.
translations.idiomatic: The mountain spirits guarded it with strict prohibition; it could not be taken away.

sentences.zh: 尋究經年，粗舉綱要。

translations.literal: Your subject studied it for a year and roughly grasped its main outlines.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject pursued it for a full year and roughly grasped its main outlines.

sentences.zh: 山居險難，無以自供，不堪窘迫，心生懈怠。

translations.literal: Life in the mountains was perilous and hard; there was no means of self-support, and unable to bear the straits, your subject's heart grew slack.
translations.idiomatic: Mountain life was perilous and harsh. With no way to sustain himself, and unable to endure the hardship, your subject's resolve slackened.

sentences.zh: 以甲寅之年，日維鶉火，感物懷歸。

translations.literal: In the year jiayin, when the day was lodged in Quail Fire, moved by things, your subject longed for home.
translations.idiomatic: In the jiayin year, when the day-stem was lodged in Quail Fire, stirred by all he had seen, your subject yearned to return home.

sentences.zh: 自爾至今，二十五載。

translations.literal: From then until now, twenty-five years.
translations.idiomatic: From that time to the present, twenty-five years have passed.

sentences.zh: 臣前在東宮，以狀奏聞，奉被景穆皇帝聖詔，敕臣撰錄，集其要最。

translations.literal: Your subject, formerly in the Eastern Palace, submitted a report to inform the throne; he received the sacred edict of Emperor Jingmu, commanding your subject to compile and record, gathering its most essential points.
translations.idiomatic: While serving in the Eastern Palace, your subject submitted a report to the throne and received the sacred edict of Emperor Jingmu, commanding him to compile and set down its most essential points.

sentences.zh: 仰奉明旨，謹審先所見《四序經》文，抄撮要略，當世所須吉凶舉動，集成一卷。

translations.literal: Reverently obeying the clear command, your subject carefully examined the previously seen text of the 'Classic of the Four Seasons,' copied out the essential outlines, and gathered into one volume what the age requires for actions of fortune and misfortune.
translations.idiomatic: Reverently obeying that clear command, your subject carefully reviewed the 'Classic of the Four Seasons' as he had received it, extracted its essential outlines, and gathered into one volume what the age requires for actions of fortune and misfortune.

sentences.zh: 上至天子，下及庶人，貴賤等級，尊卑差別，吉凶所用，罔不畢備。

translations.literal: From the Son of Heaven above down to the common people below, noble and base in rank, high and low in station—the uses of fortune and misfortune are nowhere incomplete.
translations.idiomatic: From the Son of Heaven above to the common people below, high and low in rank, noble and humble in station—nothing needed for reading fortune and misfortune is left out.

sentences.zh: 未及內呈，先帝晏駕。

translations.literal: Before it could be presented within the palace, the late Emperor passed away.
translations.idiomatic: Before it could be presented at court, the late Emperor passed away.

sentences.zh: 依先撰錄，謹以上聞。」

translations.literal: According to the earlier compilation, your subject respectfully submits this report.'
translations.idiomatic: Following the earlier compilation, your subject respectfully submits this report.

sentences.zh: 共《四序堪輿》遂大行於世。

translations.literal: Together with 'The Four Seasons of Geomancy,' it then spread widely in the world.
translations.idiomatic: Thus 'The Four Seasons of Geomancy' went forth and circulated widely in the world.

sentences.zh: 其從子玖，亦以學術著名。

translations.literal: His nephew Jiu was also renowned for scholarship.
translations.idiomatic: His nephew Jiu was likewise famed for learning.

sentences.zh: 王早，勃海南皮人也。

translations.literal: Wang Zao was a man of Nanpi in Bohai.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zao was a native of Nanpi in Bohai.

sentences.zh: 明陰陽、九宮及兵法，善風角。

translations.literal: He understood yin and yang, the Nine Palaces, and military strategy, and was skilled in wind divination.
translations.idiomatic: He mastered yin and yang, the Nine Palaces, and the art of war, and was adept at wind divination.

sentences.zh: 明元時，喪亂之後，有人詣早，求問勝術。

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Mingyuan, after the chaos of war and disorder, someone came to Wang Zao seeking techniques for victory.
translations.idiomatic: During Emperor Mingyuan's reign, after the devastation of war, a man came to Wang Zao to ask for methods of victory.

sentences.zh: 早為設法，令各無咎，由是州裏稱之。

translations.literal: Wang Zao devised methods for him so that each would be without calamity; thereby he was praised throughout the district.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zao devised rites for him so that each undertaking would pass without harm, and from that time he was praised throughout the district.

sentences.zh: 時有東莞鄭氏，執得仇人趙氏，克明晨會宗族，當就墓所刑之。

translations.literal: At that time the Zheng clan of Dongguan had seized their enemy Zhao; at dawn the next morning they would assemble the clan and execute him at the ancestral tomb.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Zheng clan of Dongguan had taken their enemy Zhao captive. At dawn the next morning they would gather the clan and put him to death at the family grave.

sentences.zh: 趙氏求救於早。

translations.literal: Zhao appealed to Wang Zao for help.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao appealed to Wang Zao for rescue.

sentences.zh: 早為占候，並授以一符曰：「君今且還，選取七人，令一人為行主者佩此符，于雞鳴時，伏在仇家宅東南二里。

translations.literal: Wang Zao performed divination and also gave him a talisman, saying, 'Return home now, select seven men, and let one of them, who shall be leader of the party, wear this talisman. At cockcrow lie in wait two li southeast of your enemy's house.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zao read the signs and gave him a talisman as well, saying, 'Go home now. Choose seven men and have one of them—the leader of the party—wear this talisman. At cockcrow, lie in ambush two li southeast of your enemy's house.

sentences.zh: 平旦，當有十人相隨向西北，行中有二人乘黑牛，一黑牛最在前，一黑牛應第七。

translations.literal: At daybreak ten men will come together heading northwest. Among them two will ride black oxen—one black ox foremost, and the black ox corresponding to the seventh man.
translations.idiomatic: At daybreak ten men will walk together toward the northwest. Two among them will ride black oxen—one black ox at the head of the line, and one black ox beside the seventh man.

sentences.zh: 但捉取第七者將還，事必無他。」

translations.literal: Simply seize the seventh man and bring him back; the affair will surely have no further trouble.
translations.idiomatic: Seize only the seventh man and bring him back, and the matter will surely end without further harm.

sentences.zh: 趙氏從之，果如其言。

translations.literal: Zhao followed this, and it happened exactly as Wang Zao had said.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao did as he was told, and events unfolded exactly as Wang Zao had foretold.

sentences.zh: 乃是鄭氏男五父也，諸子並為其族所宗敬，故和解二家，趙氏竟免。

translations.literal: It was Wu Fu, a son of the Zheng clan; the sons were all revered by their clan, so the two families were reconciled and Zhao was spared in the end.
translations.idiomatic: The man was Wu Fu, a son of the Zheng clan. Because the sons were all held in honor by their kin, the two families were reconciled and Zhao was spared.

sentences.zh: 後早與客清晨立於門內，遇有卒風振樹，早語客曰：「依法當有千里外急使。

translations.literal: Later Wang Zao was standing inside the gate with a guest early in the morning when a sudden wind shook the trees. Wang Zao told the guest, 'According to the method, there should be an urgent messenger from a thousand li away.
translations.idiomatic: Later, early one morning, Wang Zao was standing inside his gate with a guest when a sudden gust shook the trees. Wang Zao said to the guest, 'By the rules of my art, an urgent messenger should be coming from a thousand li away.

sentences.zh: 日中時，有兩匹馬，一白一赤，從西南來，至即取我，逼我不聽與妻子別。」

translations.literal: At midday two horses, one white and one red, will come from the southwest. As soon as they arrive they will take me, pressing me so that I will not be allowed to bid farewell to my wife and children.
translations.idiomatic: At midday two horses, one white and one red, will come from the southwest. The moment they arrive they will take me away and will not even let me say farewell to my wife and children.

sentences.zh: 語訖便入，召家人鄰里辭別，仍沐浴帶書囊，日中出門候使。

translations.literal: When he finished speaking he went inside, summoned family and neighbors to say farewell, bathed and took up a book satchel, and at midday went out to wait for the messenger.
translations.idiomatic: When he had finished speaking he went inside, called his family and neighbors to take leave of them, bathed, took up a book satchel, and at midday went out to await the messenger.

sentences.zh: 如期，果有馬一白一赤，從州而至，即促早上馬，遂詣行宮。

translations.literal: As expected, indeed two horses, one white and one red, came from the provincial capital. They immediately urged Wang Zao onto horseback, and he proceeded to the imperial mobile palace.
translations.idiomatic: At the appointed time two horses, one white and one red, came from the provincial capital. They at once pressed Wang Zao to mount and rode with him to the imperial camp.

sentences.zh: 時太武圍涼州未拔，故許彥薦之。

translations.literal: At that time Emperor Taiwu was besieging Liangzhou but had not taken it, so Xu Yan recommended him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taiwu was then besieging Liangzhou without success, and Xu Yan recommended Wang Zao to him.

sentences.zh: 早，彥師也。

translations.literal: Wang Zao was Xu's teacher.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zao had been Xu's teacher.

sentences.zh: 及至，詔問何時當克此城。

translations.literal: When he arrived, the Emperor asked by edict when the city would be taken.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Zao arrived, the Emperor asked by edict when the city would fall.

sentences.zh: 早對曰：「陛下但移據西北角，三日內必克。」

translations.literal: Wang Zao replied, 'Your Majesty need only move camp to the northwest corner; within three days it will surely be taken.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zao answered, 'Your Majesty need only shift your camp to the northwest corner, and within three days the city will surely fall.

sentences.zh: 帝從之，如期而克。

translations.literal: The Emperor followed his advice, and the city was taken on schedule.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor did as he advised, and the city fell on the day foretold.

sentences.zh: 輿駕還都，久不雨，帝問早。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage returned to the capital, there had been no rain for a long time. The Emperor asked Wang Zao.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial procession returned to the capital, rain had long been absent, and the Emperor questioned Wang Zao.

sentences.zh: 早曰：「今日申時必大雨。」

translations.literal: Wang Zao said, 'At the shen hour today there will surely be heavy rain.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zao said, 'At the shen hour today there will surely be a great downpour.

sentences.zh: 比至未，猶無片雲，帝召早詰之。

translations.literal: By the time it reached the wei hour, still not a single cloud. The Emperor summoned Wang Zao and questioned him.
translations.idiomatic: By the wei hour not a cloud had appeared, and the Emperor summoned Wang Zao to reproach him.

sentences.zh: 早曰：「願更少時。」

translations.literal: Wang Zao said, 'I ask for a little more time.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zao said, 'I beg Your Majesty to grant me a little more time.

sentences.zh: 至申時，雲四合，遂大雨滂沱。

translations.literal: When the shen hour came, clouds gathered from all four quarters, and then rain poured down in torrents.
translations.idiomatic: When the shen hour came, clouds closed in from every side and rain fell in torrents.

sentences.zh: 早苦以疾辭，乞歸鄉里。

translations.literal: Wang Zao pleaded illness with difficulty and requested to return to his native place.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zao pleaded illness and begged to return to his home district.

sentences.zh: 詔許之，遂終於家。

translations.literal: An edict granted this, and he died at home.
translations.idiomatic: An edict granted his request, and he died at home.

sentences.zh: 或言許彥以其術勝，恐終紡己，譎令歸之耳。

translations.literal: Some said that Xu Yan, because Wang Zao's art was superior, feared he would ultimately harm him, and deceived the Emperor into sending him home—that is all.
translations.idiomatic: Some said that Xu Yan, seeing Wang Zao's art surpass his own, feared Wang would eventually prove his undoing and therefore tricked the court into sending him home.

sentences.zh: 耿玄，钜鹿宋子人也。

translations.literal: Geng Xuan was a man of Songzi in Julu.
translations.idiomatic: Geng Xuan was a native of Songzi in Julu.

sentences.zh: 善卜占。

translations.literal: He was skilled in divination.
translations.idiomatic: He was skilled in divination.

sentences.zh: 有客叩門，玄在室已知其姓字，並所齎持及來問之意。

translations.literal: When a guest knocked at the door, Geng Xuan already knew from inside his room the guest's surname and given name, what he had brought, and the purpose of his visit.
translations.idiomatic: When a guest knocked at the door, Geng Xuan already knew from within his room the visitor's name, what he carried, and what he had come to ask.

sentences.zh: 其所卜筮，十中八九。

translations.literal: Of his divinations, eight or nine out of ten came true.
translations.idiomatic: Eight or nine of every ten of his divinations proved true.

sentences.zh: 別有《林占》，時或傳之。

translations.literal: He also had a work called 'Forest Divination,' which circulated from time to time.
translations.idiomatic: He also possessed a work called 'Forest Divination,' which circulated from time to time.

sentences.zh: 而性不和俗，時有王公欲求其筮者，玄則拒而不許。

translations.literal: But his nature was not in harmony with common custom. When nobles and princes wished to consult his divination, Geng Xuan would refuse and not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: But his temperament set him against the ways of the world. When nobles and princes sought his divination, Geng Xuan refused them.

sentences.zh: 每云：「今既貴矣，何所求而復卜也？

translations.literal: He would always say, 'Now that you are already honored, what do you seek that you must divine again?
translations.idiomatic: He would always say, 'You are already exalted—what is left to seek that you must consult the oracle again?

sentences.zh: 欲望意外乎？」

translations.literal: Do you desire the unexpected?
translations.idiomatic: Do you crave the unforeseen?

sentences.zh: 代京法禁嚴切，王公聞之，莫不驚悚而退。

translations.literal: In the capital of Dai the laws and prohibitions were strict and severe. When nobles and princes heard this, none failed to retreat in shock and fear.
translations.idiomatic: In the capital of Dai the laws were stern and close. When nobles and princes heard this, none failed to withdraw in alarm.

sentences.zh: 故玄多見憎忿，不為貴勝所親。

translations.literal: Thus Geng Xuan was often hated in anger and was not favored by the powerful and eminent.
translations.idiomatic: For this reason Geng Xuan was often met with resentment and found no favor among the great.

sentences.zh: 官止钜鹿太守。

translations.literal: His official rank went no higher than Administrator of Julu.
translations.idiomatic: His highest office was Administrator of Julu.

sentences.zh: 劉靈助，燕郡人也。

translations.literal: Liu Lingzhu was a man of Yan Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Lingzhu was a native of Yan Commandery.

sentences.zh: 師事范陽劉弁，而粗疏無賴。

translations.literal: He studied under Liu Bian of Fanyang but was crude, careless, and worthless.
translations.idiomatic: He studied under Liu Bian of Fanyang, but he was coarse, undisciplined, and good for nothing.

sentences.zh: 或時負販，或復劫盜，賣術於市。

translations.literal: Sometimes he peddled goods, sometimes he robbed; he sold his arts in the market.
translations.idiomatic: At times he hawked goods; at other times he turned to robbery. He sold his arts in the marketplace.

sentences.zh: 後事爾硃榮，榮信卜筮，靈助所占屢中，遂被親待，為榮府功曹參軍。

translations.literal: Later he served Erzhu Rong. Rong believed in divination; Lingzhu's predictions repeatedly proved correct, so he was treated with favor and became Staff Officer for Records in Rong's household.
translations.idiomatic: Later he entered the service of Erzhu Rong. Rong trusted divination, and Lingzhu's readings repeatedly came true, so Rong treated him with favor and made him Staff Officer for Records in his household.

sentences.zh: 建義初，榮于河陰害王公卿士。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Jianyi era, Rong killed nobles and ministers at Heyin.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Jianyi era, Rong slaughtered the nobles and ministers at Heyin.

sentences.zh: 時奉車都尉盧道虔兄弟，亦相率朝行宮，靈助以其州裏，衛護之。

translations.literal: At that time Colonel of Following Chariots Lu Daojian and his brothers also led each other to attend the mobile palace. Lingzhu protected them as fellow townsmen.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Colonel of Following Chariots Lu Daojian and his brothers were also making their way together to the imperial camp. Lingzhu shielded them as men of his own district.

sentences.zh: 由是朝士與諸盧相隨免害者數十人。

translations.literal: Hence dozens of court officials and members of the Lu clan who followed them escaped harm.
translations.idiomatic: By this means several dozen court officials and members of the Lu clan who went with them escaped death.

sentences.zh: 榮入京師，超拜光祿大夫，封長子縣公。

translations.literal: When Rong entered the capital, Lingzhu was promoted extraordinary to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and enfeoffed as Duke of Changzi County.
translations.idiomatic: When Rong entered the capital, Lingzhu was promoted out of turn to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and enfeoffed as Duke of Changzi County.

sentences.zh: 從上党王元天穆討邢杲。

translations.literal: He followed Shangdang Wang Yuan Tianmu to campaign against Xing Gao.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Shangdang Wang Yuan Tianmu in the campaign against Xing Gao.

sentences.zh: 元顥入洛，天穆度河，會爾硃榮於太行。

translations.literal: Yuan Hao entered Luoyang; Tianmu crossed the river and met Erzhu Rong at Taihang.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Hao entered Luoyang. Tianmu crossed the river and joined Erzhu Rong at Taihang.

sentences.zh: 及將攻河內，令靈助筮之。

translations.literal: When they were about to attack Henei, Rong had Lingzhu divine the outcome.
translations.idiomatic: When they were about to attack Henei, Rong had Lingzhu cast the oracle.

sentences.zh: 靈助曰：「未時必克。」

translations.literal: Lingzhu said, 'At the wei hour it will surely be taken.
translations.idiomatic: Lingzhu said, 'At the wei hour the city will surely fall.

sentences.zh: 時已向中，士眾疲怠，靈助曰：「時將至矣！」

translations.literal: The time was already approaching noon and the troops were weary. Lingzhu said, 'The hour approaches!'
translations.idiomatic: The day was already past noon and the troops were exhausted. Lingzhu cried, 'The hour is nearly here!'

sentences.zh: 榮鼓之，即便克陷。

translations.literal: Rong beat the drums, and immediately they broke through and captured it.
translations.idiomatic: Rong sounded the drums, and at once the city was stormed and taken.

sentences.zh: 及至北中，榮攻城不獲。

translations.literal: When they reached Beizhong, Rong besieged the city but could not take it.
translations.idiomatic: When they reached Beizhong, Rong laid siege to the city but could not capture it.

sentences.zh: 以時盛暑，議欲且還，以待秋涼。

translations.literal: Because it was the height of summer, they deliberated returning for the time being to wait for autumn cool.
translations.idiomatic: The season was fiercely hot, and they debated withdrawing for the time being to wait for the cool of autumn.

sentences.zh: 莊帝詔靈助筮之。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhuang had Lingzhu divine it.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhuang ordered Lingzhu to divine the outcome.

sentences.zh: 靈助曰：「必破，十八九間。」

translations.literal: Lingzhu said, 'It will surely fall—between the eighteenth and nineteenth.
translations.idiomatic: Lingzhu said, 'It will surely fall—between the eighteenth and nineteenth days.

sentences.zh: 果如言。

translations.literal: It happened exactly as he said.
translations.idiomatic: Events unfolded exactly as he had said.

sentences.zh: 車駕還宮，進爵燕郡公，贈其父僧安為幽州刺史。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage returned to the palace, Lingzhu was advanced in rank to Duke of Yan Commandery; his father Seng'an was posthumously appointed Governor of You Province.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial procession returned to the palace, Lingzhu was raised to Duke of Yan Commandery, and his father Seng'an was posthumously appointed Governor of You Province.

sentences.zh: 尋兼尚書左僕射，慰勞幽州流人。

translations.literal: Soon he also served concurrently as Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat, to comfort and reassure refugees from You Province.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he also served concurrently as Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat, charged with comforting the refugees of You Province.

sentences.zh: 北還，與都督侯深等討葛榮餘黨韓婁，滅之於薊。

translations.literal: Returning north, together with Area Commander Hou Shen and others he campaigned against Han Lou, a remnant of Ge Rong's faction, and destroyed him at Ji.
translations.idiomatic: On his return north he joined Area Commander Hou Shen and others in campaigning against Han Lou, a remnant of Ge Rong's forces, and destroyed him at Ji.

sentences.zh: 仍厘州務，又為幽、并、營、安四州行台。

translations.literal: He continued to put provincial affairs in order and also served as itinerant commissioner for the four provinces of You, Bing, Ying, and An.
translations.idiomatic: He continued to set provincial affairs in order and also served as itinerant commissioner for the four provinces of You, Bing, Ying, and An.

sentences.zh: 及爾硃榮死，莊帝幽崩，靈助本寒微，一朝至此，自謂方術堪能動眾，又以爾硃有誅滅之兆，遂自號燕王、大行台，為莊帝舉義兵。

translations.literal: When Erzhu Rong died and Emperor Zhuang died in secret confinement, Lingzhu, who had come from humble origins to this height in a single morning, believed his arts could move the masses. He also saw omens of the Erzhu clan's destruction, so he styled himself King of Yan and Grand Itinerant Commissioner, raising righteous troops for Emperor Zhuang.
translations.idiomatic: When Erzhu Rong died and Emperor Zhuang perished in confinement, Lingzhu—who had risen overnight from humble origins to such eminence—believed his arts could stir the people. He also read in the signs that the Erzhu were marked for destruction, and so styled himself King of Yan and Grand Itinerant Commissioner, raising righteous troops in Emperor Zhuang's name.

sentences.zh: 馴養大鳥，稱為己瑞，妄說圖讖，言劉氏當王。

translations.literal: He trained large birds and called them his auguries; he recklessly propounded chart apocrypha, saying the Liu clan should rule as kings.
translations.idiomatic: He reared great birds and called them his heavenly portents; he spread false prophecies from the charts, declaring that the Liu house was destined to reign.

sentences.zh: 又云：「欲知避世入鳥村。」

translations.literal: He also said, 'If you wish to know how to flee the world, enter Bird Village.
translations.idiomatic: He also proclaimed, 'If you would know how to flee the world, enter Bird Village.

sentences.zh: 遂刻氈為人象，書桃木為符書，作詭道厭祝法，人多信之。

translations.literal: He then carved felt into human effigies, wrote charms on peachwood, and devised sorcerous rites of curse and prayer—and many believed him.
translations.idiomatic: He carved felt into human images, wrote talismans on peachwood, and devised sorcerous rites of curse and prayer—and many believed him.

sentences.zh: 時西河人紇豆陵步籓，舉兵逼晉陽，爾硃兆頻戰不利。

translations.literal: At that time Bedouling Bufan of Xihe raised troops and pressed upon Jinyang; Erzhu Zhao repeatedly fought without success.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Bedouling Bufan of Xihe raised an army and pressed on Jinyang, while Erzhu Zhao fought again and again without victory.

sentences.zh: 故靈助唱言：「爾硃自然當滅，不須我兵。」

translations.literal: So Lingzhu proclaimed, 'The Erzhu will perish of themselves; my troops are not needed.
translations.idiomatic: Lingzhu therefore proclaimed, 'The Erzhu will perish of their own accord—my army need not strike.

sentences.zh: 由是幽、瀛、滄、冀人悉從之。

translations.literal: Hence people of You, Ying, Cang, and Ji all followed him.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the people of You, Ying, Cang, and Ji all rallied to him.

sentences.zh: 從之者，夜舉火為號；

translations.literal: Those who followed raised fires at night as signals;
translations.idiomatic: Those who joined him lit fires by night as signals;

sentences.zh: 不舉火者，諸村共屠之。

translations.literal: those who did not raise fires were jointly slaughtered by the villages.
translations.idiomatic: any village that failed to light a fire was jointly put to the sword by its neighbors.

sentences.zh: 普泰元年，率眾至博陵之安國城，與叱列延慶、侯深，爾硃羽生等戰。

translations.literal: In the first year of Putai, he led his forces to Anguo City in Boling and fought with Chilie Yanqing, Hou Shen, Erzhu Yusheng, and others.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Putai he led his forces to Anguo City in Boling and fought Chilie Yanqing, Hou Shen, Erzhu Yusheng, and others.

sentences.zh: 戰敗被禽，斬於定州，傳首洛陽，支分其體。

translations.literal: Defeated in battle, he was captured and beheaded at Dingzhou; his head was sent to Luoyang and his body quartered.
translations.idiomatic: Defeated in battle, he was taken captive and beheaded at Dingzhou. His head was sent to Luoyang and his body cut into pieces.

sentences.zh: 初，靈助每云：「三月末，我必入定州，爾硃亦必滅。」

translations.literal: Earlier Lingzhu had always said, 'At the end of the third month I will surely enter Dingzhou, and the Erzhu will surely be destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Lingzhu had often declared, 'At the end of the third month I shall surely enter Dingzhou, and the Erzhu shall surely be destroyed.

sentences.zh: 及將戰，靈助自筮，卦不吉，以手折蓍棄之地，云：「此何知！」

translations.literal: When battle was about to begin, Lingzhu divined for himself; the hexagram was inauspicious. He broke the yarrow stalks with his hand and threw them to the ground, saying, 'What does this know!'
translations.idiomatic: When battle was about to begin, Lingzhu divined for himself and received an ill omen. He snapped the yarrow stalks in his hand and cast them to the ground, crying, 'What does this know!'

sentences.zh: 尋見禽。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he was captured.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was taken captive.

sentences.zh: 果以三月入定州。

translations.literal: Indeed he entered Dingzhou in the third month.
translations.idiomatic: He did indeed enter Dingzhou in the third month.

sentences.zh: 而齊神武以明年閏三月，滅兆等於韓陵山。

translations.literal: And Gao Huan destroyed Zhao and the others at Hanling Mountain in the intercalary third month of the following year.
translations.idiomatic: And in the intercalary third month of the following year Gao Huan destroyed Zhao and his allies at Hanling Mountain.

sentences.zh: 永熙二年，贈尚書左僕射、開府儀同三司、幽州刺史，諡曰恭。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongxi, he was posthumously granted Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat, Grand Master in the Palace with Honored Staff Equal to a Three-Duty Office, and Governor of You Province; his posthumous title was Gong.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yongxi he was posthumously granted the titles of Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat, Grand Master in the Palace with Honored Staff Equal to a Three-Duty Office, and Governor of You Province, with the posthumous name Gong.

sentences.zh: 時又有沙門靈遠者，不知何許人，有道術。

translations.literal: There was also a monk named Lingyuan, of unknown origin, who possessed the arts of the Way.
translations.idiomatic: There was also a monk named Lingyuan, of unknown origin, who possessed the arts of the Way.

sentences.zh: 嘗言爾硃榮成敗，預知其時。

translations.literal: He had spoken of Erzhu Rong's rise and fall and foreknown the time.
translations.idiomatic: He had spoken of Erzhu Rong's rise and fall and foretold the time of it.

sentences.zh: 又言代魏者齊。

translations.literal: He also said that Qi would replace Wei.
translations.idiomatic: He also declared that Qi would replace Wei.

sentences.zh: 葛榮聞之，故自號齊。

translations.literal: Ge Rong heard this and therefore styled himself Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Ge Rong heard this and therefore styled himself Qi.

sentences.zh: 及齊神武至信都，靈遠與勃海李嵩來謁。

translations.literal: When Gao Huan came to Xindu, Lingyuan and Li Song of Bohai came to pay homage.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Huan arrived at Xindu, Lingyuan and Li Song of Bohai came to pay him homage.

sentences.zh: 神武待靈遠以殊禮，問其天文人事。

translations.literal: Gao Huan treated Lingyuan with special honor and asked him about celestial affairs and human affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan received Lingyuan with exceptional honor and questioned him about the stars and the affairs of men.

sentences.zh: 對曰：「齊當興，東海出天子。

translations.literal: He replied, 'Qi shall rise; from the Eastern Sea will come a Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: He answered, 'Qi shall rise, and from the Eastern Sea a Son of Heaven shall appear.

sentences.zh: 今王據勃海，是齊地。

translations.literal: Now Your Highness holds Bohai—that is Qi territory.
translations.idiomatic: Your Highness now holds Bohai—that is the land of Qi.

sentences.zh: 又太白與月並，宜速用兵，遲則不吉。」

translations.literal: Further, Venus and the moon are in conjunction; you should employ troops swiftly—delay will be inauspicious.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Venus stands with the moon. You should take up arms at once; delay will bring ill fortune.

sentences.zh: 靈遠後罷道，姓荊字次德。

translations.literal: Later Lingyuan left the monastic order; his surname was Jing and his courtesy name Cide.
translations.idiomatic: Later Lingyuan left the monastic life. His surname was Jing and his courtesy name Cide.

sentences.zh: 求之，不知所在。

translations.literal: Men sought him but did not know where he was.
translations.idiomatic: Men searched for him, but none knew where he had gone.

sentences.zh: 李順興，京兆杜陵人也。

translations.literal: Li Shunxing was a man of Duling in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shunxing was a native of Duling in Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 年十餘，乍愚乍智，時莫識之。

translations.literal: In his teens he was sometimes foolish, sometimes wise; for a time no one understood him.
translations.idiomatic: From his teens onward he was by turns dull and bright, and for a time no one could make sense of him.

sentences.zh: 其言未來事，時有中者。

translations.literal: When he spoke of future events, sometimes he hit the mark.
translations.idiomatic: When he spoke of things yet to come, he sometimes proved right.

sentences.zh: 盛冬單布衣，跣行冰上及入洗浴，略不患寒。

translations.literal: In deep winter he wore only a single cloth garment; he walked barefoot on ice and bathed in cold water, scarcely troubled by the cold.
translations.idiomatic: In the depths of winter he wore but a single cloth robe, walked barefoot on the ice, and bathed in icy water, yet scarcely felt the cold.

sentences.zh: 家嘗為齋，方食，器用不周。

translations.literal: Once when his family held a fasting ritual and were about to eat, they lacked sufficient vessels.
translations.idiomatic: Once, when his household was holding a fast and about to eat, they had not enough dishes.

sentences.zh: 順興言：「昆明池中有大荷葉，可取盛餅食。」

translations.literal: Shunxing said, 'In the Kunming Pool there are great lotus leaves—they can be taken to hold the cakes for eating.
translations.idiomatic: Shunxing said, 'In Kunming Pool there are great lotus leaves. Go fetch them to hold the cakes.

sentences.zh: 其所居去池十數里，日不移影，順興負荷葉而歸，腳猶泥，舉坐驚異。

translations.literal: His dwelling was more than ten li from the pool; the sun had not yet shifted its shadow when Shunxing returned bearing lotus leaves, his feet still muddy—all present were astonished.
translations.idiomatic: His home lay more than ten li from the pool, yet before the sun had moved its shadow he returned bearing lotus leaves, his feet still muddy. All who were present were astonished.

sentences.zh: 後稍出城市，常冠道士冠，人有憶者，不過數日，輒至其家。

translations.literal: Later he began to go out into the cities, usually wearing a Taoist cap. If anyone remembered him, within a few days he would arrive at that person's home.
translations.idiomatic: Later he began to appear in the cities, usually wearing a Taoist cap. If anyone merely thought of him, within a few days he would show up at that person's door.

sentences.zh: 號為李練。

translations.literal: He was called Master Li.
translations.idiomatic: He was known as Master Li.

sentences.zh: 好飲酒，但不至醉。

translations.literal: He loved to drink wine, but never to the point of drunkenness.
translations.idiomatic: He loved wine, yet never drank himself into a stupor.

sentences.zh: 貴賤並敬之。

translations.literal: He treated the noble and the low alike with respect.
translations.idiomatic: High and low alike he honored with equal courtesy.

sentences.zh: 得人所施，輒散乞貧人。

translations.literal: Whatever gifts people gave him, he would at once distribute them, begging on behalf of the poor.
translations.idiomatic: Whatever anyone gave him, he immediately passed it on to the poor.

sentences.zh: 蕭寶夤反，召順興問曰：「朕王可幾年？」

translations.literal: When Xiao Baoyin rebelled, he summoned Shunxing and asked, 'How many years may I reign as king?
translations.idiomatic: When Xiao Baoyin rose in rebellion, he called Shunxing before him and asked, 'How many years may I reign as king?

sentences.zh: 對曰：「為天子自有百年者，十年者，一年者，百日者，事由可知。」

translations.literal: Shunxing replied, 'There are those who reign as Son of Heaven for a hundred years, for ten years, for one year, and for a hundred days—the matter may be known from the circumstances.'
translations.idiomatic: Shunxing answered, 'Some reign as Son of Heaven for a hundred years, some for ten, some for one, and some for a hundred days—the outcome can be read from the signs.'

sentences.zh: 及寶夤敗，裁百日也。

translations.literal: When Baoyin was defeated, it had been only a hundred days.
translations.idiomatic: When Baoyin fell, it had been scarcely a hundred days.

sentences.zh: 有侯終德者，寶夤之黨。

translations.literal: There was one Hou Zhongde, a partisan of Baoyin.
translations.idiomatic: One Hou Zhongde was among Baoyin's followers.

sentences.zh: 寶夤敗後，收集反者。

translations.literal: After Baoyin's defeat, he gathered the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: After Baoyin's defeat, Zhongde rallied the rebels.

sentences.zh: 順興稱其必敗，德乃棒殺順興，置城隍中。

translations.literal: Shunxing declared that he would surely be defeated; Zhongde thereupon clubbed Shunxing to death and cast him into the city moat.
translations.idiomatic: Shunxing prophesied that Zhongde would surely fail. In rage, Zhongde beat Shunxing to death with a club and threw his body into the moat.

sentences.zh: 頃之，起活如初。

translations.literal: Before long, Shunxing revived as if nothing had happened.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he rose alive, as though untouched.

sentences.zh: 後賀拔嶽北征，順興與魏收書，上為毛鴻賓等九人姓名者悉放貴還。

translations.literal: Later, when Heba Yue marched north, Shunxing wrote to Wei Shou; all nine men whose names headed the letter, including Mao Hongbin, were released and sent home in honor.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Heba Yue marched north, Shunxing wrote to Wei Shou. The nine men listed at the top of the letter, including Mao Hongbin, were all released and sent home with honor.

sentences.zh: 順興從後提一河東酒缸，以繩系之，於城巷牽行。

translations.literal: Shunxing followed behind, dragging a Hedong wine jar tied with a rope through the lanes of the city.
translations.idiomatic: Shunxing came behind them, hauling a great Hedong wine jar on a rope through the city streets.

sentences.zh: 俄而蒲阪降。

translations.literal: Before long, Puban surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, Puban fell.

sentences.zh: 又無何，至太傅梁覽家庭中臥，以布衫倒覆身上。

translations.literal: Not long after, he came to the household of Grand Tutor Liang Lan and lay down, with a cloth shirt thrown upside down over his body.
translations.idiomatic: Not long afterward he appeared in Grand Tutor Liang Lan's household and lay down with a cloth shirt draped upside down over him.

sentences.zh: 後覽于趙崔反，通使東魏，事泄被誅，覽以衣倒覆，果如順興之形。

translations.literal: Later Lan joined Zhao Cui in rebellion and sent envoys to Eastern Wei; when the plot was exposed he was executed. Lan's body was covered with his garment upside down, exactly as Shunxing's form had been.
translations.idiomatic: Later Lan took part in Zhao Cui's rebellion and sent envoys to Eastern Wei. When the plot was exposed he was put to death, his corpse covered by his robe exactly as Shunxing had lain.

sentences.zh: 周文嘗至溫泉，順興求乞溫泉東間驪山下二畝地，周文曰：「李練用此何為？」

translations.literal: Duke Wen of Zhou once came to the hot springs; Shunxing begged for two mu of land east of the springs below Mount Li. Duke Wen said, 'What would Li Lian use this for?
translations.idiomatic: Duke Wen of Zhou once visited the hot springs. Shunxing asked for two mu of land east of the springs below Mount Li. The Duke said, 'What does Li Lian want with that land?

sentences.zh: 對曰：「有用。」

translations.literal: Shunxing replied, 'It will be useful.'
translations.idiomatic: Shunxing answered, 'It will serve a purpose.'

sentences.zh: 未幾，至溫湯遇患，卒於其地。

translations.literal: Before long he fell ill at the hot springs and died on that very spot.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he took ill at the hot springs and died there.

sentences.zh: 初，大統十三年，順興謂周文曰：「可于沙苑北作一老君象，面向北，作笑狀。」

translations.literal: Earlier, in the thirteenth year of Great Unity, Shunxing told Duke Wen of Zhou, 'You may erect an image of Lord Lao north of Shayuan, facing north, in a laughing posture.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, in the thirteenth year of Great Unity, Shunxing said to Duke Wen of Zhou, 'Erect a statue of Lord Lao north of Shayuan, facing north, with a laughing expression.

sentences.zh: 周文曰：「何為？」

translations.literal: Duke Wen said, 'For what purpose?'
translations.idiomatic: The Duke asked, 'Why?'

sentences.zh: 答曰：「令笑破蠕蠕。」

translations.literal: Shunxing answered, 'Let it laugh the Rouran to ruin.'
translations.idiomatic: Shunxing replied, 'Let laughter break the Rouran.'

sentences.zh: 時甚惑，未解其意。

translations.literal: At the time all were greatly puzzled and did not understand his meaning.
translations.idiomatic: At the time everyone was baffled and could not grasp his meaning.

sentences.zh: 及蠕蠕國滅，周文憶語，遂作順興象於老君側。

translations.literal: When the Rouran state was destroyed, Duke Wen recalled his words and had a statue of Shunxing made beside Lord Lao.
translations.idiomatic: When the Rouran kingdom fell, Duke Wen remembered his words and had a statue of Shunxing placed beside Lord Lao.

sentences.zh: 檀特師者，名惠豐，身為比丘，不知何處人。

translations.literal: Tante Shi, whose given name was Huifeng, was a Buddhist monk; no one knew whence he came.
translations.idiomatic: Tante Shi, named Huifeng, lived as a Buddhist monk. No one knew his origin.

sentences.zh: 飲酒啖肉，語默無常，逆論來事，後皆如言。

translations.literal: He drank wine and ate meat; his speech and silence were unpredictable, and when he spoke contrary to expectation of future events, afterward all came to pass as he had said.
translations.idiomatic: He drank wine and ate meat. His words and silences were erratic, yet when he spoke against expectation of things to come, events always unfolded as he had foretold.

sentences.zh: 居於涼州，宇文仲和為刺史，請之至州內，曆觀廄庫。

translations.literal: He lived in Liangzhou; Yuwen Zhonghe was prefect and invited him into the prefectural seat, where they toured the stables and storehouses together.
translations.idiomatic: He lived in Liangzhou. Yuwen Zhonghe, then prefect, invited him to the city and led him through the stables and storehouses.

sentences.zh: 乃云：「何意畜他官馬官物！」

translations.literal: Tante Shi then said, 'Why do you keep other men's official horses and official goods!
translations.idiomatic: Tante Shi cried out, 'Why are you hoarding other men's official horses and government property!

sentences.zh: 仲和怒，不聽住涼州。

translations.literal: Zhonghe grew angry and would not allow him to remain in Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhonghe flew into a rage and forbade him to stay in Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 未幾，仲和拒不受代，朝廷令獨孤信禽之，仲和身死，資財沒官。

translations.literal: Before long Zhonghe refused to accept replacement and the court ordered Dugu Xin to seize him. Zhonghe died, and his property was confiscated by the state.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Zhonghe refused to yield his post, and the court sent Dugu Xin to arrest him. Zhonghe was killed, and his wealth was seized by the state.

sentences.zh: 周文遣書召之，檀特發至岐州，會齊神武來寇玉壁，檀特曰：「狗豈能至龍門也？」

translations.literal: Duke Wen of Zhou sent a letter summoning him. Tante Shi set out and reached Qizhou just as Gao Huan of Northern Qi came to attack Yubi. Tante Shi said, 'Can a dog reach Longmen?
translations.idiomatic: Duke Wen of Zhou summoned him by letter. Tante Shi traveled as far as Qizhou just as Gao Huan of Northern Qi marched against Yubi. Tante Shi said, 'Can a dog reach Longmen?

sentences.zh: 神武果不至龍門而還。

translations.literal: Gao Huan indeed did not reach Longmen and turned back.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan never reached Longmen and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 侯景未叛東魏之前，忽捉一杖，杖頭刻為獼猴。

translations.literal: Before Hou Jing rebelled against Eastern Wei, he suddenly seized a staff and carved its head in the shape of a monkey.
translations.idiomatic: Before Hou Jing turned against Eastern Wei, he suddenly took up a staff and carved its head into the shape of a monkey.

sentences.zh: 令其面常向西，日夜弄之。

translations.literal: He made it face constantly westward and played with it day and night.
translations.idiomatic: He kept its face turned west and fiddled with it day and night.

sentences.zh: 又索一角弓，牽挽之。

translations.literal: He also asked for a horn bow and drew it back repeatedly.
translations.idiomatic: He also demanded a horn bow and pulled it back again and again.

sentences.zh: 俄而景啟降，尋復背叛，人皆以為驗。

translations.literal: Before long Jing offered surrender, then soon rebelled again; all regarded these acts as omens fulfilled.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Jing offered surrender, then rebelled again. All took these antics as fulfilled portents.

sentences.zh: 至大統十七年春初，忽著一布帽，周文左右驚問之。

translations.literal: In the early spring of the seventeenth year of Great Unity he suddenly put on a cloth cap; Duke Wen's attendants were startled and asked him about it.
translations.idiomatic: In early spring of the seventeenth year of Great Unity he suddenly donned a cloth cap. Duke Wen's attendants were alarmed and questioned him.

sentences.zh: 檀特曰：「汝亦著，王亦著也。」

translations.literal: Tante Shi said, 'You will wear one too, and the King will wear one too.
translations.idiomatic: Tante Shi said, 'You will wear one as well, and the King will wear one as well.

sentences.zh: 至三月而魏文帝崩。

translations.literal: By the third month Emperor Wen of Wei had died.
translations.idiomatic: By the third month Emperor Wen of Wei was dead.

sentences.zh: 復取一白絹帽著之，左右復問之。

translations.literal: He then put on a white silk cap; the attendants again questioned him.
translations.idiomatic: He next put on a white silk cap, and the attendants questioned him again.

sentences.zh: 檀特云：「汝亦著，王亦著也。」

translations.literal: Tante Shi said, 'You will wear one too, and the King will wear one too.
translations.idiomatic: Tante Shi said, 'You will wear one as well, and the King will wear one as well.

sentences.zh: 未幾，丞相夫人薨。

translations.literal: Before long the Chancellor's wife died.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the Chancellor's wife passed away.

sentences.zh: 後又著白絹帽，左右復問之。

translations.literal: Later he again put on a white silk cap, and the attendants again questioned him.
translations.idiomatic: Later he donned a white silk cap once more, and the attendants questioned him again.

sentences.zh: 云：「汝不著，王亦著也。」

translations.literal: He said, 'You will not wear one, but the King will wear one.
translations.idiomatic: He said, 'You will not wear one, but the King will wear one.

sentences.zh: 尋而丞相第二兒武邑公薨。

translations.literal: Before long the Chancellor's second son, Duke of Wuyi, died.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the Chancellor's second son, the Duke of Wuyi, died.

sentences.zh: 其事驗多如此也。

translations.literal: His fulfilled prophecies were mostly of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: Most of his fulfilled omens followed this pattern.

sentences.zh: 俄而疾死。

translations.literal: Before long he died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he fell ill and died.

sentences.zh: 由吾道榮，琅琊沐陽人也。

translations.literal: Youwu Daorong was a man of Muyang in Langye.
translations.idiomatic: Youwu Daorong was a native of Muyang in Langye.

sentences.zh: 少為道士，入長白山、太山，又游燕、趙間。

translations.literal: In youth he became a Daoist priest, entered Mount Changbai and Mount Tai, and also traveled through Yan and Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he took orders as a Daoist, entered Mount Changbai and Mount Tai, and wandered through Yan and Zhao.

sentences.zh: 聞晉陽有人大明法術，乃尋之。

translations.literal: He heard that in Jinyang there was a man who greatly understood magical arts, and went to seek him.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing that a man in Jinyang was deeply versed in the occult arts, he went in search of him.

sentences.zh: 是人為人家傭力，無名者，久求訪始得。

translations.literal: That man worked as a hired laborer in someone's household and had no name; only after long searching did Daorong find him.
translations.idiomatic: The man was a hired hand in a private household and bore no name. Daorong searched a long while before he found him.

sentences.zh: 其人道家，符水禁呪、陰陽曆數、天文藥性，無不通解。

translations.literal: He was of the Daoist school and thoroughly understood talismanic water, forbidden incantations, yin-yang calendrics, astronomy, and the properties of drugs.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the Daoist way and was master of talismanic water, forbidden spells, yin-yang reckoning, astronomy, and pharmacology alike.

sentences.zh: 以道榮好尚，乃悉授之。

translations.literal: Because Daorong admired these things, the man taught him everything.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing Daorong's devotion, the man taught him all he knew.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，是人謂榮云：「我本恆岳仙人，有少罪過，為天官所謫。

translations.literal: After more than a year the man said to Daorong, 'I am originally an immortal of Mount Heng. I committed a small offense and was banished by the celestial officers.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a year the man told Daorong, 'I am in truth an immortal of Mount Heng. I committed a minor fault and was banished by the officers of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 今限滿將歸，卿宜送吾至汾水。」

translations.literal: Now my term is fulfilled and I am about to return. You should escort me to the Fen River.
translations.idiomatic: My term of exile is now complete and I am returning. Escort me to the Fen River.

sentences.zh: 及至汾河，遇水暴長，橋壞，船渡艱難。

translations.literal: When they reached the Fen River, they found the water suddenly swollen; the bridge was broken and crossing by boat was difficult.
translations.idiomatic: When they reached the Fen, the river was in sudden flood. The bridge had collapsed, and ferrying across was perilous.

sentences.zh: 是人乃臨水禹步，以一符投水中，流便絕。

translations.literal: The man then performed Yu's Pace beside the water and cast a talisman into the stream; the current at once ceased.
translations.idiomatic: The man performed Yu's Pace at the water's edge and cast a talisman into the river. The current stopped at once.

sentences.zh: 俄頃，水積將至天。

translations.literal: In a moment the water piled up until it nearly reached the sky.
translations.idiomatic: In moments the water rose in a wall nearly to the heavens.

sentences.zh: 是人徐自沙石上渡。

translations.literal: The man then crossed slowly over the sand and stones.
translations.idiomatic: The man then walked calmly across on the exposed sand and stone.

sentences.zh: 唯道榮見其如是，傍人咸云：「水如此長，此人遂能浮過。」

translations.literal: Only Daorong saw him do this; those standing nearby all said, 'The water is so high—how can this man float across?
translations.idiomatic: Only Daorong saw what truly happened. Those standing nearby cried, 'The water stands so high—how can this man cross it?

sentences.zh: 共驚異之。

translations.literal: All were startled and astonished together.
translations.idiomatic: All marveled together in astonishment.

sentences.zh: 如此法，道榮所不得也。

translations.literal: Arts such as this Daorong could not attain.
translations.idiomatic: Such arts were beyond Daorong's reach.

sentences.zh: 道榮仍歸本郡，隱於琅邪山中，辟穀餌松茯苓，求長生之秘。

translations.literal: Daorong returned to his home commandery and hid himself in the Langye mountains, fasting from grain and taking pine fungus and poria, seeking the secret of long life.
translations.idiomatic: Daorong returned to his home commandery and withdrew to the Langye mountains. He abstained from grain, nourished himself on pine fungus and poria, and sought the secret of immortality.

sentences.zh: 又善洞視，蕭軌等之敗於江南，其日，道榮言之如目見。

translations.literal: He was also skilled at distant sight; on the day Xiao Gui and the others were defeated in the south, Daorong described it as though he had seen it with his own eyes.
