translations.idiomatic: He could also see at a distance. On the day Xiao Gui and his forces were routed in the south, Daorong described the battle as though he had watched it with his own eyes.

sentences.zh: 其後鄉人從役得歸者，勘問敗時形勢，與道榮所說符同。

translations.literal: Later, when men of his district returned from military service, they questioned them about the circumstances of the defeat and found that Daorong's account matched exactly.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when neighbors came home from the campaign, they questioned them about the defeat and found Daorong's account matched in every detail.

sentences.zh: 尋為文宣追往晉陽，道榮恆野宿，不入逆旅。

translations.literal: Before long Emperor Wenxuan summoned him to Jinyang; Daorong always slept in the open and never entered an inn.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Emperor Wenxuan summoned him to Jinyang. Daorong always camped outdoors and never lodged at an inn.

sentences.zh: 至遼陽山中，夜初馬驚，有猛獸去馬止十餘步，所追人及防援者並驚怖將走。

translations.literal: In the mountains of Liaoyang, at the first watch of the night the horses panicked; a fierce beast stood little more than ten paces from the horses. Those in pursuit and the guards alike were terrified and about to flee.
translations.idiomatic: In the Liaoyang mountains, at the first watch of night the horses bolted in terror. A savage beast stood scarcely ten paces from them. Pursuers and guards alike were stricken with fear and ready to run.

sentences.zh: 道榮徐以杖畫地成火坑，猛獸遽走。

translations.literal: Daorong calmly traced a fire pit on the ground with his staff, and the beast fled at once.
translations.idiomatic: Daorong calmly drew a ring of fire on the ground with his staff, and the beast fled instantly.

sentences.zh: 道榮至晉陽，文宣見之甚悅。

translations.literal: When Daorong reached Jinyang, Wenxuan was greatly pleased to see him.
translations.idiomatic: When Daorong arrived in Jinyang, Wenxuan received him with great delight.

sentences.zh: 後歸鄉里。

translations.literal: Later he returned to his home district.
translations.idiomatic: Later he went home to his native place.

sentences.zh: 隋開皇初，備禮徵辟，授上儀同三司、諫議大夫、沐陽縣公。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Kaihuang era of Sui he was summoned with full ceremony and appointed Senior Master of Ceremonies of the Third Rank, Remonstrating Grandee, and Duke of Muyang County.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Sui's Kaihuang era he was summoned with full honors and made Senior Master of Ceremonies of the Third Rank, Remonstrating Grandee, and Duke of Muyang County.

sentences.zh: 從晉王平陳還，苦辭歸。

translations.literal: After returning from campaigning with the Prince of Jin to pacify Chen, he earnestly begged to go home.
translations.idiomatic: After returning from the Prince of Jin's campaign against Chen, he pleaded hard to be released to his home.

sentences.zh: 至鄉卒，年八十五。

translations.literal: He reached his district and died there at the age of eighty-five.
translations.idiomatic: He reached his home and died there at eighty-five.

sentences.zh: 又有張遠遊者，文宣時，令與諸術士合九轉金丹。

translations.literal: There was also Zhang Yuanyou; in Wenxuan's time the Emperor ordered him to join other masters in compounding the nine-turn golden elixir.
translations.idiomatic: There was also Zhang Yuanyou. In Wenxuan's reign the Emperor ordered him to join other adepts in refining the nine-turn golden elixir.

sentences.zh: 及成，帝置之玉匣云：「我貪人間作樂，不能飛上天，待臨死時取服。」

translations.literal: When it was finished, the Emperor placed it in a jade casket and said, 'I am too greedy for the pleasures of the human world to fly up to Heaven. I shall take it only when death is near.'
translations.idiomatic: When the elixir was complete, the Emperor sealed it in a jade casket and said, 'I am too fond of earthly pleasures to ascend to Heaven now. I shall swallow it only when death draws near.'

sentences.zh: 顏惡頭，章武郡人也。

translations.literal: Yan Etou was a man of Zhangwu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Etou was a native of Zhangwu commandery.

sentences.zh: 妙于《易》筮。

translations.literal: He was skilled in divination by the Book of Changes.
translations.idiomatic: He was a master of the yarrow stalks of the Book of Changes.

sentences.zh: 游州市觀卜，有婦人負囊粟來卜，曆七人，皆不中而強索其粟，惡頭尤之。

translations.literal: While divining in the market he saw a woman carrying a sack of millet come to have her fortune told. She had visited seven diviners in succession; none had hit the mark yet all forcibly demanded her millet. Etou rebuked them.
translations.idiomatic: While practicing divination in the market he saw a woman with a sack of millet seeking a reading. She had already consulted seven diviners. None had guessed correctly, yet each had demanded her grain anyway. Etou reproached them.

sentences.zh: 卜者曰：「君若能中，何不為卜？」

translations.literal: One diviner said, 'If you can hit the mark, why don't you divine for her?
translations.idiomatic: One diviner said, 'If you can read truly, why not cast for her yourself?

sentences.zh: 惡頭因筮之，曰：「登高臨下水泂泂，唯聞人聲不見形。」

translations.literal: Etou thereupon cast the stalks and said, 'Climbing high and looking down on water running clear and deep—only a human voice is heard, but no form is seen.'
translations.idiomatic: Etou cast the stalks and said, 'You climb high and look down on water running deep and clear—you hear a human voice but see no form.'

sentences.zh: 婦人曰：「妊身已七月矣，向井上汲水，忽聞胎聲，故卜。」

translations.literal: The woman said, 'I have been pregnant seven months. While drawing water at a well I suddenly heard a fetal voice, and so I came to divine.'
translations.idiomatic: The woman said, 'I am seven months with child. While drawing water at a well I suddenly heard the fetus cry out, and so I came to ask the oracle.'

sentences.zh: 惡頭曰：「吉，十月三十日有一男子。」

translations.literal: Etou said, 'It is auspicious. On the thirtieth day of the tenth month there will be a male child.'
translations.idiomatic: Etou said, 'It is auspicious. On the thirtieth day of the tenth month you will bear a son.'

sentences.zh: 詣卜者乃驚服曰：「是顏生邪？」

translations.literal: The diviners were startled and submitted, saying, 'Are you Master Yan?'
translations.idiomatic: The diviners were astonished and humbled themselves. 'Are you Master Yan?' they asked.

sentences.zh: 相與具羊酒謝焉。

translations.literal: Together they prepared sheep and wine to apologize.
translations.idiomatic: Together they brought sheep and wine to make amends.

sentences.zh: 有人以三月十三日詣惡頭求卜，遇《兌》之《履》。

translations.literal: On the thirteenth day of the third month someone came to Etou seeking divination and obtained the hexagram Dui changing to Lu.
translations.idiomatic: On the thirteenth day of the third month a man came to Etou for a reading and drew the hexagram Dui changing to Lu.

sentences.zh: 惡頭占曰：「君卜父，父已亡，當上天，聞哭聲，忽復蘇，而有言。」

translations.literal: Etou interpreted it, saying, 'You are divining about your father. Your father is already dead and about to ascend to Heaven. You will hear weeping, then he will suddenly revive and speak.
translations.idiomatic: Etou read the signs and said, 'You ask about your father. He is already dead and about to ascend to Heaven. You will hear weeping, then he will suddenly wake and speak.

sentences.zh: 其人曰：「父臥疾三年矣，昨日雞鳴時氣盡，舉家大哭。

translations.literal: The man said, 'My father has lain ill three years. At cockcrow yesterday his breath failed, and the whole household wept.
translations.idiomatic: The man said, 'My father has been bedridden three years. At cockcrow yesterday his breath stopped, and the whole household wailed.

sentences.zh: 父忽驚寤云：'我死，有三尺人來迎，欲升天，聞哭聲，遂墜地。

translations.literal: His father suddenly awoke in alarm and said, 'I died. A man three feet tall came to welcome me and I was about to ascend to Heaven, but when I heard the weeping I fell back to earth.'
translations.idiomatic: His father suddenly woke in alarm and said, 'I died. A man three feet tall came to welcome me and I was about to ascend, but when I heard the weeping I fell back to earth.'

sentences.zh: '」惡頭曰：「更三日，當永去。」

translations.literal: Etou said, 'In three more days he will depart forever.'
translations.idiomatic: Etou said, 'In three days he will be gone for good.'

sentences.zh: 果如言。

translations.literal: It happened exactly as he had said.
translations.idiomatic: It came to pass exactly as he had said.

sentences.zh: 人問其故，惡頭曰：「《兌》上天下土，是今日庚辛本宮火，故知卜父。

translations.literal: When people asked the reason, Etou said, 'Dui is heaven above and earth below. Today is geng-xin; the native palace is fire—therefore I knew he was divining about his father.
translations.idiomatic: When people asked how he knew, Etou said, 'Dui is heaven above and earth below. Today is geng-xin, and the native palace is fire—so I knew he asked about his father.

sentences.zh: 今三月，土入墓，又見宗廟爻發，故知死。

translations.literal: Now it is the third month; earth enters the tomb, and the ancestral-temple line also stirs—therefore I knew he was dead.
translations.idiomatic: It is the third month, when earth enters the tomb, and the ancestral-temple line is active—so I knew he was dead.

sentences.zh: 變見生氣，故知蘇。

translations.literal: In the change I saw the breath of life—therefore I knew he would revive.
translations.idiomatic: In the change I saw the breath of life—so I knew he would wake again.

sentences.zh: 《兌》為口，主音聲，故知哭。

translations.literal: Dui is the mouth and governs sound—therefore I knew there would be weeping.
translations.idiomatic: Dui is the mouth and governs voice—so I knew there would be weeping.

sentences.zh: 《兌》變為《乾》，《乾》天也，故升天。

translations.literal: Dui changes to Qian; Qian is Heaven—therefore ascent to Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Dui changes to Qian, and Qian is Heaven—hence ascent to Heaven.

sentences.zh: 《兌》為言，故父言。

translations.literal: Dui is speech—therefore the father spoke.
translations.idiomatic: Dui is speech—hence the father's words.

sentences.zh: 故知有言。

translations.literal: Therefore I knew there would be speech.
translations.idiomatic: That is how I knew he would speak.

sentences.zh: 未化入戍為土，三月土墓，戍又是本宮鬼墓，未後三日至戍，故知三日復死。」

translations.literal: The unchanging line enters xu as earth. In the third month earth is in the tomb, and xu is also the ghost-tomb of the native palace. Three days after wei comes xu—therefore I knew he would die again in three days.
translations.idiomatic: The unchanging line enters xu as earth. In the third month earth lies in the tomb, and xu is the ghost-tomb of the native palace as well. Three days after wei comes xu—so I knew he would die again in three days.

sentences.zh: 惡頭又語人曰：「長樂王某年某月某日當為天子。」

translations.literal: Etou also told people, 'A certain Wang of Changle on such-and-such a year, month, and day will become Son of Heaven.'
translations.idiomatic: Etou also told people, 'A certain Wang of Changle will become Son of Heaven on such-and-such a year, month, and day.'

sentences.zh: 有人姓張，聞其言，數以寶物獻之，豫乞東益州刺史。

translations.literal: A man surnamed Zhang heard his words and repeatedly presented him with treasures, begging in advance to be made Governor of Eastern Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: A man named Zhang heard this and repeatedly sent him gifts of treasure, asking in advance to be made Governor of Eastern Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 及期，果為天子，擢張用之。

translations.literal: When the day came, Wang indeed became Son of Heaven and promoted Zhang to office.
translations.idiomatic: When the day arrived, Wang did become Son of Heaven and raised Zhang to office as he had promised.

sentences.zh: 惡頭自言厄在彭城。

translations.literal: Etou himself said that his misfortune lay in Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Etou himself declared that calamity awaited him at Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 後游東都，逢彭城王爾硃仲遠將伐齊神武於鄴，召惡頭令筮。

translations.literal: Later, traveling in the Eastern Capital, he met the Prince of Pengcheng, Erzhu Zhongyuan, who was about to march against Gao Huan at Ye and summoned Etou to perform divination.
translations.idiomatic: Later, while traveling in the Eastern Capital, he encountered Erzhu Zhongyuan, Prince of Pengcheng, who was preparing to attack Gao Huan at Ye. Zhongyuan summoned Etou to read the signs.

sentences.zh: 惡頭野生，不知避忌，高聲言：「大惡。」

translations.literal: Etou was rough by nature and knew nothing of taboo. He cried out in a loud voice, 'Great ill fortune.'
translations.idiomatic: Etou was uncouth by nature and heedless of omens. He shouted aloud, 'Great ill fortune.'

sentences.zh: 仲遠怒其沮眾，斬之。

translations.literal: Zhongyuan, angered that he had dampened the army's spirit, had him executed.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged that Etou had shaken the troops' resolve, Zhongyuan had him beheaded.

sentences.zh: 王春，河東安邑人也。

translations.literal: Wang Chun was a man of Anyi in Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chun was a native of Anyi in Hedong.

sentences.zh: 少精《易》占，明陰陽風角，齊神武引為館客。

translations.literal: In youth he mastered divination by the Changes, understood yin-yang and wind divination, and Gao Huan took him on as a house guest.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he was skilled in divination by the Changes and versed in yin-yang lore and wind divination. Gao Huan retained him as a house guest.

sentences.zh: 韓陵之戰，四面受敵，從寅至午，三合三離，將士皆懼。

translations.literal: At the battle of Hanling the army was besieged on every side. From the hour of yin to the hour of wu the lines broke and re-formed three times, and officers and soldiers alike were afraid.
translations.idiomatic: At Hanling the army was attacked from every side. From dawn until midday the ranks broke and re-formed three times, and officers and soldiers alike were seized with fear.

sentences.zh: 神武將退軍，春叩馬諫曰：「比至未時，必當大捷。」

translations.literal: Gao Huan was about to withdraw. Chun seized his horse's bridle and remonstrated, saying, 'By the hour of wei there will surely be a great victory.'
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan was on the point of retreating when Chun caught his horse by the bridle and urged him, 'Before the hour of wei there will surely be a great victory.'

sentences.zh: 遽縛其子詣軍門為質，若不勝請斬之。

translations.literal: He at once bound his son and sent him to the camp gate as a hostage, asking that if they did not win he might be executed.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately bound his son and sent him to the camp gate as a hostage, offering his own life if the battle should be lost.

sentences.zh: 賊果大敗。

translations.literal: The enemy was indeed routed.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy was indeed put to rout.

sentences.zh: 後從征討，恆令占卜，其言多中。

translations.literal: Thereafter, on every campaign he was ordered to perform divination, and his words mostly proved true.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward, on every campaign he was asked to read the signs, and his predictions usually hit the mark.

sentences.zh: 位東徐州刺史，賜爵安夷縣公。

translations.literal: He rose to Governor of Eastern Xuzhou and was enfeoffed as Duke of Anyi County.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Governor of Eastern Xuzhou and was enfeoffed as Duke of Anyi County.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈秦州刺史。

translations.literal: At his death he was posthumously made Governor of Qinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After his death he was posthumously appointed Governor of Qinzhou.

sentences.zh: 信都芳，字玉琳，河間人也。

translations.literal: Xindu Fang, courtesy name Yulin, was a man of Hejian.
translations.idiomatic: Xindu Fang, styled Yulin, was a native of Hejian.

sentences.zh: 少明算術，兼有巧思，每精心研究，或墜坑坎。

translations.literal: In youth he was skilled in calculation and also possessed ingenious wit. Whenever he gave himself over to deep study he might even fall into pits and ditches.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he excelled in calculation and possessed a keen inventive mind. When he lost himself in study he might even tumble into pits and ditches.

sentences.zh: 常語人云：「算曆玄妙，機巧精微，我每一沈思，不聞雷霆之聲也。」

translations.literal: He often told people, 'Calendars and reckonings are profound and subtle, their devices refined to the finest point. Whenever I sink into thought I do not even hear the sound of thunder.'
translations.idiomatic: He often said, 'Calendars and reckonings are profound and subtle, their devices refined beyond measure. When I lose myself in thought I do not even hear thunder.'

sentences.zh: 其用心如此。

translations.literal: Such was the intensity of his mind.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the depth of his concentration.

sentences.zh: 後為安豐王延明召入賓館。

translations.literal: Later he was summoned by Prince Yanming of Anfeng to enter his guest house.
translations.idiomatic: Later Prince Yanming of Anfeng summoned him to serve in his guest house.

sentences.zh: 有江南人祖暼恆者，先於邊境被獲，在延明家，舊明算曆，而不為王所待。

translations.literal: There was a man of the south, Zu Minheng, who had earlier been captured on the frontier and was kept in Yanming's household. He was versed in calendars and reckonings but was not treated with honor by the prince.
translations.idiomatic: A southerner named Zu Minheng had earlier been taken captive on the frontier and was kept in Yanming's household. Though skilled in calendars and reckonings, he received no honor from the prince.

sentences.zh: 芳諫王禮遇之。

translations.literal: Fang remonstrated with the prince to treat him with courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Fang urged the prince to treat Minheng with proper courtesy.

sentences.zh: 暼恆後還，留諸法授芳，由是彌復精密。

translations.literal: When Minheng later returned south he left all his methods with Fang, and from that time Fang's work grew still more precise.
translations.idiomatic: When Minheng later returned south he entrusted all his methods to Fang, and from that time Fang's calculations grew still more exact.

sentences.zh: 延明家有群書，欲抄集《五經》算事為《五經宗》，及古今樂事為《樂書》，又聚渾天、欹器、地動、銅烏、漏刻、候風諸巧事，並圖畫為《器准》，並令芳算之。

translations.literal: Yanming's household possessed many books. He wished to compile calendrical matters from the Five Classics into a work called Five Classics Essentials, and to gather ancient and modern matters of music into a Book of Music. He also collected ingenious devices—the armillary sphere, the tipping vessel, the seismoscope, the bronze crow, clepsydras, and wind-indicators—and had them all illustrated in Standards of Instruments, ordering Fang to calculate for them.
translations.idiomatic: Yanming's household held a great library. He planned to compile calendrical material from the Five Classics into Five Classics Essentials, and to gather ancient and modern music into a Book of Music. He also collected ingenious devices—the armillary sphere, the tipping vessel, the seismoscope, the bronze crow, clepsydras, and wind-indicators—illustrated them in Standards of Instruments, and set Fang to working out their calculations.

sentences.zh: 會延明南奔，芳乃自撰注。

translations.literal: When Yanming fled south, Fang composed his own commentary.
translations.idiomatic: When Yanming fled south, Fang wrote his own commentary instead.

sentences.zh: 後隱于并州樂平之東山，太守慕容保樂聞而召之，芳不得已而見焉。

translations.literal: Later he withdrew to Mount Dongshan in Leping, Bingzhou. The prefect Murong Baole heard of him and summoned him; Fang, unable to refuse, went to see him.
translations.idiomatic: Later he retired to Mount Dongshan in Leping, Bingzhou. Prefect Murong Baole heard of him and summoned him, and Fang, unable to refuse, presented himself.

sentences.zh: 於是保樂弟紹宗薦之于齊神武，為館客，授中外府田曹參軍。

translations.literal: Thereupon Baole's younger brother Shaozong recommended him to Gao Huan. He became a house guest and was appointed Clerk of the Fields in the Central and External Offices.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Baole's younger brother Shaozong recommended him to Gao Huan. He became a house guest and was appointed Clerk of the Fields in the Central and External Offices.

sentences.zh: 芳性清儉質樸，不與物和。

translations.literal: Fang's nature was pure, frugal, and plain; he did not mingle easily with others.
translations.idiomatic: Fang was pure, frugal, and plain by nature, and kept apart from the world.

sentences.zh: 紹宗給其羸馬，不肯乘騎；

translations.literal: Shaozong gave him a lean horse, but he would not ride it;
translations.idiomatic: Shaozong gave him a scrawny horse, but he refused to ride it;

sentences.zh: 夜遣婢侍以試之，芳忿呼毆擊，不聽近己。

translations.literal: at night he sent a maid to attend him as a test, but Fang angrily shouted and struck her, refusing to let her come near.
translations.idiomatic: at night Shaozong sent a maid to attend him as a test, but Fang shouted in anger and beat her away, refusing to let her come near.

sentences.zh: 狷介自守，無求於物。

translations.literal: Fastidious and self-contained, he sought nothing from others.
translations.idiomatic: Fastidious and self-contained, he asked nothing of the world.

sentences.zh: 後亦注重差、勾股，復撰《史宗》。

translations.literal: Later he also turned to differential calculus and right triangles, and again composed Historical Essentials.
translations.idiomatic: Later he also took up differential reckoning and right-triangle mathematics, and composed Historical Essentials as well.

sentences.zh: 芳精專不已，又多所窺涉。

translations.literal: Fang pursued his specialty without cease and ranged widely in many fields.
translations.idiomatic: Fang pursued his specialty without rest and ranged widely through many fields.

sentences.zh: 丞相倉曹祖珽謂芳曰：「律管吹灰，術甚微妙，絕來既久，吾思所不至，卿試思之。」

translations.literal: Zu Ting, Clerk of the Granary under the Chancellor, said to Fang, 'When the pitch-pipe blows ash, the method is exceedingly subtle. The art has long been lost, and what I can think of falls short. Will you try to think it through?'
translations.idiomatic: Zu Ting, Clerk of the Granary under the Chancellor, said to Fang, 'The pitch-pipe method of blowing ash is exceedingly subtle. The art has long been lost, and my own thinking cannot reach it. Will you try?'

sentences.zh: 芳留意十數日，便報珽云：「吾得之矣，然終須河內葭莩灰。」

translations.literal: After ten-odd days of attention Fang reported to Ting, 'I have got it—but in the end it will require reed-pith ash from Henei.'
translations.idiomatic: After a dozen days of study Fang reported to Ting, 'I have found it—but it will require reed-pith ash from Henei.'

sentences.zh: 祖對試之，無驗。

translations.literal: Zu tested it with him, but there was no result.
translations.idiomatic: Zu tested the method with him, but it failed.

sentences.zh: 後得河內灰，用術，應節便飛，餘灰即不動也。

translations.literal: Later, when Henei ash was obtained and the method applied, the ash at the proper node would fly up, while the rest remained still.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when ash from Henei was obtained and the method applied, the ash at the proper seasonal node would fly up while the rest remained still.

sentences.zh: 為時所重，竟不行用，故此法遂絕。

translations.literal: He was highly regarded in his time, but the method was never put into use, and so the art died out.
translations.idiomatic: He was greatly esteemed in his day, yet the method was never adopted, and so the art died out.

sentences.zh: 又著《樂書》、《遁甲經》、《四術周髀宗》。

translations.literal: He also wrote a Book of Music, a Classic of Hidden Armor, and Four Methods and the Zhou Bi Essentials.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote a Book of Music, a Classic of Hidden Armor, and Four Methods and the Zhou Bi Essentials.

sentences.zh: 其序曰：「漢成帝時，學者問蓋天，楊雄曰：'蓋哉，未幾也。

translations.literal: Its preface says, 'In the time of Emperor Cheng of Han, scholars asked about the Canopy Heaven. Yang Xiong said, "Canopy indeed—yet not for long.
translations.idiomatic: Its preface reads, 'In the reign of Emperor Cheng of Han, scholars asked about the Canopy Heaven theory. Yang Xiong said, "Canopy indeed—yet not for long.

sentences.zh: 問渾天，曰：'落下閎為之，鮮于妄人度之，耿中丞象之，幾乎，莫之息矣。'

translations.literal: They asked about the Spherical Heaven, and he said, "Luoxia Hong made it, Xianyu Wangren measured it, and Vice Director Geng modeled it—almost, yet never at rest."
translations.idiomatic: They asked about the Spherical Heaven, and he said, "Luoxia Hong devised it, Xianyu Wangren measured it, and Vice Director Geng modeled it—almost perfect, yet never at rest."

sentences.zh: 此言蓋差而渾密也。

translations.literal: This says that the Canopy is coarse while the Sphere is precise.
translations.idiomatic: By this he meant that the Canopy is coarse while the Sphere is precise.

sentences.zh: 蓋器測影而造，用之日久，不同于祖，故云'未幾也'。

translations.literal: The canopy instrument was made by measuring shadows; used over long years it no longer agreed with the ancients—hence "not for long."
translations.idiomatic: The canopy instrument was made by measuring shadows; used over many years it no longer matched the ancients—hence "not for long."

sentences.zh: 渾器量天而作，乾坤大象，隱見難變，故云'幾乎 '。

translations.literal: The sphere instrument was made by measuring Heaven itself. The great image of yin and yang is hard to alter in its hidden and visible aspects—hence "almost."
translations.idiomatic: The sphere instrument was fashioned by measuring Heaven itself. The great image of yin and yang is hard to alter in what it hides and reveals—hence "almost."

sentences.zh: 是時，太史令尹咸窮研晷蓋，易古周法，雄乃見之，以為難也。

translations.literal: At that time Grand Astrologer Yin Xian exhaustively studied the gnomon and canopy and changed the ancient Zhou methods. Xiong saw this and judged it difficult.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Grand Astrologer Yin Xian exhaustively studied the gnomon and canopy and altered the ancient Zhou methods. Xiong saw this and deemed it a hard matter.

sentences.zh: 自昔周公定影王城，至漢朝，蓋器一改焉。

translations.literal: From antiquity, when the Duke of Zhou fixed the shadow at Wangcheng down to the Han dynasty, the canopy instrument was altered once.
translations.idiomatic: From antiquity, when the Duke of Zhou fixed the shadow at Wangcheng down to the Han, the canopy instrument was altered once.

sentences.zh: 渾天覆觀，以《靈憲》為文；

translations.literal: The spherical heaven looks down upon all; its text is the Mysterious Charter;
translations.idiomatic: The spherical heaven looks down upon all; its text is the Mysterious Charter;

sentences.zh: 蓋天仰觀，以《周髀》為法，覆仰難殊，大歸是一。

translations.literal: the canopy heaven looks up; its method is the Zhou Bi. Looking down and looking up differ in form, yet in the end they are one.
translations.idiomatic: the canopy heaven looks upward; its method is the Zhou Bi. To look down and to look up differ in form, yet in the end they are one.

sentences.zh: 古之人制者，所表天效玄象。

translations.literal: The men of old who devised these things displayed Heaven's mysterious signs.
translations.idiomatic: The ancients who devised these instruments displayed Heaven's mysterious signs.

sentences.zh: 芳以渾算精微，術機萬首，故約本為之省要，凡述二篇，合六法，名《四術周髀宗》。」

translations.literal: Fang, because spherical calculation is subtle and its devices number in the myriad, reduced the root text to essentials. In all he set forth two treatises comprising six methods, called Four Methods and the Zhou Bi Essentials.'
translations.idiomatic: Because spherical calculation is subtle and its devices number in the myriad, Fang reduced the root text to essentials. In all he set forth two treatises comprising six methods, called Four Methods and the Zhou Bi Essentials.'

sentences.zh: 又上党李業興撰新曆，自以為長於趙匪攵、何承天、祖沖之三家，芳難業興五闕。

translations.literal: Also, Li Yexing of Shangdang composed a new calendar, believing himself superior to the three houses of Zhao Wei, He Chengtian, and Zu Chongzhi. Fang challenged Yexing on five points of failure.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yexing of Shangdang also composed a new calendar, claiming to surpass the three traditions of Zhao Wei, He Chengtian, and Zu Chongzhi. Fang challenged Yexing on five defects.

sentences.zh: 又私撰曆書，名曰《靈憲曆》，算月頻大頻小，食必以朔，證據甚甄明。

translations.literal: He also privately composed a calendrical book called the Mysterious Charter Calendar, calculating that the moon would often appear large or small and that eclipses must fall on new moon days. The evidence was very clear.
translations.idiomatic: He also privately composed a calendrical book called the Mysterious Charter Calendar, showing that the moon would often appear large or small and that eclipses must fall on new-moon days. The evidence was very clear.

sentences.zh: 每云：「何承天亦為此法，而不能精。

translations.literal: He often said, 'He Chengtian also used this method, but could not refine it.
translations.idiomatic: He often said, 'He Chengtian also used this method, but could not perfect it.

sentences.zh: 《靈憲》若成，必當百代無異議者。」

translations.literal: If the Mysterious Charter is completed, there will surely be no dispute for a hundred generations.'
translations.idiomatic: If the Mysterious Charter is completed, there will surely be no dispute for a hundred generations.'

sentences.zh: 書未成而卒。

translations.literal: The book was unfinished when he died.
translations.idiomatic: The book was unfinished when he died.

sentences.zh: 宋景業，廣宗人也。

translations.literal: Song Jingye was a man of Guangzong.
translations.idiomatic: Song Jingye was a native of Guangzong.

sentences.zh: 明《周易》，為陰陽緯候之學，兼明歷數。

translations.literal: He understood the Book of Changes and the study of yin-yang, weft-texts, and seasonal signs, and was also versed in calendrical reckoning.
translations.idiomatic: He mastered the Book of Changes and the lore of yin-yang, weft-texts, and seasonal signs, and was also skilled in calendrical reckoning.

sentences.zh: 魏武定初，任北平太守。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Wuding era of Northern Wei he served as Governor of Northern Ping.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Wuding era in Northern Wei he served as Governor of Northern Ping.

sentences.zh: 齊文宣作相，在晉陽。

translations.literal: When Wenxuan became Chancellor he was at Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Wenxuan became Chancellor he was at Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 景業因高德政上言：「《易稽覽圖》曰：' 《鼎》，五月，聖人君，天與延年齒，東北水中，庶人王，高得之。

translations.literal: Jingye, through Gao Dezheng, submitted a memorial: 'The Apocryphal Charts of the Changes says, "The Cauldron, in the fifth month: a sage rules as lord; Heaven grants him prolonged years. In the northeastern waters a common man becomes king—Gao will obtain it.
translations.idiomatic: Jingye, through Gao Dezheng, submitted a memorial: 'The Apocryphal Charts of the Changes says, "The Cauldron, in the fifth month: a sage rules as lord; Heaven grants him prolonged years. In the northeastern waters a common man becomes king—Gao will obtain it.

sentences.zh: '謹案：東北水，謂勃海也。

translations.literal: I respectfully note: the northeastern water means the Bohai Sea.
translations.idiomatic: I respectfully note: the northeastern water means the Bohai Sea.

sentences.zh: 高得之，明高氏得天下也。」

translations.literal: That Gao will obtain it shows clearly that the Gao clan will gain the realm.'
translations.idiomatic: That Gao will obtain it shows clearly that the Gao clan will gain the realm.'

sentences.zh: 時魏武定八年三月也。

translations.literal: It was the third month of the eighth year of Wuding.
translations.idiomatic: This was the third month of the eighth year of Wuding.

sentences.zh: 高德政、徐之才並勸文宣應天受禪，乃之鄴。

translations.literal: Gao Dezheng and Xu Zhicai both urged Wenxuan to accept Heaven's mandate, and he went to Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Dezheng and Xu Zhicai both urged Wenxuan to accept Heaven's mandate, and he set out for Ye.

sentences.zh: 至平城都，諸大臣沮計，將還。

translations.literal: When he reached the capital at Pingcheng the great ministers discouraged the plan and he was about to return.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached the capital at Pingcheng the great ministers discouraged the plan and he was on the point of turning back.

sentences.zh: 賀拔仁等又云：「宋景業誤王，宜斬之以謝天下。」

translations.literal: He Ba Ren and others also said, 'Song Jingye has misled the prince. He should be executed to appease the realm.'
translations.idiomatic: He Ba Ren and others also said, 'Song Jingye has misled the prince. He should be executed to appease the realm.'

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「宋景業當為帝王師，何可殺也？」

translations.literal: The emperor said, 'Song Jingye is fit to be teacher to an emperor—how could he be killed?'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, 'Song Jingye is fit to be teacher to an emperor—how could he be killed?'

sentences.zh: 還至并州，文宣令景業筮，遇《乾》之《鼎》。

translations.literal: Returning to Bingzhou, Wenxuan ordered Jingye to perform divination. He obtained Qian changing to Cauldron.
translations.idiomatic: On returning to Bingzhou, Wenxuan ordered Jingye to perform divination. The result was Qian changing to Cauldron.

sentences.zh: 景業曰：「乾，君也，天也。

translations.literal: Jingye said, 'Qian is the ruler and is Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Jingye said, 'Qian is the ruler and is Heaven.

sentences.zh: 《易》曰：'時乘六龍，以禦天。

translations.literal: The Changes says, "In season he rides the six dragons to govern Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: The Changes says, "In season he rides the six dragons to govern Heaven.

sentences.zh: '《鼎》，五月卦也，宜以仲夏吉辰，順天受禪。」

translations.literal: Cauldron is the hexagram of the fifth month. You should on an auspicious day in midsummer receive the mandate in accord with Heaven.'
translations.idiomatic: Cauldron is the hexagram of the fifth month. You should on an auspicious day in midsummer receive the mandate in accord with Heaven.'

sentences.zh: 或曰：「陰陽書，五月不可入官。

translations.literal: Some said, 'Books of yin and yang hold that in the fifth month one must not enter office.
translations.idiomatic: Some said, 'Books of yin and yang hold that in the fifth month one must not enter office.

sentences.zh: 犯之，卒於其位。」

translations.literal: If one violates this, one dies in that post.'
translations.idiomatic: If one violates this, one dies in that post.'

sentences.zh: 景業曰：「此乃大吉，王為天子，無復下期，豈得不終於其位？」

translations.literal: Jingye said, 'This is in fact great good fortune. When the prince becomes Son of Heaven there is no further term of office—how could he fail to end his days in that post?'
translations.idiomatic: Jingye said, 'This is in fact great good fortune. When the prince becomes Son of Heaven there is no further term of office—how could he fail to end his days upon the throne?'

sentences.zh: 帝大悅。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was greatly pleased.

sentences.zh: 天保初，封長城縣子，受詔撰《天保曆》，李廣為之序。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianbao he was enfeoffed as Viscount of Changcheng and received an edict to compose the Tianbao Calendar, with Li Guang writing the preface.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Tianbao he was enfeoffed as Viscount of Changcheng and received an edict to compose the Tianbao Calendar, with Li Guang writing the preface.

sentences.zh: 許遵，高陽新城人也。

translations.literal: Xu Zun was a man of Xincheng in Gaoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Zun was a native of Xincheng in Gaoyang.

sentences.zh: 明《易》善筮，兼曉天文、風角、占相、逆刺，其驗若神。

translations.literal: He understood the Changes and was skilled in divination, and also knew astronomy, wind divination, physiognomy, and reverse divination. His verification was as if divine.
translations.idiomatic: He mastered the Changes and excelled at divination, and was also versed in astronomy, wind divination, physiognomy, and reverse divination. His predictions seemed almost supernatural.

sentences.zh: 齊神武引為館客。

translations.literal: Gao Huan took him on as a house guest.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan retained him as a house guest.

sentences.zh: 自言祿命不富貴，不橫死，是以任性疏誕，多所犯忤，神武常容借之。

translations.literal: He himself said that his allotted fortune was neither wealth nor high rank, and that he would not die by violence; therefore he acted as he pleased, rude and unrestrained, often giving offense, yet Gao Huan always indulged him.
translations.idiomatic: He declared that his allotted fortune held neither wealth nor high rank, and that he would not die by violence; therefore he acted as he pleased, rude and unrestrained, often giving offense, yet Gao Huan always indulged him.

sentences.zh: 芒陰之役，遵謂李業興曰：「賊為水陳，我為火陳，水勝火，我必敗。」

translations.literal: At the battle of Mangyin, Zun said to Li Yexing, 'The enemy has a water formation and we have a fire formation. Water overcomes fire—we are sure to be defeated.'
translations.idiomatic: At the battle of Mangyin, Zun said to Li Yexing, 'The enemy has a water formation and we have a fire formation. Water overcomes fire—we are sure to be defeated.'

sentences.zh: 果如其言。

translations.literal: It happened exactly as he said.
translations.idiomatic: Events unfolded exactly as he had said.

sentences.zh: 清河王嶽以遵為開府記室。

translations.literal: Prince Yue of Qinghe made Zun his Opening Office Recorder.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yue of Qinghe appointed Zun Opening Office Recorder.

sentences.zh: 嶽後將救江陵，遵曰：「此行必致後凶，宜辭疾勿去。」

translations.literal: When Yue was about to march to relieve Jiangling, Zun said, 'This expedition will surely bring later calamity. You should plead illness and not go.'
translations.idiomatic: When Yue was about to march to relieve Jiangling, Zun said, 'This expedition will surely bring later calamity. You should plead illness and stay behind.'

sentences.zh: 嶽曰：「勢不免去，正當與君同行。」

translations.literal: Yue said, 'Given the circumstances I cannot avoid going. I should simply go with you.'
translations.idiomatic: Yue said, 'Given the circumstances I cannot avoid going. I should simply go with you.'

sentences.zh: 遵曰：「遵好與生人相隨，不欲與死人同路。」

translations.literal: Zun said, 'Zun likes to keep company with the living and does not wish to walk the same road as the dead.
translations.idiomatic: Zun said, 'I prefer the company of the living and have no wish to walk the same road as the dead.

sentences.zh: 岳強給其馬以行。

translations.literal: Yue forcibly supplied him with a horse and made him go.
translations.idiomatic: Yue forcibly supplied him with a horse and made him go.

sentences.zh: 至都，尋喪。

translations.literal: When they reached the capital he soon died.
translations.idiomatic: When they reached the capital Yue soon died.

sentences.zh: 三台初成，文宣宴會尚書以上，三日不出。

translations.literal: When the Three Platforms tower was first completed, Wenxuan held a banquet for those of Minister rank and above and did not emerge for three days.
translations.idiomatic: When the Three Platforms tower was first completed, Wenxuan held a banquet for those of Minister rank and above and did not emerge for three days.

sentences.zh: 許遵妻季氏憂之，以問遵。

translations.literal: Zun's wife, née Ji, was anxious and asked Zun about it.
translations.idiomatic: Zun's wife, née Ji, was anxious and asked him about it.

sentences.zh: 遵曰：「明日當得三百匹絹。」

translations.literal: Zun said, 'Tomorrow you will receive three hundred bolts of silk.'
translations.idiomatic: Zun said, 'Tomorrow you will receive three hundred bolts of silk.'

sentences.zh: 季氏曰：「若然，當奉三束。

translations.literal: Ji said, 'If that is so, I shall offer three bundles in thanks.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Ji said, 'If that is so, I shall offer three bundles in thanks.

sentences.zh: 遵曰：「不滿十匹。」

translations.literal: Zun said, 'Not even ten bolts.'
translations.idiomatic: Zun said, 'Not even ten bolts.'

sentences.zh: 既而皆如言。

translations.literal: Afterwards everything happened as he had said.
translations.idiomatic: Afterwards everything happened as he had said.

sentences.zh: 文宣無道日盛，遵語人曰：「多折算來，吾筮此狂夫何時得死。」

translations.literal: As Wenxuan's cruelty grew daily, Zun told people, 'I have calculated again and again when this madman will die.'
translations.idiomatic: As Wenxuan's cruelty grew daily, Zun told people, 'I have calculated again and again when this madman will die.'

sentences.zh: 於是布算滿床，大言曰：「不出冬初，我乃不見。」

translations.literal: Thereupon he spread counting-rods over the bed and cried aloud, 'Before the beginning of winter I shall not see him.'
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he spread counting-rods over the bed and cried aloud, 'Before the beginning of winter I shall not see him.'

sentences.zh: 文宣以十月崩，遵果以九月死。

translations.literal: Wenxuan died in the tenth month, and Zun indeed died in the ninth.
translations.idiomatic: Wenxuan died in the tenth month, and Zun indeed died in the ninth.

sentences.zh: 子暉，亦學術數。

translations.literal: His son Hui also studied the arts of calculation.
translations.idiomatic: His son Hui also studied the arts of calculation.

sentences.zh: 遵謂曰：「汝聰明不及我，不勞多學。」

translations.literal: Zun told him, 'You are not as clever as I; there is no need to study much.'
translations.idiomatic: Zun told him, 'You are not as clever as I; there is no need to study much.'

sentences.zh: 唯授以婦人產法，豫言男女及產日，無不中。

translations.literal: He taught him only the method for childbirth, foretelling male or female and the day of delivery, and was never wrong.
translations.idiomatic: He taught him only the method for childbirth, foretelling whether the child would be male or female and the day of delivery, and was never wrong.

sentences.zh: 武成時，以此數獲賞焉。

translations.literal: In the Wucheng era he was repeatedly rewarded for this skill.
translations.idiomatic: In the Wucheng era he was repeatedly rewarded for this skill.

sentences.zh: 又有滎陽麹紹者，亦善占。

translations.literal: There was also Qu Shao of Xingyang, who was likewise skilled in divination.
translations.idiomatic: There was also Qu Shao of Xingyang, who was likewise skilled in divination.

sentences.zh: 侯景欲試之，使與郭生俱卜二伏牛何者先起。」

translations.literal: Hou Jing wished to test him and had him and Master Guo together perform divination on which of two recumbent oxen would rise first.'
translations.idiomatic: Hou Jing wished to test him and had him and Master Guo perform divination together on which of two recumbent oxen would rise first.'

sentences.zh: 卜得火兆，郭生曰：「赤牛先起。

translations.literal: They obtained the omen of fire. Master Guo said, 'The red ox will rise first.
translations.idiomatic: They obtained the omen of fire. Master Guo said, 'The red ox will rise first.

sentences.zh: 紹曰：「青牛先起。」

translations.literal: Shao said, 'The green ox will rise first.'
translations.idiomatic: Shao said, 'The green ox will rise first.'

sentences.zh: 景問其故，郭生曰：「火色赤，故知赤牛先起。」

translations.literal: Jing asked the reason. Master Guo said, 'Fire is red, so I know the red ox will rise first.'
translations.idiomatic: Jing asked the reason. Master Guo said, 'Fire is red, so I know the red ox will rise first.'

sentences.zh: 紹曰：「火將然，煙先起。

translations.literal: Shao said, 'When fire is about to burn, smoke rises first.
translations.idiomatic: Shao said, 'When fire is about to burn, smoke rises first.

sentences.zh: 煙上色青，故知青牛起。」

translations.literal: Smoke above is green, so I know the green ox will rise.'
translations.idiomatic: Smoke above is green, so I know the green ox will rise.'

sentences.zh: 既而如紹言。

translations.literal: Before long it happened as Shao had said.
translations.idiomatic: Before long it happened as Shao had said.

sentences.zh: 吳遵世，字季緒，勃海人也。

translations.literal: Wu Zunshi, courtesy name Jixu, was a man of Bohai.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Zunshi, styled Jixu, was a native of Bohai.

sentences.zh: 少學《易》。

translations.literal: In youth he studied the Changes.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he studied the Changes.

sentences.zh: 入恆山，忽見一老翁，授之開心符。

translations.literal: Entering Mount Heng, he suddenly saw an old man who gave him the Open-Heart Talisman.
translations.idiomatic: Entering Mount Heng, he suddenly met an old man who gave him the Open-Heart Talisman.

sentences.zh: 遵世跪，水吞之，遂明占卜。

translations.literal: Zunshi knelt, swallowed it with water, and thereupon understood divination.
translations.idiomatic: Zunshi knelt, swallowed it with water, and thereupon mastered divination.

sentences.zh: 後出遊京洛，以卜筮知名。

translations.literal: Later he traveled to the capital regions and became renowned for divination.
translations.idiomatic: Later he traveled to the capital regions and became renowned for divination.

sentences.zh: 魏孝武帝之將即位，使之筮，遇《否》之《萃》，曰：「先否後喜。」

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu of Wei was about to ascend the throne, he had Zunshi perform divination. He obtained Obstruction changing to Gathering and said, 'First obstruction, then joy.'
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu of Wei was about to ascend the throne, he had Zunshi perform divination. The result was Obstruction changing to Gathering, and Zunshi said, 'First obstruction, then joy.'

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「喜在何時？」

translations.literal: The emperor said, 'When will the joy come?'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, 'When will the joy come?'

sentences.zh: 遵世曰：「剛決柔，則春末夏初也。」

translations.literal: Zunshi said, 'When the firm overcomes the yielding, that will be late spring and early summer.'
translations.idiomatic: Zunshi said, 'When the firm overcomes the yielding, that will be late spring and early summer.'

sentences.zh: 又筮，遇《明夷》之《賁》，曰：「初登於天，後入於地。

translations.literal: He performed divination again and obtained Darkening of the Light changing to Adornment. He said, 'At first he ascends to Heaven; afterward he enters the earth.
translations.idiomatic: He performed divination again and obtained Darkening of the Light changing to Adornment. He said, 'At first he ascends to Heaven; afterward he enters the earth.

sentences.zh: 若能敬始慎終，不失法度，無憂入地矣。」

translations.literal: If you can be reverent at the beginning and careful at the end, not failing in law and measure, there is no need to fear entering the earth.'
translations.idiomatic: If you can be reverent at the beginning and careful at the end, not failing in law and measure, there is no need to fear entering the earth.'

sentences.zh: 終如其言。

translations.literal: In the end it happened as he had said.
translations.idiomatic: In the end it happened as he had said.

sentences.zh: 後齊文襄引為大將軍府墨曹參軍。

translations.literal: Later Wenxiang took him on as Ink Clerk in the Grand General's Office.
translations.idiomatic: Later Wenxiang retained him as Ink Clerk in the Grand General's Office.

sentences.zh: 從遊東山，有雲起，恐雨廢射，戲使筮。

translations.literal: On an excursion to Mount Dong clouds rose, and fearing rain would spoil the archery, Wenxiang playfully had him perform divination.
translations.idiomatic: On an excursion to Mount Dong clouds rose, and fearing rain would spoil the archery, Wenxiang playfully had him perform divination.

sentences.zh: 遇《剝》，李業興云：「坤上艮下，《剝》。

translations.literal: He obtained Splitting Apart. Li Yexing said, 'Earth above, mountain below—Splitting Apart.
translations.idiomatic: He obtained Splitting Apart. Li Yexing said, 'Earth above, mountain below—Splitting Apart.

sentences.zh: 艮為山，山出雲，故知有雨。」

translations.literal: Mountain is Gen; mountains produce clouds, so I know there will be rain.'
translations.idiomatic: Gen is the mountain; mountains produce clouds, so I know there will be rain.'

sentences.zh: 遵世云：「坤為地，土制水，故知無雨。」

translations.literal: Zunshi said, 'Earth is Kun; earth restrains water, so I know there will be no rain.
translations.idiomatic: Zunshi said, 'Kun is earth; earth restrains water, so I know there will be no rain.

sentences.zh: 文襄使崔暹書之云：「遵世若著，賞絹十匹；

translations.literal: Wenxiang had Cui Xian write it down: 'If Zunshi is right, reward him with ten bolts of silk;
translations.idiomatic: Wenxiang had Cui Xian write it down: 'If Zunshi is right, reward him with ten bolts of silk;

sentences.zh: 不著，罰杖十。

translations.literal: if wrong, punish him with ten strokes of the staff.
translations.idiomatic: if wrong, punish him with ten strokes of the staff.

sentences.zh: 業興若著，無賞；

translations.literal: If Yexing is right, no reward;
translations.idiomatic: If Yexing is right, no reward;

sentences.zh: 不著，罰杖十。」

translations.literal: if wrong, punish him with ten strokes of the staff.'
translations.idiomatic: if wrong, punish him with ten strokes of the staff.'

sentences.zh: 業興曰：「同是著，何獨無賞？」

translations.literal: Yexing said, 'If both are right, why is there no reward for me alone?'
translations.idiomatic: Yexing said, 'If both are right, why is there no reward for me alone?'

sentences.zh: 文襄曰：「遵世著，會我意，故賞也。」

translations.literal: Wenxiang said, 'When Zunshi is right it accords with my wish, and so he is rewarded.'
translations.idiomatic: Wenxiang said, 'When Zunshi is right it accords with my wish, and so he is rewarded.'

sentences.zh: 須臾雲散，二人各受賞罰。

translations.literal: Before long the clouds dispersed, and each received his reward or punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the clouds dispersed, and each received his reward or punishment.

sentences.zh: 皇建中，武成以丞相在鄴下居守，自致猜疑，甚懷憂懼。

translations.literal: In the Huangjian era, Wucheng, as Chancellor, remained at Ye to hold the capital and worked himself into suspicion, greatly filled with fear.
translations.idiomatic: In the Huangjian era, Wucheng, serving as Chancellor, remained at Ye to hold the capital and worked himself into suspicion, greatly filled with fear.

sentences.zh: 謀起兵，每宿輒令遵世筮。

translations.literal: He plotted to raise troops and every night had Zunshi perform divination.
translations.idiomatic: He plotted to raise troops and every night had Zunshi perform divination.

sentences.zh: 遵世云：「自有大慶。」

translations.literal: Zunshi said, 'There will be great celebration of itself.'
translations.idiomatic: Zunshi said, 'There will be great celebration of itself.'

sentences.zh: 由是不決。

translations.literal: Because of this he could not decide.
translations.idiomatic: Because of this he could not make up his mind.

sentences.zh: 俄而趙郡王等奉太后令，以遺詔追武成。

translations.literal: Before long the Prince of Zhao and others, acting on the empress dowager's order, recalled Wucheng by the late emperor's testament.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the Prince of Zhao and others, acting on the empress dowager's order, recalled Wucheng by the late emperor's testament.

sentences.zh: 更令筮之。

translations.literal: He again had Zunshi perform divination.
translations.idiomatic: He again had Zunshi perform divination.

sentences.zh: 遵世云：「比已作十餘卦，其占自然有天下之征。」

translations.literal: Zunshi said, 'I have already performed more than ten divinations, and the omens naturally show the signs of possessing the realm.'
translations.idiomatic: Zunshi said, 'I have already performed more than ten divinations, and the omens naturally show the signs of possessing the realm.'

sentences.zh: 及即位，除中書舍人，固辭老疾，授中散大夫。

translations.literal: When Wucheng took the throne he was appointed Palace Secretary, but firmly declined on grounds of age and illness and was made Grand Master of Palace Leisure.
translations.idiomatic: When Wucheng took the throne he was appointed Palace Secretary, but firmly declined on grounds of age and illness and was made Grand Master of Palace Leisure.

sentences.zh: 和士開封王，妻元氏無子，以側室長孫為妃，令遵世筮。

translations.literal: He Shikai was enfeoffed as prince. His wife, née Yuan, had no son, and he took the eldest son of a concubine as consort. He ordered Zunshi to perform divination.
translations.idiomatic: He Shikai was enfeoffed as prince. His wife, née Yuan, had no son, and he took the eldest son of a concubine as consort. He ordered Zunshi to perform divination.

sentences.zh: 遵世云：「此卦偶與占同。」

translations.literal: Zunshi said, 'This hexagram happens to match my earlier divination.'
translations.idiomatic: Zunshi said, 'This hexagram happens to match my earlier divination.'

sentences.zh: 乃出其占書云：「元氏無子，長孫為妃。」

translations.literal: He then produced his book of divinations, which read, 'The Yuan clan has no son; the eldest grandson becomes consort.'
translations.idiomatic: He then produced his book of divinations, which read, 'The Yuan clan has no son; the eldest grandson becomes consort.'

sentences.zh: 士開喜於妙中，於是起叫而舞。

translations.literal: Shikai rejoiced at the uncanny accuracy and thereupon leapt up shouting and dancing.
translations.idiomatic: Shikai rejoiced at the uncanny accuracy and thereupon leapt up shouting and dancing.

sentences.zh: 遵世著《易林雜占》百餘卷。

translations.literal: Zunshi wrote Miscellaneous Divinations from the Forest of Changes in more than a hundred scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: Zunshi wrote Miscellaneous Divinations from the Forest of Changes in more than a hundred scrolls.

sentences.zh: 後預尉遲迥亂，死焉。

translations.literal: Later he took part in Yuchi Jiong's rebellion and died in it.
translations.idiomatic: Later he took part in Yuchi Jiong's rebellion and died in it.

sentences.zh: 趙輔和，清都臨漳人也。

translations.literal: Zhao Fuhe was a man of Linzhang in Qingdu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Fuhe was a native of Linzhang in Qingdu.

sentences.zh: 少以明《易》善筮為齊神武館客。

translations.literal: In youth, because he understood the Changes and was skilled in divination, he became a house guest of Gao Huan.
translations.idiomatic: From youth, because he mastered the Changes and excelled at divination, he became a house guest of Gao Huan.

sentences.zh: 神武崩于晉陽，葬有日矣，文襄令文宣與吳遵世等擇地，頻卜不吉。

translations.literal: When Gao Huan died at Jinyang and the day of burial was set, Wenxiang ordered Wenxuan, together with Wu Zunshi and others, to choose the site. Repeated divinations were inauspicious.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Huan died at Jinyang and the day of burial was set, Wenxiang ordered Wenxuan, together with Wu Zunshi and others, to choose the site. Repeated divinations were inauspicious.

sentences.zh: 又至一所，筮遇《革》，咸雲凶。

translations.literal: When they came to one place and performed divination they obtained Revolution. All said it was ill-omened.
translations.idiomatic: When they came to one place and performed divination they obtained Revolution. All said it was ill-omened.

sentences.zh: 輔和少年，最在眾人後，進云：「《革卦》於天下人皆凶，唯王家用之大吉。

translations.literal: Fuhe was young and stood last among the company. He stepped forward and said, 'The Revolution hexagram is ill-omened for all under Heaven, but for the royal house it is greatly auspicious.
translations.idiomatic: Fuhe was young and stood last among the company. He stepped forward and said, 'The Revolution hexagram is ill-omened for all under Heaven, but for the royal house it is greatly auspicious.

sentences.zh: 《革彖辭》雲'湯武革命，應天順人。

translations.literal: The Judgment of Revolution says, "Tang and Wu changed the mandate, responding to Heaven and accord with the people."
translations.idiomatic: The Judgment of Revolution says, "Tang and Wu changed the mandate, responding to Heaven and accord with the people."

sentences.zh: '」文宣遽登車，顧云：「以此地為定。」

translations.literal: Wenxuan at once mounted his carriage, looked back, and said, 'Let this place be fixed.'
translations.idiomatic: Wenxuan at once mounted his carriage, looked back, and said, 'Let this place be fixed.'

sentences.zh: 即義平陵也。

translations.literal: It was the Yiping Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: It was the Yiping Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 有人父為刺史，得書雲疾。

translations.literal: A man's father was governor and sent word that he was ill.
translations.idiomatic: A man's father was governor and sent word that he was ill.

sentences.zh: 是人詣館，別托相知者筮。

translations.literal: The man came to the guest house and, through another acquaintance, had divination performed.
translations.idiomatic: The man came to the guest house and, through another acquaintance, had divination performed.

sentences.zh: 遇《泰》，筮者云：「此卦甚吉。」

translations.literal: He obtained Peace. The diviner said, 'This hexagram is very auspicious.'
translations.idiomatic: He obtained Peace. The diviner said, 'This hexagram is very auspicious.'

sentences.zh: 是人出後，輔和謂筮者云：「《泰》，乾下坤上，則父入土矣，豈得言吉。」

translations.literal: After the man left, Fuhe said to the diviner, 'Peace has Heaven below and Earth above—the father enters the earth. How can it be called auspicious?'
translations.idiomatic: After the man left, Fuhe said to the diviner, 'Peace has Heaven below and Earth above—the father enters the earth. How can it be called auspicious?'

sentences.zh: 果凶問至。

translations.literal: Ill news of death indeed arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Ill news of death indeed arrived.

sentences.zh: 有人父疾，托輔和筮，遇《乾》之《晉》，慰諭令去。

translations.literal: Another man's father was ill and entrusted Fuhe with divination. He obtained Qian changing to Advance, consoled and urged him to go.
translations.idiomatic: Another man's father was ill and entrusted Fuhe with divination. He obtained Qian changing to Advance, consoled the man, and urged him to go.

sentences.zh: 後告人云：「《乾》之遊魂。

translations.literal: Later he told people, 'Qian changing to the Wandering Soul.
translations.idiomatic: Later he told people, 'Qian changing to the Wandering Soul.

sentences.zh: 乾為天，為父，父變為魂，而升於天，能無死乎？」

translations.literal: Qian is Heaven and is the father. The father becomes a soul and ascends to Heaven—how could he not die?'
translations.idiomatic: Qian is Heaven and is the father. The father becomes a soul and ascends to Heaven—how could he not die?'

sentences.zh: 亦如其言。

translations.literal: This too happened as he had said.
translations.idiomatic: This too happened as he had said.

sentences.zh: 大寧、武平中，筮後宮誕男女及時日，多中，遂至通直常侍。

translations.literal: In the Daining and Wuping eras he performed divination on whether children born in the inner palace would be male or female and on the days of birth. He was often right and rose to Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In the Daining and Wuping eras he performed divination on whether children born in the inner palace would be male or female and on the days of birth. He was often right and rose to Regular Attendant.

sentences.zh: 入周，亦為儀同。

translations.literal: After entering Zhou he also held the rank of Yitong.
translations.idiomatic: After entering Zhou he also held the rank of Yitong.

sentences.zh: 隋開皇中，卒。

translations.literal: In the Kaihuang era of Sui he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the Kaihuang era of Sui he died.

sentences.zh: 皇甫玉，不知何許人也，善相人。

translations.literal: Huangfu Yu—no one knows where he was from—was skilled in physiognomy.
translations.idiomatic: Huangfu Yu—no one knows where he was from—was skilled in physiognomy.

sentences.zh: 齊文襄之自潁川歸，文宣從後。

translations.literal: When Wenxiang returned from Yingchuan, Wenxuan followed behind.
translations.idiomatic: When Wenxiang returned from Yingchuan, Wenxuan followed behind.

sentences.zh: 玉於傍縱觀，謂人曰：「大將軍不作物。」

translations.literal: Yu watched from the side and told people, 'The Grand General will not become Son of Heaven.'
translations.idiomatic: Yu watched from the side and told people, 'The Grand General will not become Son of Heaven.'

sentences.zh: 指文宣曰：「會道北垂鼻洟者。」

translations.literal: Pointing at Wenxuan he said, 'It will be the one with the hanging nose and running mucus in the north of the road.
translations.idiomatic: Pointing at Wenxuan he said, 'It will be the one with the hanging nose and running mucus on the north side of the road.

sentences.zh: 及文宣即位，試玉相術，故以帛巾襪其眼，使曆摸諸人。

translations.literal: When Wenxuan took the throne he tested Yu's art of physiognomy. He therefore bound his eyes with a cloth kerchief and had him feel his way among the people.
translations.idiomatic: When Wenxuan took the throne he tested Yu's art of physiognomy. He bound his eyes with a cloth kerchief and had him feel his way among the people.

sentences.zh: 至文宣曰：「此最大達官。」

translations.literal: Coming to Wenxuan he said, 'This is the highest official.'
translations.idiomatic: Coming to Wenxuan he said, 'This is the highest official.'

sentences.zh: 于任城王曰：「當至丞相。」

translations.literal: Of Prince Rencheng he said, 'He will reach the rank of Chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: Of Prince Rencheng he said, 'He will reach the rank of Chancellor.

sentences.zh: 於常山、長廣二王，並曰：「亦貴。」

translations.literal: Of the Princes of Changshan and Changgang he said together, 'They too will be noble.
translations.idiomatic: Of the Princes of Changshan and Changgang he said together, 'They too will be noble.

sentences.zh: 至石動桶曰：「此弄癡人。」

translations.literal: Coming to Shi Dongtong he said, 'This is a fool who plays the fool.
translations.idiomatic: Coming to Shi Dongtong he said, 'This is a fool who plays the fool.

sentences.zh: 至二供膳曰：「正得好飲食而已。」

translations.literal: Coming to the two food servers he said, 'They will simply get good food and drink.
translations.idiomatic: Coming to the two food servers he said, 'They will simply get good food and drink.

sentences.zh: 玉嘗為高歸彥相曰：「位極人臣，但莫反。」

translations.literal: Yu once read the physiognomy of Gao Guiyan and said, 'Your rank will reach the summit of ministers, but do not rebel.'
translations.idiomatic: Yu once read the physiognomy of Gao Guiyan and said, 'Your rank will reach the summit of ministers, but do not rebel.'

sentences.zh: 歸彥曰：「我何為反？」

translations.literal: Guiyan said, 'Why would I rebel?
translations.idiomatic: Guiyan said, 'Why would I rebel?

sentences.zh: 玉曰：「公有反骨。」

translations.literal: Yu said, 'You have rebellious bones.
translations.idiomatic: Yu said, 'You have rebellious bones.

sentences.zh: 孝昭賜趙郡王十死不問，王喜曰：「皇甫玉相臣，雲當惡死，今復何慮？」

translations.literal: Xiaozhao granted the Prince of Zhao ten deaths without question. The prince rejoiced and said, 'Huangfu Yu read my physiognomy and said I would meet a violent death—what is there to fear now?'
translations.idiomatic: Xiaozhao granted the Prince of Zhao ten deaths without question. The prince rejoiced and said, 'Huangfu Yu read my physiognomy and said I would meet a violent death—what is there to fear now?'

sentences.zh: 帝以玉輒為諸王相，心不平之。

translations.literal: The emperor, displeased that Yu so readily read the physiognomy of the princes, was ill at ease in his heart.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, displeased that Yu so readily read the physiognomy of the princes, was ill at ease in his heart.

sentences.zh: 玉謂其妻曰：「殿上者不過二年。」

translations.literal: Yu told his wife, 'The one on the throne will not last two years.
translations.idiomatic: Yu told his wife, 'The one on the throne will not last two years.

sentences.zh: 妻以告舍人斛斯洪慶妻，洪慶以啟帝。

translations.literal: His wife told the wife of Palace Attendant Husih Hongqing, and Hongqing reported it to the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: His wife told the wife of Palace Attendant Husih Hongqing, and Hongqing reported it to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 怒曰：「向婦女小兒評論萬乘主！」

translations.literal: In anger he said, 'A mere woman and child dares judge the lord of ten thousand chariots!'
translations.idiomatic: In anger he said, 'A mere woman and child dares judge the lord of ten thousand chariots!'

sentences.zh: 敕召玉。

translations.literal: He ordered Yu summoned.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Yu summoned.

sentences.zh: 玉每照鏡，自言兵死。

translations.literal: Yu often looked in the mirror and said himself that he would die by the sword.
translations.idiomatic: Yu often looked in the mirror and said himself that he would die by the sword.

sentences.zh: 及被召，謂妻曰：「我今去，不回，若過日午時，當得活。」

translations.literal: When he was summoned he told his wife, 'I go now and will not return. If I pass the hour of noon I may live.'
translations.idiomatic: When he was summoned he told his wife, 'I go now and will not return. If I pass the hour of noon I may live.'

sentences.zh: 既至正中，遂斬之。

translations.literal: When he arrived it was exactly midday, and he was executed.
translations.idiomatic: When he arrived it was exactly midday, and he was executed.

sentences.zh: 文襄時，有吳士，雙盲，妙於聲。

translations.literal: In Wenxiang's time there was a man of Wu, blind in both eyes, marvelous in the art of sound.
translations.idiomatic: In Wenxiang's time there was a man of Wu, blind in both eyes, marvelous in the art of sound.

sentences.zh: 文襄曆試之，聞劉桃枝聲曰：「有所系屬，然當大富貴。

translations.literal: Wenxiang tested him repeatedly. Hearing Liu Taozhi's voice he said, 'He has someone he is bound to, yet he will become greatly rich and noble.
translations.idiomatic: Wenxiang tested him repeatedly. Hearing Liu Taozhi's voice he said, 'He has someone he is bound to, yet he will become greatly rich and noble.

sentences.zh: 王侯將相，多死其手。

translations.literal: Kings, marquises, generals, and chancellors—many will die by his hand.
translations.idiomatic: Kings, marquises, generals, and chancellors—many will die by his hand.

sentences.zh: 譬如鷹犬，為人所使。」

translations.literal: He is like a hawk or hound, used by others.'
translations.idiomatic: He is like a hawk or hound, used by others.'

sentences.zh: 聞趙道德聲曰：「亦系屬人，富貴翕赫，不及前人。」

translations.literal: Hearing Zhao Daode's voice he said, 'He too is bound to others; his wealth and glory blaze forth, but not equal to the former man.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing Zhao Daode's voice he said, 'He too is bound to others; his wealth and glory blaze forth, but not equal to the former man.

sentences.zh: 聞侯呂芬聲，與道德相似。

translations.literal: Hearing Hou Lüfen's voice, it was similar to Daode's.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing Hou Lüfen's voice, it was similar to Daode's.

sentences.zh: 聞太原公聲曰：「當為人主。」

translations.literal: Hearing the voice of the Duke of Taiyuan he said, 'He will become lord of men.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing the voice of the Duke of Taiyuan he said, 'He will become lord of men.

sentences.zh: 聞文襄聲，不動。

translations.literal: Hearing Wenxiang's voice, he did not stir.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing Wenxiang's voice, he did not stir.

sentences.zh: 崔暹私掏之，乃謬言：「亦國主也。」

translations.literal: Cui Xian privately prompted him, and he then falsely said, 'He too is fit to be lord of the state.'
translations.idiomatic: Cui Xian privately prompted him, and he then falsely said, 'He too is fit to be lord of the state.'

sentences.zh: 文襄以為我家群奴猶極貴，況吾身也。

translations.literal: Wenxiang thought, 'Even the slaves of my house reach the utmost nobility—how much more myself!
translations.idiomatic: Wenxiang thought, 'Even the slaves of my house reach the utmost nobility—how much more myself!

sentences.zh: 又時有御史賈子儒，亦能相人。

translations.literal: At that time there was also the Censor Jia Ziru, who could also read physiognomy.
translations.idiomatic: At that time there was also the Censor Jia Ziru, who could also read physiognomy.

sentences.zh: 崔暹嘗將子儒私視文襄，子儒曰：「人有七尺之形，不如一尺之面；

translations.literal: Cui Xian once took Ziru to observe Wenxiang privately. Ziru said, 'A man's seven-foot frame is not equal to one foot of face;
translations.idiomatic: Cui Xian once took Ziru to observe Wenxiang privately. Ziru said, 'A man's seven-foot frame is not equal to one foot of face;

sentences.zh: 一之面，不如一寸之眼。

translations.literal: one foot of face is not equal to one inch of eye.
translations.idiomatic: one foot of face is not equal to one inch of eye.

sentences.zh: 大將軍臉薄眄速，非帝王相也。」

translations.literal: The Grand General's face is thin and his glances are quick—he does not have the physiognomy of an emperor.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand General's face is thin and his glances are quick—he does not have the physiognomy of an emperor.

sentences.zh: 竟如言。

translations.literal: In the end it was exactly as he had said.
translations.idiomatic: In the end, everything came to pass exactly as he had foretold.

sentences.zh: 齊代善相者，有館客趙瓊。

translations.literal: In Qi there was one skilled at physiognomy, the house guest Zhao Qiong.
translations.idiomatic: During Qi there lived a master physiognomist, a house guest named Zhao Qiong.

sentences.zh: 其婦叔寄弓，弓已轉在人處，盡知之。

translations.literal: When his wife's uncle Ji Gong sent away a bow, and the bow had already passed into another's hands, he knew everything.
translations.idiomatic: When his wife's uncle Ji Gong disposed of a bow that had already changed hands, Zhao Qiong knew every detail of the transaction.

sentences.zh: 時人疑其別有假託，不然，則姑布子卿不如也。

translations.literal: People of the time suspected he had some other artifice or pretense; otherwise Gu Buzi would not have been his inferior.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporaries suspected he relied on some hidden trickery; otherwise the famed Gu Buzi could scarcely have been his better.

sentences.zh: 初，魏正始前，有沙門學相，遊懷朔，舉目見人，皆有富貴之表。

translations.literal: At the beginning, before Wei's Zhengshi era, there was a Buddhist monk who studied physiognomy. Traveling to Huaishuo, he looked up and saw that everyone had the appearance of wealth and rank.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, before the Zhengshi era of Wei, a Buddhist monk trained in physiognomy traveled to Huaishuo. Every person he looked upon bore the marks of wealth and high station.

sentences.zh: 以為必無此理，燔其書。

translations.literal: Thinking this could not possibly be so, he burned his books.
translations.idiomatic: Convinced such a thing was impossible, he burned his texts on the art.

sentences.zh: 而後皆如言，乃知相法不虛也。

translations.literal: Afterwards everything was as he had said, and he then knew that physiognomy was no empty art.
translations.idiomatic: Later events proved him right on every count, and he understood at last that physiognomy was no hollow superstition.

sentences.zh: 解法選，河內人也。

translations.literal: Jiefa Xuan was a man of Henei.
translations.idiomatic: Jiefa Xuan came from Henei.

sentences.zh: 少明相術，又受《易》于權會，筮亦頗工。

translations.literal: In youth he was skilled in physiognomy; he also received the Changes from Quan Hui, and his divination was quite adept.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he excelled at physiognomy; he had also studied the Book of Changes under Quan Hui, and his divination was remarkably sure.

sentences.zh: 陳郡袁叔德以太子庶子出行博陵太守，不願之官，以親老言于執政楊愔。

translations.literal: Yuan Shude of Chen Commandery, as a crown prince attendant, went out to serve as Administrator of Boling. He did not wish to take the post and, citing aged parents, spoke to the chief minister Yang Yin.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shude of Chen Commandery, serving as an attendant to the crown prince, was dispatched as Administrator of Boling. Unwilling to go, he pleaded with Chief Minister Yang Yin on account of his elderly parents.

sentences.zh: 愔語云：「既非正除，尋當遣代。」

translations.literal: Yin said, 'Since this is not a regular appointment, a replacement will soon be sent.
translations.idiomatic: Yin told him, 'This is not a permanent commission; a successor will be sent before long.

sentences.zh: 叔德意欲留尊累在京，令法選占。

translations.literal: Shude wished to keep his honored kin in the capital and had Jiefa Xuan perform divination.
translations.idiomatic: Shude hoped to keep his family in the capital and asked Jiefa Xuan to cast the lots.

sentences.zh: 云：「不逾三年，得代，終不還也。」

translations.literal: Xuan said, 'Within three years you will be replaced, and in the end you will not return.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan replied, 'You will be relieved within three years—and you will never come back.

sentences.zh: 勸其盡家而行。

translations.literal: He urged him to move his entire household when he went.
translations.idiomatic: He advised Shude to take his whole household when he departed.

sentences.zh: 又為叔德相云：「公邑邑，終為吏部尚書，鑒照人物。」

translations.literal: He also read Shude's physiognomy and said, 'Sir, you are restless now, but in the end you will become Minister of Personnel, discerning and illuminating men's characters.
translations.idiomatic: Reading Shude's features, he also said, 'You are troubled now, but you will eventually become Minister of Personnel, judging men with clear insight.

sentences.zh: 後皆如言。

translations.literal: Afterwards everything was as he had said.
translations.idiomatic: In time, every prediction proved true.

sentences.zh: 又頻為和士開相中，士開牒為開府行參軍。

translations.literal: He also repeatedly read He Shikai's physiognomy favorably; Shikai appointed him Acting Staff Member of the Opening Office.
translations.idiomatic: He also read He Shikai's features several times to good effect, and Shikai made him Acting Staff Member of the Opening Office.

sentences.zh: 魏甯，钜鹿人也。

translations.literal: Wei Ning was a man of Julu.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Ning came from Julu.

sentences.zh: 以善推祿命，徵為館客。

translations.literal: Because he was skilled at calculating fate and fortune, he was summoned as a house guest.
translations.idiomatic: Skilled at reading fate and fortune, he was retained as a house guest.

sentences.zh: 武成以己生年月，托為異人，問之。

translations.literal: Emperor Wucheng, using another man's birth year and month as a pretext, posed as a stranger and questioned him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wucheng disguised himself as a stranger, giving another man's birth date, and put questions to him.

sentences.zh: 寧曰：「極富貴，今年入墓。」

translations.literal: Ning said, 'Extremely wealthy and noble—and this year you enter the tomb.
translations.idiomatic: Ning said, 'You are destined for the highest wealth and rank—and this year you enter the grave.

sentences.zh: 武成驚曰：「是我！」

translations.literal: Wucheng startled and said, 'That is me!'
translations.idiomatic: Wucheng started and cried, 'That is me!'

sentences.zh: 寧變辭曰：「若帝王，自有法。」

translations.literal: Ning changed his words and said, 'If one is an emperor, there is a law of his own.'
translations.idiomatic: Ning quickly amended his answer: 'For an emperor, the rules are different.'

sentences.zh: 又有陽子術語人曰：「謠言：盧十六，雉十四，犍子拍頭三十二。

translations.literal: There was also Yang Zishu, who told people, 'The saying goes: Lu sixteen, pheasant fourteen, the lad claps his head—thirty-two.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Zishu also told people, 'There is a saying: Lu at sixteen, the pheasant at fourteen, the lad clapping his head—thirty-two.

sentences.zh: 且四八天之大數，太上之祚，恐不過此。」

translations.literal: Moreover, four times eight is Heaven's great number; the reign of the Supreme Lord, I fear, will not exceed this.
translations.idiomatic: Four times eight is Heaven's great number; the Supreme Sovereign's reign, I suspect, will not surpass it.

sentences.zh: 既而武成崩，年三十二。

translations.literal: Before long Wucheng died, aged thirty-two.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Wucheng died, at the age of thirty-two.

sentences.zh: 綦母懷文，不知何許人也，以道術事齊神武。

translations.literal: Qimou Huaiwen—no one knew whence he came—served Northern Qi's Shenwu with Daoist arts.
translations.idiomatic: Qimou Huaiwen, whose origins were unknown, served Gao Huan, the Shenwu Emperor, with occult arts.

sentences.zh: 武定初，齊軍戰芒山，時齊軍旗幟盡赤，西軍盡黑，懷文曰：「赤，火色；

translations.literal: In the early Wuding era, when Qi forces fought at Mangshan, Qi's banners were all red and the Western army all black. Huaiwen said, 'Red is the color of fire;
translations.idiomatic: Early in Wuding, when Qi fought at Mangshan, Qi's banners were all red and the Western army's all black. Huaiwen said, 'Red is the color of fire;

sentences.zh: 黑。

translations.literal: black
translations.idiomatic: black

sentences.zh: 水色。

translations.literal: is the color of water.
translations.idiomatic: is the color of water.

sentences.zh: 水能滅火，不宜以赤對黑。

translations.literal: Water can extinguish fire; it is not fitting to oppose black with red.
translations.idiomatic: Water quenches fire; red should not be matched against black.

sentences.zh: 土勝水，宜改為黃。」

translations.literal: Earth overcomes water; you should change to yellow.
translations.idiomatic: Earth conquers water; you should change to yellow.

sentences.zh: 神武遂改為赭黃，所謂河陽幡者也。

translations.literal: Shenwu thereupon changed to ochre-yellow—the so-called Heyang banners.
translations.idiomatic: Shenwu changed his banners to ochre-yellow—the banners later known as the Heyang standards.

sentences.zh: 懷文造宿鐵刀，其法，燒生鐵精以重柔鋌，數宿則成剛。

translations.literal: Huaiwen made night-forged iron blades. The method was to burn raw iron essence and repeatedly fold it with soft iron ingots; after several nights it became hard.
translations.idiomatic: Huaiwen devised night-forged iron blades. Raw iron was fired and folded with soft ingots again and again; after several nights the metal grew hard.

sentences.zh: 以柔鐵為刀脊，浴以五牲之溺，淬以五牲之脂，斬甲過三十劄。

translations.literal: Soft iron formed the spine of the blade; it was bathed in the urine of the five sacrificial beasts and quenched in their fat, and could cut through more than thirty layers of armor.
translations.idiomatic: The spine was soft iron, bathed in the urine of the five sacrificial animals and quenched in their fat; such blades could shear through more than thirty layers of armor.

sentences.zh: 今襄國冶家所鑄宿柔鋌，是其遺法，作刀猶甚快利，但不能頓截三十劄也。

translations.literal: The night-soft ingots cast today by smiths of Xiangguo preserve his method; the knives are still very sharp, but they cannot sever thirty layers at a stroke.
translations.idiomatic: Smiths of Xiangguo still cast night-soft ingots by his method; their blades remain keen, but they cannot cut thirty layers in one blow.

sentences.zh: 懷文又云：「廣平郡南幹子城，是幹將鑄劍處，其土可瑩刀。」

translations.literal: Huaiwen also said, 'Ganzi Fortress south of Guangping Commandery is where Gan Jiang forged swords; its soil can polish blades bright.
translations.idiomatic: Huaiwen also said, 'Ganzi Fortress south of Guangping Commandery is where the swordsmith Gan Jiang worked; its soil can bring a blade to a mirror finish.

sentences.zh: 每云：「昔在晉陽為監館，館中有一蠕蠕客，同館胡沙門指語懷文云：此人別有異算術。

translations.literal: He often said, 'Formerly at Jinyang I was overseer of the hostel. A Rouran guest lodged there, and a foreign Buddhist monk in the same hostel pointed at him and told Huaiwen that this man had a different, wondrous art of calculation.
translations.idiomatic: He often recalled, 'At Jinyang I supervised the hostel. A Rouran guest stayed there, and a foreign monk in the same lodge pointed to him and told me that this man possessed a strange gift for calculation.

sentences.zh: '仍指庭中一棗樹云：'令其布運算元，即知其實數。

translations.literal: He then pointed at a jujube tree in the courtyard and said, 'Have him spread calculation tokens beneath it, and at once the true number will be known.'
translations.idiomatic: The monk then indicated a jujube tree in the courtyard and said, 'Have him lay out his counting tokens beneath it, and the true count will be revealed.'

sentences.zh: '乃試之，並辨若干純赤，若干赤白相半。

translations.literal: They tested him, and he distinguished how many were wholly red and how many half red and half white.
translations.idiomatic: They tried him, and he distinguished how many fruits were wholly red and how many were half red and half white.

sentences.zh: 於是剝數之，唯少一子。

translations.literal: They then peeled and counted them; only one fruit was short.
translations.idiomatic: They peeled and counted the fruit; one was missing.

sentences.zh: 算者曰：'必不少，但更撼之。

translations.literal: The calculator said, 'It cannot be short; only shake the tree again.'
translations.idiomatic: The calculator said, 'The count cannot be wrong—shake the tree once more.'

sentences.zh: '果落一實。」

translations.literal: Sure enough one fruit fell.'
translations.idiomatic: Sure enough, one fruit dropped.'

sentences.zh: 懷文位信州刺史。

translations.literal: Huaiwen held the post of Inspector of Xinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Huaiwen served as Inspector of Xinzhou.

sentences.zh: 又有孫正言謂人曰：「我昔聞曹普演有言：'高王諸兒，阿保當為天子，至高德之承之，當滅。

translations.literal: There was also Sun Zhengyan, who told people, 'I once heard Cao Puyan say, "Among the sons of the High King, Abao will become Son of Heaven; when it reaches Degao and Cheng, there will be extinction.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Zhengyan also told people, 'I once heard Cao Puyan say, "Of the High King's sons, Abao will become emperor; when the line reaches Degao and the reign Cheng, it will perish.

sentences.zh: '阿保，謂天保也；

translations.literal: Abao meant Tianbao;
translations.idiomatic: Abao referred to Tianbao;

sentences.zh: 德之，謂德昌也；

translations.literal: Degao meant Dechang;
translations.idiomatic: Degao meant Dechang;

sentences.zh: 滅年號承光，即承之矣。」

translations.literal: extinction'—the reign title Chengguang, that is, 'Cheng'—was fulfilled thereby."
translations.idiomatic: and 'extinction' pointed to the reign title Chengguang—'Cheng'—which duly came to pass."

sentences.zh: 張子信，河內人也。

translations.literal: Zhang Zixin was a man of Henei.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zixin came from Henei.

sentences.zh: 頗涉文學，少以醫術知名。

translations.literal: He had some acquaintance with letters and in youth was known for medical skill.
translations.idiomatic: He had some literary training and in youth was known for his medical skill.

sentences.zh: 恆隱白鹿山，時出遊京邑，甚為魏收、崔季舒所重。

translations.literal: He always hid himself on White Deer Mountain, but sometimes came to the capital, where Wei Shou and Cui Jishu held him in high regard.
