translations.idiomatic: He lived in seclusion on White Deer Mountain, though he sometimes visited the capital, where Wei Shou and Cui Jishu greatly esteemed him.

sentences.zh: 大寧中，徵為尚藥典禦。

translations.literal: In the Daning era he was summoned as Director of the Imperial Pharmacy.
translations.idiomatic: During Daning he was summoned to serve as Director of the Imperial Pharmacy.

sentences.zh: 武平初，又乙太中大夫征之，聽其所志，還山。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Wuping he was again summoned as Grand Master of Palace Attendance, but was allowed to follow his wish and returned to the mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Wuping he was again summoned as Grand Master of Palace Attendance, but was permitted to follow his inclination and returned to the mountain.

sentences.zh: 又善《易》筮及風角之術。

translations.literal: He was also skilled in Changes divination and wind-angle arts.
translations.idiomatic: He was also adept at divination with the Book of Changes and wind-angle prognostication.

sentences.zh: 武衛奚永洛與子信對坐，有鵲鳴庭樹，鬥而墮焉。

translations.literal: Xi Yongluo of the Martial Guard sat facing Zixin when a magpie cried in the courtyard tree, fought, and fell.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Yongluo of the Martial Guard was sitting opposite Zixin when a magpie cried in the courtyard tree, fought, and fell to the ground.

sentences.zh: 子信曰：「不善。

translations.literal: Zixin said, 'This is ill-omened.
translations.idiomatic: Zixin said, 'This bodes ill.

sentences.zh: 向夕，當有風從西南來，曆此樹，拂堂角，則有口舌事。

translations.literal: Toward evening wind will come from the southwest, pass this tree, and brush the hall corner—then there will be a matter of quarrel and slander.
translations.idiomatic: Toward evening wind will rise from the southwest, sweep this tree, and strike the hall corner—then trouble of tongue and quarrel will follow.

sentences.zh: 今夜有人喚，必不可往，雖敕亦以病辭。」

translations.literal: Tonight if someone summons you, you must on no account go; even if it is an imperial order, plead illness.
translations.idiomatic: If you are summoned tonight, you must not go; even if the summons bears the imperial seal, plead sickness.

sentences.zh: 子信去後，果有風如其言。

translations.literal: After Zixin left, wind indeed came as he had said.
translations.idiomatic: After Zixin departed, the wind came exactly as he had foretold.

sentences.zh: 是夜，琅邪王五使切召永洛，且云：「敕喚。」

translations.literal: That night the Prince of Langye urgently summoned Yongluo five times, saying, 'It is an imperial summons.
translations.idiomatic: That night the Prince of Langye summoned Yongluo five times in urgent succession, declaring it an imperial order.

sentences.zh: 永洛欲起，其妻苦留之，稱墜馬腰折，不堪動。

translations.literal: Yongluo wished to rise, but his wife forcibly detained him, claiming he had fallen from a horse and broken his waist and could not move.
translations.idiomatic: Yongluo meant to go, but his wife forcibly kept him back, claiming he had fallen from a horse, broken his waist, and could not stir.

sentences.zh: 詰朝而難作。

translations.literal: At dawn disaster broke out.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn the catastrophe erupted.

sentences.zh: 子信，齊亡卒。

translations.literal: Zixin died when Qi fell.
translations.idiomatic: Zixin died when Qi fell.

sentences.zh: 陸法和，不知何許人也。

translations.literal: Lu Fahe—no one knew whence he came.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Fahe was a man whose origins no one knew.

sentences.zh: 隱於江陵百里洲，衣食居處，一與戒行沙門同。

translations.literal: He hid himself on Bailizhou in Jiangling; his food, clothing, and dwelling were all the same as those of monks under discipline.
translations.idiomatic: He lived in seclusion on Bailizhou near Jiangling. His food, clothing, and dwelling were indistinguishable from those of a monk under strict discipline.

sentences.zh: 耆老自幼見之，容色常定，人莫能測也。

translations.literal: The elders had seen him from childhood; his countenance was always unchanged, and no one could fathom him.
translations.idiomatic: The old people had known him since childhood; his face never changed, and no one could plumb his depths.

sentences.zh: 或謂出自嵩高，遍遊遐邇。

translations.literal: Some said he came from Song Mountain and had traveled far and wide.
translations.idiomatic: Some said he came from Song Mountain and had wandered the breadth of the realm.

sentences.zh: 既入荊州汶陽郡高要縣之紫石山，無故舍所居山，俄有蠻賊文道期之亂，時人以為預見萌兆。

translations.literal: After he entered Zishi Mountain in Gaoyao County, Wenyang Commandery, Jingzhou, he suddenly abandoned the mountain where he dwelt; soon afterward the barbarian bandit Wen Daoqi rebelled, and people took it as a foreseen omen.
translations.idiomatic: After he entered Zishi Mountain in Gaoyao County, Wenyang, Jingzhou, he abruptly left the mountain where he had lived; soon the barbarian rebel Wen Daoqi rose, and people took it as a sign he had foreseen.

sentences.zh: 及侯景始告降于梁，法和謂南郡硃元英曰：「貧道共檀越擊侯景去。」

translations.literal: When Hou Jing first announced his surrender to Liang, Fahe told Zhu Yuanying of Nan Commandery, 'This poor monk together with my patron will drive Hou Jing away.
translations.idiomatic: When Hou Jing first offered his surrender to Liang, Fahe told Zhu Yuanying of Nan Commandery, 'This humble monk, together with my patron, will drive Hou Jing away.

sentences.zh: 元英曰：「侯景為國立效，師雲擊之何也？」

translations.literal: Yuanying said, 'Hou Jing is serving the state with merit—why do you, Master, say you will attack him?'
translations.idiomatic: Yuanying said, 'Hou Jing is serving the state—why do you, Master, speak of attacking him?'

sentences.zh: 法和曰：「正自如此。」

translations.literal: Fahe said, 'It is precisely for this reason.'
translations.idiomatic: Fahe replied, 'Precisely for that reason.'

sentences.zh: 及景度江，法和時在青溪山，元英往問曰：「景今圍城，其事云何？」

translations.literal: When Jing crossed the river, Fahe was then at Qingxi Mountain. Yuanying went to ask, 'Jing now besieges the city—how will the affair turn out?'
translations.idiomatic: When Jing crossed the Yangzi, Fahe was on Qingxi Mountain. Yuanying came to ask, 'Jing now besieges the capital—what will become of this?'

sentences.zh: 法和曰：「凡人取果，宜待熟時。」

translations.literal: Fahe said, 'When ordinary men take fruit, they should wait until it is ripe.'
translations.idiomatic: Fahe said, 'When men gather fruit, they wait until it is ripe.'

sentences.zh: 固問之，曰：「亦克，亦不克。」

translations.literal: Pressed further, he said, 'It may succeed, and it may not succeed.'
translations.idiomatic: Pressed further, he said, 'He may succeed—and he may not.'

sentences.zh: 景遣將任約擊梁湘東王於江陵，法和乃詣湘東乞征約。

translations.literal: Jing sent his general Ren Yue to attack the Prince of Xiangdong at Jiangling, and Fahe thereupon went to the Prince of Xiangdong begging to campaign against Yue.
translations.idiomatic: Jing sent his general Ren Yue against the Prince of Xiangdong at Jiangling, and Fahe went to the prince begging leave to campaign against Yue.

sentences.zh: 召諸蠻弟子八百人在江津，二日便發。

translations.literal: He assembled eight hundred barbarian disciples at the river crossing and set out in two days.
translations.idiomatic: He gathered eight hundred barbarian disciples at the river crossing and marched within two days.

sentences.zh: 湘東遣胡僧祐領千餘人與同行。

translations.literal: The Prince of Xiangdong sent Hu Sengyou leading more than a thousand men to go with him.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Xiangdong sent Hu Sengyou with more than a thousand men to accompany him.

sentences.zh: 法和登艦，大笑曰：「無量兵馬。」

translations.literal: Fahe boarded the ship and laughed loudly, saying, 'Boundless troops and horses.
translations.idiomatic: Fahe boarded his vessel and laughed aloud, 'Boundless are the troops and horses.

sentences.zh: 江陵多神祠，人俗恆所祈禱。

translations.literal: Jiangling had many spirit shrines that people constantly prayed at.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangling was full of spirit shrines to which people constantly prayed.

sentences.zh: 自法和軍出，無復一驗，人以為神皆從行故也。

translations.literal: From the time Fahe's army marched out, not one prayer was answered; people thought the spirits had all gone with the army.
translations.idiomatic: After Fahe's army marched out, not one prayer was answered; people believed the gods had all gone with his host.

sentences.zh: 至赤沙湖，與約相對。

translations.literal: Reaching Chisha Lake, they faced Yue's forces.
translations.idiomatic: At Chisha Lake they came face to face with Yue's army.

sentences.zh: 法和乘輕船，不介胄，沿流而下，去約軍一里乃還。

translations.literal: Fahe took a light boat, wore no armor, floated downstream, and when he was one li from Yue's army he turned back.
translations.idiomatic: Fahe took a light boat, wore no armor, drifted downstream to within a li of Yue's camp, and then returned.

sentences.zh: 謂將士曰：「聊觀彼龍睡不動，吾軍之龍，甚自踴躍，即攻之。

translations.literal: He told the officers and men, 'I have just looked—their dragon sleeps motionless, while our army's dragon leaps eagerly. Attack at once.
translations.idiomatic: He told his officers, 'I have just looked—their dragon lies asleep, while ours leaps with eagerness. Attack now.

sentences.zh: 若得彼明日，當不損客主一人而破賊，然有惡處。」

translations.literal: If we take them tomorrow, not one man of host or guest will be harmed and the bandits will be broken—yet there will be an ill place.
translations.idiomatic: If we strike tomorrow, not one man on either side will fall and the rebels will be shattered—yet there will be an ill spot.

sentences.zh: 遂縱火船，而逆風不便，法和執白羽扇麾風，風即返。

translations.literal: They then sent fire ships, but the contrary wind was unfavorable. Fahe took a white feather fan and waved at the wind, and the wind at once reversed.
translations.idiomatic: They launched fire ships, but the wind blew against them. Fahe waved a white feather fan at the wind, and it turned about at once.

sentences.zh: 約眾皆見梁兵步于水上，於是大潰，皆投水。

translations.literal: Yue's multitude all saw Liang soldiers walking on the water; thereupon they broke in great rout and all cast themselves into the river.
translations.idiomatic: Yue's men saw Liang soldiers walking upon the water; the army collapsed in panic and men threw themselves into the river.

sentences.zh: 約逃竄不知所之，法和曰：「明日午時當得。」

translations.literal: Yue fled and hid, and no one knew where he was. Fahe said, 'At noon tomorrow he will be taken.
translations.idiomatic: Yue fled into hiding, and no one knew where. Fahe said, 'At noon tomorrow he will be captured.

sentences.zh: 及期而未得，人問之，法和曰：「吾前于此洲水乾時建一刹，語檀越等：此雖為刹，實是賊標。

translations.literal: When the hour came and he was not yet taken, people questioned him. Fahe said, 'Formerly, when this shoal was dry, I built a stupa here and told my patrons: though this is called a stupa, in truth it is a marker for the bandit.
translations.idiomatic: When noon passed without capture, they questioned him. Fahe said, 'Long ago, when this shoal was dry, I built a stupa here and told my patrons: though this is a stupa, it is in truth a marker for the rebel.

sentences.zh: 今何不向標下求賊也？」

translations.literal: Why not now seek the bandit beneath the marker?'
translations.idiomatic: Why not seek the rebel beneath the marker now?'

sentences.zh: 如其言，果于水中見約抱刹，仰頭裁出鼻，遂禽之。

translations.literal: As he said, they indeed saw Yue in the water embracing the stupa, his head barely above water with only his nose showing, and seized him.
translations.idiomatic: They did as he said and found Yue in the water clinging to the stupa, his head barely breaking the surface with only his nose exposed. They captured him.

sentences.zh: 約言：「求就師目前死。」

translations.literal: Yue said, 'I beg to die before the Master's eyes.
translations.idiomatic: Yue said, 'Let me die before your eyes, Master.

sentences.zh: 法和曰：「檀越有相，必不兵死。

translations.literal: Fahe said, 'My patron has the physiognomy of one who will surely not die by the sword.
translations.idiomatic: Fahe said, 'My patron bears the marks of a man who will not die by the sword.

sentences.zh: 且于王有緣，決無他慮。

translations.literal: Moreover he has karmic ties with the prince; assuredly there is no other concern.
translations.idiomatic: He also shares karmic ties with the prince; have no other fear.

sentences.zh: 王于後當得檀越力耳。」

translations.literal: Later the prince will receive my patron's strength.'
translations.idiomatic: Later the prince will owe his strength to my patron.'

sentences.zh: 湘東果釋用為郡守。

translations.literal: The Prince of Xiangdong indeed released him and employed him as commandery administrator.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Xiangdong indeed released him and appointed him commandery administrator.

sentences.zh: 及魏圍江陵，約以兵赴救，力戰焉。

translations.literal: When Wei besieged Jiangling, Yue came with troops to the rescue and fought fiercely.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei besieged Jiangling, Yue marched to the rescue and fought fiercely.

sentences.zh: 法和既平約，往進見王僧辯于巴陵，謂曰：「貧道已卻侯景一臂，其更何能為？

translations.literal: After Fahe had pacified Yue, he went forward to see Wang Sengbian at Baling and said, 'This poor monk has already cut off one arm of Hou Jing—what more can he do?
translations.idiomatic: After defeating Yue, Fahe went to see Wang Sengbian at Baling and said, 'This humble monk has already severed one arm of Hou Jing—what more can he do?

sentences.zh: 檀越宜即逐取。」

translations.literal: My patron should at once pursue and take him.
translations.idiomatic: My patron should pursue and seize him at once.

sentences.zh: 乃請還。

translations.literal: He then asked to return.
translations.idiomatic: He then asked leave to return.

sentences.zh: 謂湘東王曰：「侯景自然平矣，無足可慮。

translations.literal: He told the Prince of Xiangdong, 'Hou Jing will naturally be pacified; there is nothing worth worrying about.
translations.idiomatic: He told the Prince of Xiangdong, 'Hou Jing will fall of his own accord; there is nothing to fear.

sentences.zh: 蜀賊將至，法和請守巫峽待之。」

translations.literal: Shu bandits are about to arrive; Fahe asked to hold Wuxia Gorge and await them.
translations.idiomatic: When Shu rebels were expected, Fahe asked to hold Wuxia Gorge and await them.

sentences.zh: 乃縱諸軍而往，親運石以填江。

translations.literal: He then released the armies and went himself, personally hauling stones to fill the river.
translations.idiomatic: He then marched with his forces and personally hauled stones to dam the river.

sentences.zh: 三日，水遂不流，橫之以鐵鎖。

translations.literal: In three days the water ceased to flow, and iron chains were stretched across.
translations.idiomatic: Within three days the current stopped, and iron chains were stretched across the gorge.

sentences.zh: 武陵王紀果遣蜀兵來度，峽口勢蹙，進退不可，王琳與法和經略，一戰而殄之。

translations.literal: Prince Ji of Wuling indeed sent Shu troops to cross; the gorge mouth was cramped and advance and retreat were impossible. Wang Lin and Fahe planned together and annihilated them in one battle.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Ji of Wuling did send Shu troops to cross, but the gorge mouth was tight and they could neither advance nor retreat. Wang Lin and Fahe coordinated a plan and destroyed them in a single battle.

sentences.zh: 軍次白帝，謂人曰：「諸葛孔明可謂為名將，吾自見之。

translations.literal: When the army halted at Baidi, he told people, 'Zhuge Kongming may be called a famous general—I have seen him myself.
translations.idiomatic: When the army halted at Baidi, he told people, 'Zhuge Kongming deserves the name of a great general—I have seen him with my own eyes.

sentences.zh: 此城旁有其埋弩箭鏃一斛許。」

translations.literal: Beside this city there is buried about a hu of crossbow bolts and arrowheads.
translations.idiomatic: Beside this city lies a buried hoard of crossbow bolts and arrowheads, about a hu in volume.

sentences.zh: 因插表令掘之，如其言。

translations.literal: He thereupon planted a marker and ordered them dug up; it was as he had said.
translations.idiomatic: He marked the spot and ordered an excavation; it was exactly as he had said.

sentences.zh: 又嘗至襄陽城北大樹下，畫地方二尺，令弟子掘之。

translations.literal: He also once came to a great tree north of Xiangyang city, drew a square two chi on the ground, and ordered his disciples to dig.
translations.idiomatic: He also once came to a great tree north of Xiangyang, marked out a square two chi across, and told his disciples to dig.

sentences.zh: 得一龜，長尺半，以杖叩之曰：「汝欲出，不能得，已數百歲。

translations.literal: They obtained a turtle a chi and a half long. He tapped it with a staff and said, 'You wish to emerge but cannot; already several hundred years have passed.
translations.idiomatic: They unearthed a turtle a foot and a half long. He struck it with his staff and said, 'You wish to come forth but cannot; already several hundred years have passed.

sentences.zh: 不逢我者，豈見天日乎？」

translations.literal: Had you not met me, how would you have seen the light of day?
translations.idiomatic: Had you not met me, would you ever have seen daylight again?

sentences.zh: 為授《三歸》，龜乃入草。

translations.literal: He administered the Three Refuges to it, and the turtle then entered the grass.
translations.idiomatic: He gave it the Three Refuges, and the turtle crawled back into the grass.

sentences.zh: 初，八疊山多惡疾人，法和為采藥療之，不過三服，皆差，即求為弟子。

translations.literal: At the beginning, on Badie Mountain there were many people afflicted with malignant illness. Fahe gathered herbs to treat them; within three doses all were cured, and they at once asked to become disciples.
translations.idiomatic: In the beginning Badie Mountain was rife with grave sickness. Fahe gathered herbs to treat the afflicted; three doses cured them, and they immediately asked to become his disciples.

sentences.zh: 山中多毒蟲猛獸，法和授其禁戒，不復噬蜇。

translations.literal: The mountain had many venomous insects and fierce beasts; Fahe imparted prohibitions to his followers, and they were no longer bitten or stung.
translations.idiomatic: The mountain swarmed with venomous creatures and fierce beasts; Fahe taught his followers protective prohibitions, and they were no longer harmed.

sentences.zh: 所泊江湖，必於峰側結表，雲此處放生。

translations.literal: Wherever he moored on rivers and lakes, he always erected a marker on a peak, saying this place was for releasing life.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever he anchored on rivers and lakes, he set up a marker on a nearby peak declaring the waters a sanctuary for releasing captive life.

sentences.zh: 漁者皆無所得。

translations.literal: Fishermen all obtained nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Fishermen caught nothing at all.

sentences.zh: 才或少獲，輒有大風雷，船人懼而放之，風雨乃定。

translations.literal: If by chance they caught a little, great wind and thunder at once arose; the boatmen in fear released the catch, and then wind and rain subsided.
translations.idiomatic: If anyone caught even a few fish, violent wind and thunder erupted at once; terrified, the fishermen released their catch, and only then did the storm abate.

sentences.zh: 晚雖將兵，猶禁諸軍漁捕，有竊違者，中夜猛獸必來欲噬之，或亡其船纜。

translations.literal: Though he later commanded troops, he still forbade the armies to fish and hunt. If anyone secretly violated the rule, at midnight fierce beasts would come seeking to devour him, or his boat cable would be lost.
translations.idiomatic: Even after he took command of armies, he forbade his troops to fish or hunt. Those who secretly disobeyed were visited at midnight by savage beasts seeking to devour them, or found their boat cables vanished.

sentences.zh: 有小弟子戲截蛇頭，來詣法和。

translations.literal: A young disciple playfully cut off a snake's head and came to Fahe.
translations.idiomatic: A young disciple playfully severed a snake's head and brought it to Fahe.

sentences.zh: 法和曰：「汝何意殺！」

translations.literal: Fahe said, 'What do you mean by killing!
translations.idiomatic: Fahe said, 'What have you done, killing like this!

sentences.zh: 因指以示之，弟子乃見蛇頭齚褲襠而不落。

translations.literal: He then pointed to show him, and the disciple then saw the snake's head biting his trouser flap and not falling away.
translations.idiomatic: He pointed, and the disciple saw the severed head clamped to his trouser flap, refusing to fall.

sentences.zh: 法和使懺悔，為蛇作功德。

translations.literal: Fahe made him repent and perform merit on the snake's behalf.
translations.idiomatic: Fahe made him repent and perform rites of merit for the snake.

sentences.zh: 又有人以牛試刀，一下而頭斷，來詣法和。

translations.literal: There was also a man who tested a blade on an ox; one stroke severed the head, and he came to Fahe.
translations.idiomatic: Another man tested a blade on an ox; one stroke took off its head, and he came to Fahe.

sentences.zh: 法和曰：「有一斷頭牛，就卿征命殊急，若不為作功德，一月內報至。」

translations.literal: Fahe said, 'There is a headless ox urgently seeking your life from you; if you do not perform merit for it, retribution will come within a month.
translations.idiomatic: Fahe said, 'A headless ox is urgently demanding your life; unless you perform merit on its behalf, retribution will arrive within a month.

sentences.zh: 其人弗信，少日果死。

translations.literal: The man did not believe; within a few days he indeed died.
translations.idiomatic: The man refused to believe him; within days he was dead.

sentences.zh: 法和又為人置宅圖墓以避禍求福。

translations.literal: Fahe also chose house sites and tomb plots for people to avoid calamity and seek blessing.
translations.idiomatic: Fahe also selected house sites and tomb plots for people seeking to avert disaster and gain fortune.

sentences.zh: 嘗謂人曰：「勿系馬於碓。」

translations.literal: He once told a man, 'Do not tie your horse to a mortar.
translations.idiomatic: He once warned a man, 'Never tie your horse to a mortar.

sentences.zh: 其人行過鄉曲，門側有碓，因系馬於其柱。

translations.literal: The man passed through a village lane; beside a gate was a mortar, and he tied his horse to its post.
translations.idiomatic: The man passed through a village lane and, finding a mortar beside a gate, tied his horse to its post.

sentences.zh: 入門中，憶法和戒，走出將解之，馬已斃矣。

translations.literal: Entering the gate, he remembered Fahe's warning, ran out intending to untie it, but the horse was already dead.
translations.idiomatic: Inside the gate he remembered Fahe's warning, rushed out to untie the horse, and found it already dead.

sentences.zh: 梁元帝以法和為都督、郢州刺史，封江乘縣公。

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan of Liang made Fahe Area Commander and Inspector of Yingzhou, enfeoffing him as Duke of Jiangcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan of Liang appointed Fahe Area Commander and Inspector of Yingzhou, enfeoffing him as Duke of Jiangcheng.

sentences.zh: 法和不稱臣，其啟文硃印名上，自稱居士，後稱司徒。

translations.literal: Fahe did not style himself subject. On his memorials he placed his vermilion seal and name above, calling himself Layman; later he called himself Excellency of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Fahe refused the title of subject. On his memorials he placed his vermilion seal and name at the top, styling himself Layman; later he styled himself Excellency of Works.

sentences.zh: 梁元帝謂其僕射王褒曰：「我未嘗有意用陸為三公，而自稱，何也？」

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan told his Vice Director Wang Bao, 'I never intended to use Lu as one of the Three Excellencies, yet he styles himself thus—why?
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan told his Vice Director Wang Bao, 'I never meant to make Lu one of the Three Excellencies, yet he styles himself as one—why?

sentences.zh: 褒曰：「彼既以道術自命，容是先知。」

translations.literal: Bao said, 'Since he claims authority through Daoist arts, perhaps he foresaw it in advance.'
translations.idiomatic: Bao replied, 'He sets himself up by occult arts; perhaps he foresaw it.'

sentences.zh: 梁元帝以法和功業稍重，遂就加司徒，都督、刺史如故。

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan, because Fahe's achievements were growing weighty, thereupon added the title Excellency of Works while his area command and inspectorship remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: As Fahe's achievements grew weightier, Emperor Yuan conferred upon him the title Excellency of Works while leaving his command and inspectorship unchanged.

sentences.zh: 部曲數千人，通呼為弟子。

translations.literal: His personal troops numbered several thousand; all were called disciples.
translations.idiomatic: His personal troops numbered several thousand, all addressed as disciples.

sentences.zh: 唯以道術為化，不以法獄加人。

translations.literal: He governed only through Daoist arts and did not impose legal punishment on men.
translations.idiomatic: He ruled solely through occult teaching and never punished men by law.

sentences.zh: 又列肆之所，不立市丞，牧佐之法，無人領受。

translations.literal: In market rows he established no market clerks; the methods of pastoral oversight had no one to receive them.
translations.idiomatic: In the marketplaces he appointed no market clerks; no official received the customary fees of trade supervision.

sentences.zh: 但以空檻龠在道間，上開一孔以受錢。

translations.literal: Only empty cages with pipes stood along the roads, with an opening above to receive money.
translations.idiomatic: Only empty cages with slots stood along the roads, open at the top to receive coins.

sentences.zh: 賈客店人，隨貨多少，計其估限，自委檻中。

translations.literal: Merchants and innkeepers, according to the quantity of goods, estimated the appraised limit and deposited it themselves in the cage.
translations.idiomatic: Merchants and innkeepers, judging the value of their goods, calculated the assessed fee and dropped it into the cage themselves.

sentences.zh: 所掌之司，夕方開取，條其孔目，輸之於庫。

translations.literal: The official in charge opened it only in the evening, checked the tally against the opening, and delivered it to the treasury.
translations.idiomatic: The responsible official opened the cages only at evening, checked the tally, and delivered the proceeds to the treasury.

sentences.zh: 又法和平常言若不出口，時有所論，則雄辯無敵，然猶帶蠻音。

translations.literal: Moreover, Fahe in ordinary speech, if he did not speak out, when he did discourse was matchlessly eloquent—yet he still bore a barbarian accent.
translations.idiomatic: Fahe seldom spoke in daily life, but when he did discourse his eloquence was unmatched—though he still spoke with a barbarian accent.

sentences.zh: 善為攻戰具。

translations.literal: He was skilled at making siege engines.
translations.idiomatic: He was skilled at constructing siege engines.

sentences.zh: 在江夏，大聚兵艦，欲襲襄陽而入武關，梁元帝使止之。

translations.literal: At Jiangxia he greatly assembled warships, intending to strike Xiangyang and enter Wuguan; Emperor Yuan sent orders to stop him.
translations.idiomatic: At Jiangxia he massed warships, intending to strike Xiangyang and enter Wuguan; Emperor Yuan ordered him to halt.

sentences.zh: 法和曰：「法和是求佛之人，尚不希釋梵天王坐處，豈規王位？

translations.literal: Fahe said, 'Fahe is one who seeks the Buddha; he does not even covet the seat of the Brahma King of Empty Space—how would he scheme for royal rank?
translations.idiomatic: Fahe said, 'I am a seeker of the Buddha; I do not even desire the throne of the Brahma King—why would I plot for a crown?

sentences.zh: 但于空王佛所與主上有香火因緣，見主上應有報至，故救援耳。

translations.literal: Only at the shrine of the Buddha of Empty Space do I share incense ties with my lord; seeing that my lord should receive retribution, I came to his aid.
translations.idiomatic: Only at the shrine of the Buddha of Empty Space do I share karmic ties with my lord; seeing that retribution was due him, I came to his rescue.

sentences.zh: 今既被疑，是業定不可改也。」

translations.literal: Now that I am already suspected, this karma is fixed and cannot be changed.
translations.idiomatic: Now that I am suspected, this karma is fixed and cannot be altered.

sentences.zh: 於是設供食，具大饣追薄餅。

translations.literal: He thereupon set out offerings of food, with great thin cakes.
translations.idiomatic: He thereupon prepared a feast of offerings, including great thin cakes.

sentences.zh: 及魏舉兵，法和自郢入漢口，將赴江陵，梁元帝使人逆之曰：「此自能破賊，師但鎮郢州，不須動也。」

translations.literal: When Wei raised troops, Fahe himself went from Ying into Hankou, intending to hurry to Jiangling. Emperor Yuan sent a messenger to meet him and say, 'We ourselves can break the bandits; Master, only hold Yingzhou—there is no need to move.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei marched, Fahe left Ying for Hankou, intending to rush to Jiangling. Emperor Yuan sent a messenger to meet him: 'We can break the enemy ourselves; Master, hold Yingzhou and do not stir.

sentences.zh: 法和乃還州，堊其城門，著粗白布衫，褲布邪巾，大繩束腰，坐葦席，終日乃脫之。

translations.literal: Fahe then returned to his province, whitewashed the city gates, wore a coarse white cloth shirt, cloth trousers and a slanting headcloth, bound his waist with a great rope, and sat on a reed mat; only at day's end did he remove them.
translations.idiomatic: Fahe returned to his province, whitewashed the city gates, dressed in coarse white cloth shirt, trousers, and a slanting headcloth, bound his waist with a thick rope, and sat on a reed mat until day's end.

sentences.zh: 及聞梁元敗滅，復取前凶服著之，哭泣受吊。

translations.literal: When he heard that Emperor Yuan had been defeated and destroyed, he again put on his former mourning garments, wept, and received condolences.
translations.idiomatic: When he learned that Emperor Yuan had fallen, he again donned his mourning garb, wept, and received those who came to condole with him.

sentences.zh: 梁人入魏，果見饣追餅焉。

translations.literal: When men of Liang entered Wei, they indeed saw the thin cakes.
translations.idiomatic: When men of Liang entered Wei, they indeed found the thin cakes he had prepared.

sentences.zh: 法和始於百里洲造壽王寺。

translations.literal: Fahe first built Shouwang Temple on Bailizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Fahe first built Shouwang Temple on Bailizhou.

sentences.zh: 既架佛殿，更截梁柱，曰：「後四十許年，佛法當遭雷雹，此寺幽僻，可以免難。」

translations.literal: After the Buddha hall was raised, he further cut the beams and pillars and said, 'In about forty years Buddhism will suffer thunder and hail; this temple is secluded and can escape the calamity.
translations.idiomatic: After raising the Buddha hall, he cut away additional beams and pillars, saying, 'In some forty years Buddhism will suffer thunder and hail; this secluded temple can escape the disaster.

sentences.zh: 及魏平荊州，宮室焚燼，總管欲發取壽王佛殿，嫌其材短，乃停。

translations.literal: When Wei pacified Jingzhou, the palace halls were burned to ash; the commander wished to take the Shouwang Buddha hall but, finding the timbers too short, stopped.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei pacified Jingzhou, the palace halls were burned to ash. The commander meant to dismantle the Shouwang Buddha hall, but finding the timbers too short, desisted.

sentences.zh: 後周氏滅佛法，此寺隔在陳境，故不及難。

translations.literal: Later Zhou extinguished the Buddhist Law; this temple lay beyond in Chen territory and therefore escaped the disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Later Zhou suppressed Buddhism; the temple lay in Chen territory and so escaped destruction.

sentences.zh: 天保六年春，清河王岳進軍臨江，法和舉州入齊。

translations.literal: In the spring of the sixth year of Tianbao, Prince Qinghe Yue marched his army to the river; Fahe surrendered the entire province to Qi.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of Tianbao year six, Prince Qinghe Yue marched to the river; Fahe surrendered the whole province to Qi.

sentences.zh: 文宣以法和為大都督、十州諸軍事、太尉公、西南大都督、五州諸軍事、荊州刺史，安湘郡公宋蒞為郢州刺史，官爵如故。

translations.literal: Emperor Wenxuan made Fahe Grand Commander of Ten Provinces' Military Affairs, Grand Duke and Grand Captain, Southwestern Grand Commander of Five Provinces' Military Affairs and Inspector of Jingzhou; Song Li of Anxiang Commandery was made Inspector of Yingzhou, ranks and titles as before.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wenxuan made Fahe Grand Commander over ten provinces, Grand Duke and Grand Captain, Southwestern Grand Commander over five provinces and Inspector of Jingzhou; Song Li of Anxiang Commandery became Inspector of Yingzhou, with ranks unchanged.

sentences.zh: 蒞弟簉為散騎常侍、儀同三司、湘州刺史、義興縣公。

translations.literal: Li's younger brother Cui was made Regular Attendant, Companions of the Same Rank as the Three Excellencies, Inspector of Xiangzhou, and Duke of Yixing County.
translations.idiomatic: Li's younger brother Cui was made Regular Attendant, Companion of the Same Rank as the Three Excellencies, Inspector of Xiangzhou, and Duke of Yixing County.

sentences.zh: 梁將侯瑱來逼江夏，齊軍棄城而退，法和與宋蒞兄弟入朝。

translations.literal: The Liang general Hou Tian came pressing Jiangxia; Qi forces abandoned the city and withdrew, and Fahe entered court with the Song Li brothers.
translations.idiomatic: The Liang general Hou Tian pressed Jiangxia; Qi forces abandoned the city and withdrew, and Fahe entered court with the Song Li brothers.

sentences.zh: 文宣聞其有奇術，虛心相見之。

translations.literal: Emperor Wenxuan, hearing he had wondrous arts, received him with sincere humility.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing of his occult powers, Emperor Wenxuan received him with sincere humility.

sentences.zh: 備三公鹵簿，于城南十二里供帳以待之。

translations.literal: The full regalia of the Three Excellencies was prepared; twelve li south of the city a pavilion was set up to await him.
translations.idiomatic: The full regalia of the Three Excellencies was prepared, and a pavilion twelve li south of the city was erected to receive him.

sentences.zh: 法和遙見鄴城，下馬禹步。

translations.literal: Fahe saw Ye city from afar and dismounted to walk with measured steps.
translations.idiomatic: Fahe saw Ye from afar and dismounted to walk with ritual steps.

sentences.zh: 辛術謂曰：「公既萬里歸誠，主上虛心相待，何作此術？」

translations.literal: Xin Shu said to him, 'Sir, having returned in faith from ten thousand li, the sovereign receives you with open heart—why perform this art?
translations.idiomatic: Xin Shu said to him, 'You have come in faith from afar, and the sovereign welcomes you with an open heart—why perform this rite?

sentences.zh: 法和手持香爐，步從路車至於館。

translations.literal: Fahe held an incense burner and walked behind the road carriage to the lodge.
translations.idiomatic: Fahe carried an incense burner and walked behind the state carriage to his lodging.

sentences.zh: 明日引見，給通晄憲油絡網車，仗身百人。

translations.literal: The next day he was granted audience and given an imperial carriage with lacquered canopy and net, and a hundred armed attendants.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he was granted audience and given an imperial carriage with lacquered canopy and net, attended by a hundred armed guards.

sentences.zh: 詣闕通名，不稱官爵，不稱臣，但雲荊山居士。

translations.literal: Arriving at the palace gate he announced his name, neither styling his office and rank nor calling himself subject, but only saying Layman of Jing Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: At the palace gate he announced himself neither by office nor as subject, but only as Layman of Jing Mountain.

sentences.zh: 文宣宴法和及其徒屬於昭陽殿，賜法和錢百萬、物萬段、甲第一區、田一百頃、奴婢二百人，生資什物稱是；

translations.literal: Emperor Wenxuan feasted Fahe and his followers in Zhaoyang Hall, granting Fahe a million coins, ten thousand lengths of goods, one first-rank mansion, a hundred qing of fields, two hundred slaves, and living supplies in proportion;
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wenxuan feasted Fahe and his followers in Zhaoyang Hall, granting Fahe a million coins, ten thousand lengths of goods, a first-rank mansion, a hundred qing of fields, two hundred slaves, and commensurate provisions;

sentences.zh: 宋蒞千段；

translations.literal: Song Li a thousand lengths;
translations.idiomatic: Song Li a thousand lengths;

sentences.zh: 其餘儀同、刺史以下各有差。

translations.literal: the rest, Companions of the Same Rank, inspectors, and those below each received gifts in differing measure.
translations.idiomatic: the remaining Companions of the Same Rank, inspectors, and subordinates each received gifts according to rank.

sentences.zh: 法和所得奴婢，盡免之，曰：「各隨緣去。」

translations.literal: The slaves Fahe received he entirely freed, saying, 'Each may go as karma directs.
translations.idiomatic: Fahe freed every slave given him, saying, 'Go wherever your karma leads.

sentences.zh: 錢帛散施，一日便盡。

translations.literal: Coins and silks he distributed in charity; in one day they were all spent.
translations.idiomatic: He distributed coins and silks in charity; within a single day all was gone.

sentences.zh: 以官所賜宅營佛寺，自居一房，與凡人無異。

translations.literal: With the mansion granted by the court he built a Buddhist temple and dwelt in one room, no different from an ordinary man.
translations.idiomatic: He built a Buddhist temple from the mansion the court had granted and lived in a single room, indistinguishable from any common man.

sentences.zh: 三年間再為太尉，世猶謂之居士。

translations.literal: Within three years he was again made Grand Captain; the world still called him Layman.
translations.idiomatic: Within three years he was again made Grand Captain; people still called him Layman.

sentences.zh: 無疾，而告弟子死期。

translations.literal: Without illness he told his disciples the day of his death.
translations.idiomatic: Though free of illness, he told his disciples the day he would die.

sentences.zh: 至時，燒香禮佛，坐繩床而終。

translations.literal: When the time came, he burned incense, worshipped the Buddha, and died seated on a rope bed.
translations.idiomatic: When the day came, he burned incense, bowed before the Buddha, and died seated on a rope bed.

sentences.zh: 浴訖將殮，屍小縮止三尺許。

translations.literal: After bathing, when they were about to enclose the corpse in the coffin, the body shrank to only three chi.
translations.idiomatic: After the bathing rites, as they prepared to place him in the coffin, the corpse shrank to only three chi.

sentences.zh: 文宣令開棺而視之，空棺而已。

translations.literal: Emperor Wenxuan ordered the coffin opened and looked inside; it was an empty coffin.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wenxuan ordered the coffin opened—and found it empty.

sentences.zh: 法和書其所居屋壁而塗之，及剝落，有文曰：「十年天子為尚可，百日天子急如火，周年天子遞代坐。」

translations.literal: Fahe had written on the wall of the room where he dwelt and then plastered it over; when the plaster fell away, there was text saying, 'Ten years as Son of Heaven is still tolerable; a hundred days as Son of Heaven is urgent as fire; a full year as Son of Heaven, one succeeds another in turn.
translations.idiomatic: Fahe had written on the wall of his room and plastered it over; when the plaster fell away, the text read, 'Ten years as emperor is bearable; a hundred days as emperor burns like fire; a year as emperor, one succeeds another in turn.

sentences.zh: 又曰：「一母生三天，兩天共五年。」

translations.literal: It also said, 'One mother bears three Sons of Heaven; two Sons of Heaven together five years.'
translations.idiomatic: It also read, 'One mother bears three emperors; two emperors together five years.'

sentences.zh: 說者以為婁太后生三天子，自孝昭即位至武成傳位後主，共五年焉。

translations.literal: Commentators took it to mean that Empress Dowager Lou bore three Sons of Heaven; from Xiaozhao's accession until Wucheng transferred the throne to the later sovereign, together five years.
translations.idiomatic: Commentators took this to mean that Empress Dowager Lou bore three emperors; from Xiaozhao's accession until Wucheng abdicated in favor of the later sovereign, together five years.

sentences.zh: 法和在荊郢，有少姬，年可二十餘，自稱越姥，身披法服，不肯嫁娶。

translations.literal: Fahe, while in Jing and Ying, had a young concubine about twenty years old who called herself Old Woman Yue, wore religious robes, and would not marry.
translations.idiomatic: While in Jing and Ying, Fahe kept a young concubine of about twenty who called herself Old Woman Yue, wore religious robes, and refused marriage.

sentences.zh: 恆隨法和東西，或與其私通，十有餘年。

translations.literal: She always followed Fahe east and west, and sometimes had private relations with him—for more than ten years.
translations.idiomatic: She followed Fahe wherever he went and sometimes slept with him—for more than ten years.

sentences.zh: 今者賜棄，別更他淫。

translations.literal: Now she was cast off and took other lovers.
translations.idiomatic: Now she was cast off and took other lovers.

sentences.zh: 有司考驗，並實。

translations.literal: The officials examined the matter; all was true.
translations.idiomatic: Officials investigated; every charge proved true.

sentences.zh: 越姥因爾改適，生子數人。

translations.literal: Old Woman Yue thereupon remarried and bore several sons.
translations.idiomatic: Old Woman Yue then remarried and bore several sons.

sentences.zh: 蔣升，字鳳起，楚國平河人也。

translations.literal: Jiang Sheng, styled Fengqi, was a man of Pinghe in Chu.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Sheng, styled Fengqi, came from Pinghe in Chu.

sentences.zh: 少好天文玄象之學，周文雅信待之。

translations.literal: In youth he loved the study of astronomy and occult signs; Zhou Wenya trusted and treated him well.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he loved astronomy and occult signs; Zhou Wenya trusted and favored him.

sentences.zh: 大統三年，東魏竇泰頓軍潼關，周文出師馬牧澤。

translations.literal: In the third year of Datong, Eastern Wei's Dou Tai halted his army at Tong Pass; Zhou Wen marched his army out to Maze Pasture.
translations.idiomatic: In Datong year three, Eastern Wei's Dou Tai halted at Tong Pass; Zhou Wen marched out to Maze Pasture.

sentences.zh: 時西南有黃紫氣抱日，從未至酉。

translations.literal: At that time in the southwest yellow and purple vapors embraced the sun, from wei hour to you hour.
translations.idiomatic: At that hour yellow and purple vapors in the southwest embraced the sun, from wei until you.

sentences.zh: 周文謂升曰：「此何祥也？」

translations.literal: Zhou Wen asked Sheng, 'What omen is this?
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Wen asked Sheng, 'What omen is this?

sentences.zh: 升曰：「西南未地，主土。

translations.literal: Sheng said, 'The southwest is the wei direction, which governs earth.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng said, 'The southwest is the wei direction, which governs earth.

sentences.zh: 土王四季，秦分。

translations.literal: Earth is king in the four seasons; it is the Qin region.
translations.idiomatic: Earth reigns through the four seasons; this is the Qin region.

sentences.zh: 今大軍既出，喜氣下臨，必有大慶。」

translations.literal: Now that the great army has marched out, joyous vapors descend—there must be a great victory.'
translations.idiomatic: Now that the great army has marched forth, auspicious vapors descend—there will be a great victory.'

sentences.zh: 於是與泰戰，禽之。

translations.literal: Thereupon they fought Tai and captured him.
translations.idiomatic: They fought Tai and captured him.

sentences.zh: 自後遂降河東，克弘農，破沙苑，由此愈被親禮。

translations.literal: Afterwards they successively reduced Hedong, took Hongnong, and broke Sha Garden; from this he was ever more treated with intimate honor.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter they successively reduced Hedong, took Hongnong, and broke Sha Garden; from this Sheng was ever more honored.

sentences.zh: 九年，高仲密以北豫州來附，周文欲遣兵援之。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, Gao Zhongmi came over with Northern Yuzhou to submit; Zhou Wen wished to send troops to aid him.
translations.idiomatic: In year nine, Gao Zhongmi came over with Northern Yuzhou to submit; Zhou Wen wished to send troops to his aid.

sentences.zh: 升曰：「春王在東，熒惑又在井鬼分，行軍非便。」

translations.literal: Sheng said, 'The spring king is in the east, and Mars is also in the well-ghost region—marching is not favorable.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng said, 'The spring king is in the east, and Mars stands in the well-ghost quarter—marching is ill-advised.

sentences.zh: 周文不從。

translations.literal: Zhou Wen did not follow this.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Wen did not heed him.

sentences.zh: 軍至芒山，不利而還。

translations.literal: The army reached Mangshan and, meeting misfortune, returned.
translations.idiomatic: The army reached Mangshan, met disaster, and retreated.

sentences.zh: 太師賀拔勝怒曰：「蔣升罪合萬死！」

translations.literal: Grand Preceptor Heba Sheng angrily said, 'Jiang Sheng's crime deserves ten thousand deaths!
translations.idiomatic: Grand Preceptor Heba Sheng raged, 'Jiang Sheng deserves death ten thousand times over!

sentences.zh: 周文曰：「蔣升固諫曰：'師出不利。

translations.literal: Zhou Wen said, 'Jiang Sheng firmly remonstrated, saying, "The army's march will be unfavorable.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Wen said, 'Jiang Sheng warned me plainly that the march would go ill.

sentences.zh: '此敗也，孤自取之。」

translations.literal: This defeat—I brought it upon myself.'
translations.idiomatic: This defeat, I brought upon myself.'

sentences.zh: 恭帝元年，以前後功，授車騎大將軍、儀同三司，封高城縣子。

translations.literal: In the first year of Emperor Gong, in recognition of his services over the years, he was appointed General of Chariots and Cavalry, given the third rank of the same precedence as the Three Excellencies, and enfeoffed as Viscount of Gaocheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Emperor Gong, in reward for his past and present service, he was made General of Chariots and Cavalry with third-rank ceremonial parity, and enfeoffed as Viscount of Gaocheng.

sentences.zh: 後除大中大夫，以年老請致事。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed Grand Master of Palace Affairs and, on account of old age, requested retirement.
translations.idiomatic: He was later appointed Grand Master of Palace Affairs and, citing his age, asked to retire from office.

sentences.zh: 詔許之，加定州刺史，卒于家。

translations.literal: An edict granted his request; he was additionally made Governor of Dingzhou and died at home.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved his request, additionally appointing him Governor of Dingzhou; he died at home.

sentences.zh: 強練，不知何許人也，亦不知其名字。

translations.literal: Qiang Lian was a man of unknown origin; his personal name was also unknown.
translations.idiomatic: Qiang Lian was from an unknown place, and his personal name was unknown as well.

sentences.zh: 先是李順興語默不恆，好言未然之事，當時號為李練，世人以強類之，故亦呼為練焉。

translations.literal: Earlier there had been Li Shunxing, whose speech and silence were inconstant and who liked to speak of things not yet come to pass; at the time he was called Li Lian, and because Qiang was regarded as similar, people also called him Lian.
translations.idiomatic: Before him there had been Li Shunxing, erratic in speech and silence, fond of prophesying things not yet come to pass; people called him Li Lian. Because Qiang seemed cut from the same cloth, they called him Lian too.

sentences.zh: 容貌長壯，有異於人，神情敞怳，莫之能測。

translations.literal: His appearance was tall and robust, unlike other men; his spirit and expression were open and remote, and none could fathom him.
translations.idiomatic: Tall and powerfully built, he looked unlike ordinary men; his bearing was distant and unfathomable.

sentences.zh: 意欲有所說，逢人輒言；

translations.literal: When he wished to say something, he would speak to whomever he met;
translations.idiomatic: When he wanted to speak, he would address whoever he encountered;

sentences.zh: 若值其不欲言，縱苦加祈請，不相酬答。

translations.literal: if he did not wish to speak, even when people earnestly entreated him, he would not respond.
translations.idiomatic: but when he did not wish to speak, no amount of pleading could draw a reply from him.

sentences.zh: 初聞其言，略不可解，事過後，往往有驗。

translations.literal: At first his words could scarcely be understood, but after events passed, they often proved true.
translations.idiomatic: At first his words were nearly incomprehensible, yet once events unfolded they often proved true.

sentences.zh: 恆寄住諸佛寺，好行人家，兼曆造王公邸第。

translations.literal: He constantly lodged at various Buddhist monasteries, liked to go among households, and also made the rounds of the mansions of kings and dukes.
translations.idiomatic: He habitually stayed at Buddhist monasteries, wandered through people's homes, and visited the residences of kings and nobles.

sentences.zh: 所至，人皆敬信之。

translations.literal: Wherever he went, people all revered and trusted him.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever he went, people treated him with reverence and trust.

sentences.zh: 晉公護未誅前，練曾手持一瓠，到護第門外抵破曰：「瓠破子苦。」

translations.literal: Before Duke Jin Yuwen Hu was executed, Lian once held a gourd, went to the gate of Hu's mansion, smashed it, and said: 'When the gourd breaks, the seeds are bitter.'
translations.idiomatic: Before Duke Jin Yuwen Hu was put to death, Lian once took a gourd to the gate of Hu's mansion, smashed it, and said, 'When the gourd breaks, the seeds turn bitter.'

sentences.zh: 時柱國、平高公侯伏龍恩深被任委，強練至龍恩宅，呼其妻元氏及其妾媵並婢僕等，並令連席而坐。

translations.literal: At that time the Pillar of State, Duke of Pinggao Hou Fulong'en, was deeply trusted with important duties. Qiang Lian came to Long'en's residence and summoned his wife, Lady Yuan, together with his concubines, attendants, and servants, ordering them all to sit in a row on one mat.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Pillar of State Hou Fulong'en, Duke of Pinggao, enjoyed great trust and heavy responsibility. Qiang Lian came to Long'en's house and called for his wife Lady Yuan, his concubines, attendants, and servants, ordering them all to sit together on one mat.

sentences.zh: 諸人以逼夫人，苦辭不肯。

translations.literal: The others, feeling this forced upon the lady of the house, pleaded hard and refused.
translations.idiomatic: The household, thinking this an affront to the lady of the house, pleaded hard and refused.

sentences.zh: 強練曰：「汝等一例人耳，何有貴賤。」

translations.literal: Qiang Lian said: 'You are all the same kind of people—what is there of noble and base?'
translations.idiomatic: Qiang Lian said, 'You are all the same sort of people—what difference is there between high and low?'

sentences.zh: 遂逼就坐。

translations.literal: He then forced them to take their seats.
translations.idiomatic: He then compelled them to sit.

sentences.zh: 未幾而護誅，諸子並死；

translations.literal: Before long Hu was executed, and all his sons also died;
translations.idiomatic: Before long Hu was executed, and all his sons perished as well;

sentences.zh: 龍恩亦伏法，仍籍沒其家。

translations.literal: Long'en was also put to death by law, and his household was confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: Long'en was also executed, and his property was confiscated.

sentences.zh: 建德中，每夜上街衢邊樹，大哭釋迦牟尼佛，或至申旦。

translations.literal: During the Jiande era, every night he would go to trees along the streets and alleys and weep loudly to Shakyamuni Buddha, sometimes until dawn.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jiande era he would go each night to trees along the city streets and wail to Shakyamuni Buddha, sometimes until dawn.

sentences.zh: 如此者累月，聲甚哀苦。

translations.literal: This went on for months, and his voice was very mournful.
translations.idiomatic: He did this for months on end, his cries heartbreakingly mournful.

sentences.zh: 俄而廢佛、道二教。

translations.literal: Before long Buddhism and Daoism were both suppressed.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward both Buddhism and Daoism were suppressed.

sentences.zh: 大象末，又以一無底囊，曆長安市肆告乞，市人爭以米麥遺之。

translations.literal: At the end of the Daxiang era, he again took a bottomless sack and went through the markets of Chang'an begging; townspeople competed to give him rice and grain.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Daxiang era he again took a bottomless sack and begged through the markets of Chang'an, and people vied to give him rice and grain.

sentences.zh: 強練張囊受之，隨即漏之於地。

translations.literal: Qiang Lian held the sack open to receive it, and it immediately leaked out onto the ground.
translations.idiomatic: Qiang Lian held the sack open to receive their gifts, and everything immediately spilled onto the ground.

sentences.zh: 人或問之，強練曰：「但欲使諸人見盛空耳。」

translations.literal: When people asked him about it, Qiang Lian said: 'I only want everyone to see full become empty.'
translations.idiomatic: When people asked him, Qiang Lian said, 'I only want everyone to see fullness turn to emptiness.'

sentences.zh: 至隋開皇初，果移都于龍首山，城遂空廢。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaihuang under the Sui, the capital was indeed moved to Longshou Mountain, and the city was left deserted.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Kaihuang under the Sui, the capital was indeed moved to Longshou Mountain, and the old city was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 後莫知其所終。

translations.literal: Afterward no one knew where he ended.
translations.idiomatic: After that, no one knew where he went.

sentences.zh: 又有蜀郡衛元嵩者，亦好言將來事，蓋江左寶志之流。

translations.literal: There was also Wei Yuansong of Shu Commandery, who likewise liked to speak of future events—of the same sort as Baozhi of the Jiangzuo region.
translations.idiomatic: There was also Wei Yuansong of Shu Commandery, who likewise loved to speak of things yet to come—much in the vein of Baozhi of the south.

sentences.zh: 天和中，遂著詩，預論周隋廢興及皇家受命，並有徵驗。

translations.literal: During the Tianhe era he composed poems foretelling the rise and fall of Zhou and Sui and the receiving of the mandate by the imperial house, all with corroborating signs.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianhe era he wrote poems foretelling the fall of Zhou, the rise of Sui, and the imperial house's receipt of the Mandate—all later borne out.

sentences.zh: 尤不信釋教，嘗上疏極論之。

translations.literal: He especially did not believe in Buddhism and once submitted a memorial arguing against it at length.
translations.idiomatic: He especially disbelieved Buddhism and once submitted a lengthy memorial attacking it.

sentences.zh: 庾季才，字叔弈，新野人也。

translations.literal: Yu Jicai, styled Shuyi, was a native of Xinye.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Jicai, styled Shuyi, was a native of Xinye.

sentences.zh: 八世祖滔，隨晉元帝過江，官至散騎常侍，封遂昌侯，因家于南郡江陵縣。

translations.literal: His eighth-generation ancestor Tao followed Emperor Yuan of Jin across the river, rose to Gentleman Attendant at Leisure, was enfeoffed as Marquis of Suichang, and the family settled in Jiangling County, Nan Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His eighth-generation ancestor Tao followed Emperor Yuan of Jin south across the Yangtze, rose to Gentleman Attendant at Leisure, was enfeoffed Marquis of Suichang, and the family settled in Jiangling County in Nan Commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖詵，《南史》有傳。

translations.literal: His grandfather Shen has a biography in the History of the Southern Dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Shen has a biography in the History of the Southern Dynasties.

sentences.zh: 父曼倩，光祿卿。

translations.literal: His father Manqian was Director of the Imperial Household.
translations.idiomatic: His father Manqian served as Director of the Imperial Household.

sentences.zh: 季才幼穎悟，八歲誦《尚書》，十二通《易》，好占玄象，居喪以孝聞。

translations.literal: From childhood Jicai was quick and perceptive; at eight he could recite the Documents, at twelve he mastered the Changes, loved to observe celestial and arcane signs, and was known for filial piety while in mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Jicai was bright from childhood: at eight he recited the Documents, at twelve he mastered the Changes, loved to read the heavens and hidden signs, and was famed for filial mourning.

sentences.zh: 梁湘東王繹引授外兵參軍。

translations.literal: Prince Xiangdong of Liang, Xiao Yi, summoned him and appointed him External Army Aide.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xiangdong of Liang, Xiao Yi, summoned him and made him External Army Aide.

sentences.zh: 西台建，累遷中書郎，領太史，封宣昌縣伯。

translations.literal: When the Western Terrace was established, he was promoted in succession to Palace Secretariat Gentleman, concurrently Grand Astrologer, and enfeoffed as Earl of Xuanzhang.
translations.idiomatic: When the Western Terrace was established, he rose in turn to Gentleman of the Palace Secretariat, concurrently Grand Astrologer, and was enfeoffed Earl of Xuanzhang.

sentences.zh: 季才固辭太史，梁元帝曰：「漢司馬遷曆世居掌，魏高堂隆猶領此職，卿何憚焉！」

translations.literal: Jicai firmly declined the post of Grand Astrologer. Emperor Yuan of Liang said: 'In Han, Sima Qian's family held this office for generations; in Wei, Gao Tanglong still held this charge—why do you shrink from it!'
translations.idiomatic: Jicai firmly declined the Grand Astrologer's post. Emperor Yuan of Liang said, 'Under Han, Sima Qian's family held this office for generations; under Wei, Gao Tanglong still kept it—why do you shrink from it!'

sentences.zh: 帝亦頗明星曆，謂曰：「朕猶慮禍起蕭牆。」

translations.literal: The emperor also knew the stars and calendars well and said to him: 'I still fear trouble arising within the palace walls.'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also understood the stars and calendars and told him, 'I still fear trouble rising within the palace walls.'

sentences.zh: 季才曰：「秦將入郢，陛下宜留重臣，作鎮荊陝，還都以避其患。」

translations.literal: Jicai said: 'Qin is about to enter Ying; Your Majesty should leave important ministers behind to hold Jing and Shaan, and return to the capital to avoid the disaster.'
translations.idiomatic: Jicai said, 'Qin is about to enter Ying; Your Majesty should leave trusted ministers to hold Jing and Shaan and return to the capital to escape the calamity.'

sentences.zh: 帝初然之，後與吏部尚書宗懍等議，乃止。

translations.literal: At first the emperor agreed, but after discussion with Minister of Personnel Zong Lin and others, he stopped.
translations.idiomatic: At first the emperor agreed, but after consulting Minister of Personnel Zong Lin and others, he abandoned the plan.

sentences.zh: 俄而江陵覆滅。

translations.literal: Before long Jiangling fell.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Jiangling fell.

sentences.zh: 周文帝一見，深加優禮，令參掌太史，曰：「卿宜盡誠事孤，當以富貴相答。」

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen of Zhou first met him, he treated him with exceptional courtesy and had him assist in managing the Grand Astrologer's office, saying: 'You should serve me with full loyalty; I shall repay you with wealth and honor.'
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen of Zhou first met him, he treated him with exceptional favor and had him assist in the Grand Astrologer's office, saying, 'Serve me with all your heart, and I shall reward you with wealth and rank.'

sentences.zh: 初，荊覆亡，衣冠士人，多沒為賤。

translations.literal: At first, when Jing fell, gentry and scholars for the most part were reduced to bondage.
translations.idiomatic: When Jing first fell, most gentry and scholars were reduced to servitude.

sentences.zh: 季才散所賜物，購求親故。

translations.literal: Jicai distributed the goods he had been granted to purchase and redeem relatives and friends.
translations.idiomatic: Jicai spent the gifts he had received to buy back relatives and friends.

sentences.zh: 周文問：「何能若此？」

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Zhou asked: 'How can you do this?'
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Zhou asked, 'How can you do this?'

sentences.zh: 季才曰：「郢都覆敗，君信有罪，縉紳何咎，皆為賤隸？

translations.literal: Jicai said: 'When Ying fell, the ruler indeed had guilt, but what fault had the gentry and officials, that they all became slaves?
translations.idiomatic: Jicai said, 'When Ying fell, the ruler bore guilt, but what crime had the gentry committed, that they should all become slaves?

sentences.zh: 誠竊哀之，故贖購耳。」

translations.literal: I truly pity them, and so I redeem them.'
translations.idiomatic: I pity them deeply, and so I redeem them.'

sentences.zh: 周文乃悟曰：「微君，遂失天下之望。」

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Zhou then understood and said: 'But for you, I would have lost the hope of the realm.'
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Zhou then understood and said, 'Without you, I would have lost the hearts of the realm.'

sentences.zh: 因出令，免梁浮為奴婢者數千口。

translations.literal: He therefore issued an order freeing several thousand Liang captives held as male and female slaves.
translations.idiomatic: He then issued an edict freeing several thousand Liang captives held as male and female slaves.

sentences.zh: 武定二年，與王褒、庾信同補麟趾學士，累遷稍伯大夫。

translations.literal: In the second year of Wuding, together with Wang Bao and Yu Xin he was appointed Linqi Academician, and was promoted in succession to Grand Master of the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Wuding, together with Wang Bao and Yu Xin he was appointed Linqi Academician and rose in turn to Grand Master of the Palace.

sentences.zh: 後宇文護執政，問以天道徵祥，對曰：「頃上臺有變，不利宰輔，公宜歸政天子，請老私門。」

translations.literal: Later, when Yuwen Hu held power, he asked about heavenly signs and portents. Jicai replied: 'Recently there has been a change in the Upper Platform unfavorable to the chief minister; you should return power to the Son of Heaven and retire to your private gate.'
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Yuwen Hu held power, he asked about heavenly omens. Jicai replied, 'Recently the Upper Platform has shifted in a way unfavorable to the chief minister; you should return power to the Son of Heaven and retire to private life.'

sentences.zh: 護沈吟久之，曰：「吾本意如此，但辭未獲免。」

translations.literal: Hu pondered a long time and said: 'That was originally my intent, but my resignation has not yet been accepted.'
translations.idiomatic: Hu brooded a long while and said, 'That was always my intent, but my resignation has not yet been granted.'

sentences.zh: 自是漸疏。

translations.literal: From then on he gradually grew distant.
translations.idiomatic: From then on Hu gradually kept his distance from him.

sentences.zh: 及護夷滅，閱其書記，有假託符命，妄造異端者，皆誅。

translations.literal: When Hu was destroyed, his records were examined, and those who had falsely invoked the mandate and fabricated heterodox doctrines were all executed.
translations.idiomatic: When Hu was destroyed, his papers were examined, and those who had forged omens and invented heresies were all put to death.

sentences.zh: 唯得季才兩紙，盛言緯候，宜免政歸權。

translations.literal: Only two sheets of Jicai's were found, strongly arguing from celestial patterns that power should be returned to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Only two sheets in Jicai's hand were found, arguing forcefully from celestial patterns that power should return to the throne.

sentences.zh: 帝謂少宗伯斛斯徵曰：「季才甚得人臣之禮。」

translations.literal: The emperor said to Junior Director of the Imperial Clan Husi Zheng: 'Jicai truly observes the propriety owed by a minister.'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said to Junior Director of the Imperial Clan Husi Zheng, 'Jicai truly understands a minister's duty.'

sentences.zh: 因賜粟帛，遷太史中大夫。

translations.literal: He therefore granted grain and silk and promoted him to Grand Master of the Grand Astrologer's Office.
translations.idiomatic: He granted him grain and silk and promoted him to Grand Master of the Grand Astrologer's Office.

sentences.zh: 詔撰《靈台秘苑》，封臨潁縣伯。

translations.literal: He was ordered to compile the Secret Garden of the Spirit Terrace and was enfeoffed as Earl of Linying.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to compile the Secret Garden of the Spirit Terrace and was enfeoffed Earl of Linying.

sentences.zh: 宣帝嗣位，加驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuan succeeded to the throne, Jicai was additionally made General of Agile Cavalry and given the status of a government with separate establishment and third-rank ceremonial parity.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuan succeeded to the throne, Jicai was additionally made General of Agile Cavalry with the status of an independent command and third-rank ceremonial parity.

sentences.zh: 及隋文帝為丞相，嘗夜召問天時人事，季才曰：「天道精微，難可悉察。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen of Sui was serving as chief minister, he once summoned Jicai at night to ask about heavenly signs and human affairs. Jicai said: 'Heaven's way is subtle and fine, and hard to observe fully.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen of Sui was chief minister, he once summoned Jicai at night to ask about heaven and human affairs. Jicai said, 'Heaven's way is subtle and cannot be fully discerned.

sentences.zh: 竊以人事卜之，符兆已定，季才縱言不可，公得為箕、潁事乎？」

translations.literal: Judging by human affairs on my own, the signs are already fixed; even if Jicai says it cannot be, could you become like those who farmed at Ji and Ying?'
translations.idiomatic: Judging by human affairs alone, the signs are already set; even if I say it cannot be done, could you retire to farm like Xu You at Ji and Ying?'

sentences.zh: 帝默然久之曰：「吾今譬騎武，誠不得下矣。」

translations.literal: The emperor was silent a long time and said: 'I am now like one riding a tiger—it truly cannot be dismounted.'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was silent a long while and said, 'I am now like a man riding a tiger—I truly cannot get down.'

sentences.zh: 因賜以彩帛曰：「愧公此意。」

translations.literal: He therefore granted colored silks, saying: 'I am ashamed before this intention of yours.'
translations.idiomatic: He granted colored silks, saying, 'I am ashamed before your honesty.'

sentences.zh: 大定元年正月，季才上言：「今月戊戌平旦，青氣如樓闕，見國城上。

translations.literal: In the first month of the first year of Dading, Jicai submitted a memorial: 'On the day wuxu of this month, at dawn, azure vapor like a tower-gate appeared above the national capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the first year of Dading, Jicai submitted a memorial: 'On wuxu day this month at dawn, azure vapor like a tower-gate appeared above the capital.

sentences.zh: 俄而變紫，逆風西行。

translations.literal: Before long it turned purple and moved west against the wind.
translations.idiomatic: Soon it turned purple and drifted west against the wind.

sentences.zh: 《氣經》云：'天不能無雲而雨，皇王不能無氣而立。

translations.literal: The Classic of Vapor says: 'Heaven cannot stand without clouds and rain; kings cannot stand without vapor.
translations.idiomatic: The Classic of Vapor says, 'Heaven cannot stand without clouds and rain; kings cannot stand without royal vapor.

sentences.zh: '今王氣已見，須即應之。

translations.literal: Now the kingly vapor has appeared; you must respond to it at once.
translations.idiomatic: Now the kingly vapor has appeared; you must answer it at once.

sentences.zh: 二月，日出卯入酉，居天之正位，謂之二八之門。

translations.literal: In the second month, the sun rises at mao and sets at you, occupying heaven's central position—this is called the Gate of Two Eights.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month the sun rises at mao and sets at you, occupying heaven's central position—the Gate of Two Eights.

sentences.zh: 日者人君之象，人君正位，宜用二月。

translations.literal: The sun is the image of the ruler; when the ruler occupies the correct position, the second month should be used.
translations.idiomatic: The sun is the image of the ruler; when the ruler stands in the correct position, the second month is the proper time.

sentences.zh: 其月十三日甲子，甲為六甲之始，子為十二辰之初。

translations.literal: On the thirteenth day of that month, jiazi—jia is the beginning of the six jia, and zi is the beginning of the twelve branches.
translations.idiomatic: On the thirteenth of that month, jiazi day—jia is the start of the six jia cycles, and zi the start of the twelve branches.

sentences.zh: 甲數九，子數又九，九為天數。

translations.literal: The number of jia is nine, and the number of zi is also nine; nine is heaven's number.
translations.idiomatic: Jia counts as nine, and zi counts as nine as well; nine is heaven's number.

sentences.zh: 其日即是驚蟄，陽氣壯發之時。

translations.literal: That day is precisely Awakening of Insects, the time when yang energy surges forth.
translations.idiomatic: That day is precisely Awakening of Insects, when yang energy bursts forth.

sentences.zh: 昔周武王以二月甲子定天下，享年八百；

translations.literal: Formerly King Wu of Zhou fixed the realm on jiazi in the second month and enjoyed the realm for eight hundred years;
translations.idiomatic: Formerly King Wu of Zhou established the realm on jiazi in the second month and held it for eight hundred years;

sentences.zh: 漢高帝以二月甲午即帝位，享年四百。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu of Han ascended the throne on jiawu in the second month and enjoyed the realm for four hundred years.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu of Han took the throne on jiawu in the second month and held it for four hundred years.

sentences.zh: 故知甲子、甲午為得天數。

translations.literal: Thus one knows that jiazi and jiawu accord with heaven's number.
translations.idiomatic: Thus jiazi and jiawu accord with heaven's number.

sentences.zh: 今月甲子，宜應天受命。」

translations.literal: On jiazi this month, you should receive heaven's mandate.'
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi this month, you should receive heaven's mandate.'

sentences.zh: 上從之。

translations.literal: The emperor followed his advice.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor followed his advice.

sentences.zh: 開皇元年，授通直散騎常侍。

translations.literal: In the first year of Kaihuang he was appointed Regular Attendant of the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Kaihuang he was appointed Regular Attendant of the Palace.

sentences.zh: 帝將遷都，夜與高熲、蘇威二人定議。

translations.literal: When the emperor was about to move the capital, at night he settled the plan with Gao Feng and Su Wei.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor planned to move the capital, he settled the matter at night with Gao Feng and Su Wei.

sentences.zh: 季才旦奏：「臣仰觀玄象，俯察圖記，龜兆允襲，必有遷都。

translations.literal: At dawn Jicai submitted: 'Looking up I observe the arcane signs; looking down I examine charts and records; tortoise and milfoil agree—there must be a move of the capital.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn Jicai submitted, 'Looking up I read the arcane signs; looking down I examine charts and records; tortoise and milfoil agree—a move of the capital is ordained.

sentences.zh: 且漢營此城，經今將八百歲，水皆鹹鹵，不甚宜人，願為遷徒計。」

translations.literal: Moreover, Han built this city; nearly eight hundred years have passed, and the water is all brackish and unfit for people—I beg you to plan a move.'
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, Han built this city nearly eight hundred years ago; the water is brackish and unfit for habitation—I beg you to plan a move.'

sentences.zh: 帝愕然，謂熲等曰：「是何神也！」

translations.literal: The emperor was startled and said to Gao Feng and the others: 'What kind of spirit is this!'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was startled and said to Gao Feng and the others, 'What kind of oracle is this!'

sentences.zh: 遂發詔施行。

translations.literal: He then issued an edict and carried it out.
translations.idiomatic: He then issued an edict and carried it out.

sentences.zh: 賜季才絹布及進爵為公。

translations.literal: Jicai was granted silk and cloth and advanced in rank to duke.
translations.idiomatic: Jicai was granted silk and cloth and raised to duke.

sentences.zh: 謂曰：「朕自今已後，信有天道。」

translations.literal: The emperor said to him: 'From now on I believe in heaven's way.'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told him, 'From now on I believe in heaven's way.'

sentences.zh: 於是令季才與其子質撰《垂象》、《地形》等志。

translations.literal: He then had Jicai and his son Zhi compile the treatises Hanging Signs and Topography.
translations.idiomatic: He then had Jicai and his son Zhi compile the treatises Hanging Signs and Topography.

sentences.zh: 謂曰：「天道秘奧，推測多途，執見不同，不欲令外人干預此事，故令公父子共為之。」

translations.literal: He said to him: 'Heaven's way is secret and abstruse; there are many paths of inference, and fixed views differ—I do not wish outsiders to meddle in this matter, and so I have you father and son do it together.'
translations.idiomatic: He told him, 'Heaven's way is secret and abstruse, with many paths of inference and clashing views—I do not want outsiders involved, and so I have you and your son do this together.'

sentences.zh: 及書成奏之，賜米帛甚優。

translations.literal: When the books were finished and submitted, he was granted rice and silk in generous measure.
translations.idiomatic: When the books were finished and submitted, he was granted rice and silk in generous measure.

sentences.zh: 九年，出為均州刺史。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was sent out as Governor of Junzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he was sent out as Governor of Junzhou.

sentences.zh: 時議以季才術藝精通，有詔還委舊任。

translations.literal: At the time it was debated that Jicai's arts and skills were masterful, and an edict recalled him to his former post.
translations.idiomatic: At the time, because Jicai's arts were judged supreme, an edict recalled him to his former post.

sentences.zh: 以年老，頻求去職，優旨每不許。

translations.literal: On account of old age he repeatedly asked to leave office, but gracious edicts each time refused.
translations.idiomatic: Citing his age, he repeatedly asked to retire, but gracious edicts each time refused.

sentences.zh: 會張胄玄曆行，及袁充言日景長，上以問季才，因言充謬。

translations.literal: When Zhang Zhouxuan's calendar was adopted and Yuan Chong said the sun's shadow was lengthening, the emperor questioned Jicai, who thereupon declared Yuan Chong mistaken.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Zhouxuan's calendar was adopted and Yuan Chong claimed the sun's shadow was lengthening, the emperor asked Jicai, who declared Yuan Chong mistaken.

sentences.zh: 上大怒，由是免職，給半祿歸第。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly angered and on that account removed him from office, granting half salary and sending him home.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious and dismissed him, granting half salary and sending him home.

sentences.zh: 所有祥異，常令人就家訪焉。

translations.literal: Whenever there were auspicious or strange signs, he regularly had people go to his house to inquire.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever omens appeared, the court regularly sent people to his home to inquire.

sentences.zh: 仁壽三年，卒。

translations.literal: In the third year of Renshou he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Renshou he died.

sentences.zh: 季才局量寬弘，術業優博，篤于信義，志好賓遊。

translations.literal: Jicai was broad and magnanimous in temperament, superb and abundant in skill and learning, steadfast in faith and righteousness, and fond of hosting guests.
translations.idiomatic: Jicai was broad-minded and magnanimous, superb in learning and craft, steadfast in faith and friendship, and fond of gathering guests.

sentences.zh: 常吉日良辰，與琅邪王褒、彭城劉玨、河東裴政及宗人信等為文酒之會。

translations.literal: On auspicious days and fine hours he would regularly join Wang Bao of Langye, Liu Jue of Pengcheng, Pei Zheng of Hedong, and his clansman Xin and others in literary banquets with wine.
translations.idiomatic: On fine days and at pleasant hours he regularly joined Wang Bao of Langye, Liu Jue of Pengcheng, Pei Zheng of Hedong, and his kinsman Xin and others for literary gatherings over wine.

sentences.zh: 次有劉臻、明克讓、柳{巧言}之徒，雖後進，亦申遊款。

translations.literal: Next came Liu Zhen, Ming Kerang, Liu Rang, and the like; though they were juniors, they too were admitted to his company.
translations.idiomatic: Later came Liu Zhen, Ming Kerang, Liu Rang, and others; though younger, they too were welcomed into his circle.

sentences.zh: 撰《靈台秘苑》一百二十卷，《垂象志》一百四十二卷，《地形志》八十七卷，並行於世。

translations.literal: He compiled the Secret Garden of the Spirit Terrace in one hundred twenty scrolls, the Treatise on Hanging Signs in one hundred forty-two scrolls, and the Treatise on Topography in eighty-seven scrolls, all circulating in the world.
translations.idiomatic: He compiled the Secret Garden of the Spirit Terrace in one hundred twenty scrolls, the Treatise on Hanging Signs in one hundred forty-two scrolls, and the Treatise on Topography in eighty-seven scrolls, all of which circulated in his day.

sentences.zh: 子質，字行脩。

translations.literal: His son Zhi, styled Xingxiu,
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhi, styled Xingxiu,

sentences.zh: 早有志尚，八歲誦梁元帝《玄覽》、《言志》等十賦，拜童子郎。

translations.literal: from early on had lofty aspirations; at eight he could recite ten fu by Emperor Yuan of Liang, including Mysterious Survey and Declaring Intent, and was appointed Boy Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: showed high ambition from youth; at eight he recited ten fu by Emperor Yuan of Liang, including Mysterious Survey and Declaring Intent, and was appointed Boy Attendant.

sentences.zh: 仕隋，累遷隴州司馬。

translations.literal: Serving under the Sui, he was promoted in succession to Prefectural Marshal of Longzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Sui he rose in turn to Prefectural Marshal of Longzhou.

sentences.zh: 大業初，授太史令。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Daye he was appointed Grand Astrologer.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Daye he was appointed Grand Astrologer.

sentences.zh: 操履貞懿，立言忠鯁，每有災異，必指事面陳。

translations.literal: His conduct was upright and pure; his words were loyal and blunt. Whenever there was a disaster or strange sign, he always pointed to the matter and spoke face to face.
translations.idiomatic: Upright and pure in conduct, loyal and blunt in speech, whenever omens appeared he always named the matter plainly to the emperor's face.

sentences.zh: 煬帝多忌刻，齊王暕亦被猜嫌。

translations.literal: Emperor Yang was much given to suspicion and harshness; Prince of Qi Yang Zhao was also viewed with doubt.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yang was deeply suspicious and harsh; Prince of Qi Yang Zhao was also viewed with distrust.

sentences.zh: 質子儉時為齊王屬，帝謂質曰：「汝不能一心事我，乃使兒事齊王。」

translations.literal: Zhi's son Jian was then an aide to the Prince of Qi. The emperor said to Zhi: 'You cannot serve me with undivided heart, yet you let your son serve the Prince of Qi.'
translations.idiomatic: Zhi's son Jian was then an aide to the Prince of Qi. The emperor told Zhi, 'You cannot serve me wholeheartedly, yet you let your son serve the Prince of Qi.'

sentences.zh: 由是出為合水令。

translations.literal: On that account he was sent out as Magistrate of Heshui.
translations.idiomatic: On that account he was sent out as Magistrate of Heshui.

sentences.zh: 八年，帝親伐遼東，徵至臨渝，問東伐克不。

translations.literal: In the eighth year the emperor personally campaigned against Liaodong; Zhi was summoned to Linyu and asked whether the eastern campaign would succeed.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year the emperor personally marched against Liaodong; Zhi was summoned to Linyu and asked whether the eastern campaign would succeed.

sentences.zh: 對曰：「伐之可克，不願陛下親行。」

translations.literal: He replied: 'It can be conquered, but I do not wish Your Majesty to go in person.'
translations.idiomatic: He replied, 'It can be taken, but I do not wish Your Majesty to go in person.'

sentences.zh: 帝作色曰：「朕今總兵至此，豈可未見賊而自退！」

translations.literal: The emperor's face changed and he said: 'I have now gathered the army here—how can I withdraw before even seeing the enemy!'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's face darkened and he said, 'I have brought the army this far—how can I turn back before even seeing the enemy!'

sentences.zh: 質曰：「願安駕住此，命將授規，事宜在速，緩必無功。」

translations.literal: Zhi said: 'I wish Your Majesty would secure the imperial carriage here, appoint generals and give them strategy—the matter must be swift; if delayed, there will surely be no success.'
translations.idiomatic: Zhi said, 'I wish Your Majesty would remain here in safety, appoint generals and give them strategy—the matter must be swift; delay will surely bring failure.'

sentences.zh: 帝不悅曰：「汝既難行，可住此也。」

translations.literal: The emperor, displeased, said: 'Since you find it hard to go, you may stay here.'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, displeased, said, 'Since you find the march hard, you may stay here.'

sentences.zh: 及師還，授太史令。

translations.literal: When the army returned, he was appointed Grand Astrologer.
translations.idiomatic: When the army returned, he was appointed Grand Astrologer.

sentences.zh: 九年，復征高麗，又問：「今段何如？」

translations.literal: In the ninth year Liaodong was again attacked; the emperor again asked: 'How will this campaign go?
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year Liaodong was attacked again; the emperor again asked, 'How will this campaign go?

sentences.zh: 對猶執前見。

translations.literal: He replied, still holding to his earlier view.
translations.idiomatic: He answered, still holding to his earlier view.

sentences.zh: 帝怒曰：「我自行尚不能克，遣人豈有成功？」

translations.literal: The emperor angrily said: 'If I go in person and still cannot conquer it, how could sending others succeed?'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor angrily said, 'If I go in person and still cannot conquer it, how could sending others succeed?'

sentences.zh: 帝遂行。

translations.literal: The emperor then went.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor went anyway.

sentences.zh: 既而楊玄感反，斛斯政奔高麗，帝大懼，遽歸。

translations.literal: Before long Yang Xuangan rebelled, Husi Zheng fled to Goguryeo, and the emperor was greatly afraid and hurried back.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Yang Xuangan rebelled, Husi Zheng fled to Goguryeo, and the emperor, terrified, hurried back.

sentences.zh: 謂質曰：「卿前不許我行，當為此耳。

translations.literal: He said to Zhi: 'You would not let me go—it was for this.
translations.idiomatic: He said to Zhi, 'You would not let me go—it was for this.

sentences.zh: 今玄感成乎？」

translations.literal: Will Xuangan succeed now?'
translations.idiomatic: Will Xuangan succeed now?'

sentences.zh: 質曰：「今天下一家，未易可動。」
