translations.literal: Zhi said: 'Under heaven there is now one family; he cannot easily be moved.'
translations.idiomatic: Zhi said, 'The realm is now united under one house; he cannot easily succeed.'

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「熒惑入鬥，如何？」

translations.literal: The emperor said: 'Mars enters the Dipper—what of that?'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, 'Mars enters the Dipper—what of that?'

sentences.zh: 對曰：「鬥，楚分，玄感之封。

translations.literal: He replied: 'The Dipper is the division of Chu; it is Xuangan's fief.
translations.idiomatic: He replied, 'The Dipper is the Chu division—the territory of Xuangan's fief.

sentences.zh: 今火色衰謝，終必無成。」

translations.literal: Now the fire star's color is fading; in the end he will surely not succeed.'
translations.idiomatic: Now the fire star's color is fading; in the end he will surely fail.'

sentences.zh: 十年，帝自西京將往東都。

translations.literal: In the tenth year the emperor was about to go from the Western Capital to the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year the emperor was about to travel from the Western Capital to the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 質諫宜鎮撫關內，使百姓歸農，三五年，令四海少豐，然後巡省。

translations.literal: Zhi remonstrated that he should pacify and secure the lands within the passes, let the people return to farming, and after three or five years, when the four seas were somewhat abundant, then make an inspection tour.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi urged him to pacify the lands within the passes, let the people return to farming, and wait three to five years until the realm had recovered somewhat before touring the east.

sentences.zh: 帝不悅。

translations.literal: The emperor was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was displeased.

sentences.zh: 質辭疾不從，帝聞之怒，遣馳傳鎖質詣行在所。

translations.literal: Zhi pleaded illness and would not follow; when the emperor heard of it he was angry and sent a fast courier to shackle Zhi and bring him to the imperial presence.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi pleaded illness and refused to accompany him; when the emperor heard, he was furious and sent a fast courier to shackle Zhi and bring him to the imperial presence.

sentences.zh: 至東都下獄，竟死獄中。

translations.literal: When he reached the Eastern Capital he was thrown into prison and ultimately died there.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached the Eastern Capital he was thrown into prison and died there.

sentences.zh: 子儉，亦傳父業，兼有學識。

translations.literal: His son Jian also inherited his father's craft and possessed learning as well.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jian also inherited his father's craft and had learning besides.

sentences.zh: 仕歷襄武令、元德太子學士、齊王屬。

translations.literal: In office he served as Magistrate of Xiangwu, Academician to the Heir Apparent of Yuande, and Aide to the Prince of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: In office he served as Magistrate of Xiangwu, Academician to the Heir Apparent of Yuande, and Aide to the Prince of Qi.

sentences.zh: 義甯初，為太史令。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yining he was made Grand Astrologer.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Yining he was made Grand Astrologer.

sentences.zh: 盧太翼，字協昭，河間人也。

translations.literal: Lu Taiyi, styled Xiezhao, was a native of Hejian.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Taiyi, styled Xiezhao, was a native of Hejian.

sentences.zh: 本姓章仇氏。

translations.literal: His original surname was Zhangqiu.
translations.idiomatic: His original surname was Zhangqiu.

sentences.zh: 七歲詣學，日誦數千言，州裏號曰神童。

translations.literal: At seven he went to school and recited several thousand words a day; in the district he was called a divine prodigy.
translations.idiomatic: At seven he went to school and recited several thousand words a day; locally he was called a divine prodigy.

sentences.zh: 及長，博綜群書，尤善占候、算曆之術。

translations.literal: When grown, he broadly mastered many books and was especially skilled in observing omens and the arts of calculation and calendrics.
translations.idiomatic: When grown, he mastered many books and was especially skilled in omens, calculation, and calendrics.

sentences.zh: 隱于白鹿山，徙居林慮山茱萸澗。

translations.literal: He hid himself on Mount Bailu, then moved to Cornel Creek in the Linlu Mountains.
translations.idiomatic: He withdrew to Mount Bailu, then moved to Cornel Creek in the Linlu Mountains.

sentences.zh: 受業者自遠而至。

translations.literal: Students came to receive instruction from afar.
translations.idiomatic: Students came from afar to study under him.

sentences.zh: 初無所拒，後憚其煩，逃於五臺山。

translations.literal: At first he refused none; later, fearing the bother, he fled to Mount Wutai.
translations.idiomatic: At first he turned none away; later, weary of the crowds, he fled to Mount Wutai.

sentences.zh: 地多藥物，與弟子數人，廬於岩下，以為神仙可致。

translations.literal: The place had many medicinal herbs; with several disciples he built a hut beneath the cliffs, believing immortals could be attained.
translations.idiomatic: The place abounded in medicinal herbs; with several disciples he built a hut beneath the cliffs, believing immortals could be attained.

sentences.zh: 隋太子勇聞而召之。

translations.literal: Crown Prince Yong of Sui heard of him and summoned him.
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Yong of Sui heard of him and summoned him.

sentences.zh: 太翼知太子必不為嗣，謂所親曰：「吾拘逼而來，不知所稅駕也。」

translations.literal: Taiyi knew the crown prince would surely not become heir and said to those close to him: 'I was forced here and do not know where I shall alight.'
translations.idiomatic: Taiyi knew the crown prince would never succeed and told his intimates, 'I was dragged here against my will, and I do not know where I shall end.'

sentences.zh: 及太子廢，坐法當死。

translations.literal: When the crown prince was deposed, by law he should have been put to death.
translations.idiomatic: When the crown prince was deposed, by law he should have been executed.

sentences.zh: 文帝惜其才，配為官奴，久乃釋。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen valued his talent and sentenced him to government slavery; after a long time he was released.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen valued his talent and commuted the sentence to government slavery; after a long time he was released.

sentences.zh: 其後目盲，以手摸書而知其字。

translations.literal: Afterward he went blind and knew characters by feeling books with his hands.
translations.idiomatic: Later he went blind and read by feeling books with his hands.

sentences.zh: 仁壽末，帝將避暑仁壽宮，太翼固諫曰：「恐是行鑾輿不反。」

translations.literal: At the end of Renshou the emperor was about to take the summer retreat at Renshou Palace; Taiyi firmly remonstrated, saying: 'I fear this is a journey from which the imperial carriage will not return.'
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of Renshou the emperor planned to summer at Renshou Palace; Taiyi firmly remonstrated, saying, 'I fear this is a journey from which the imperial carriage will not return.'

sentences.zh: 帝大怒，系之長安獄，期還斬之。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly angered, imprisoned him in Chang'an, and set a date to behead him on return.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious, imprisoned him in Chang'an, and set a date to behead him on his return.

sentences.zh: 帝至宮寢疾，臨崩，命皇太子釋之。

translations.literal: When the emperor reached the palace he fell ill; on the verge of death he ordered the crown prince to release him.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor reached the palace he fell ill; on his deathbed he ordered the crown prince to release him.

sentences.zh: 及煬帝即位，漢王諒反，帝問之。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang succeeded to the throne, Prince of Han Yang Liang rebelled; the emperor asked Taiyi about it.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang succeeded to the throne, Prince of Han Yang Liang rebelled; the emperor asked Taiyi about it.

sentences.zh: 答曰：「何所能為！」

translations.literal: He replied: 'What can he accomplish!'
translations.idiomatic: He replied, 'What can he accomplish!'

sentences.zh: 未幾，諒果敗。

translations.literal: Before long Liang indeed was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Liang was indeed defeated.

sentences.zh: 帝從容言天下氏族，謂太翼曰：「卿姓章仇，四嶽之胄，與盧同源。」

translations.literal: The emperor spoke at leisure of clans in the realm and said to Taiyi: 'Your surname is Zhangqiu, descendant of the Four Peaks, of the same origin as the Lu clan.'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor spoke at leisure of the realm's great clans and told Taiyi, 'Your surname is Zhangqiu, descendant of the Four Peaks, of the same origin as the Lu clan.'

sentences.zh: 於是賜姓盧氏。

translations.literal: He therefore granted him the surname Lu.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore granted him the surname Lu.

sentences.zh: 大業九年，從駕至遼東。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Daye he accompanied the imperial procession to Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Daye he accompanied the emperor to Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 太翼言黎陽有兵氣，後數日而楊玄感反書聞。

translations.literal: Taiyi said there was a military aura at Liyang; several days later word came that Yang Xuangan had rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: Taiyi said there was a military aura at Liyang; several days later came word that Yang Xuangan had rebelled.

sentences.zh: 帝甚異之，數加賞賜。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly astonished and repeatedly added rewards.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was greatly astonished and repeatedly rewarded him.

sentences.zh: 太翼所言天文之事，不可稱數，關諸秘密，時莫能聞。

translations.literal: What Taiyi spoke of in celestial matters cannot be counted; it touched on secrets, and at the time none could hear of it.
translations.idiomatic: Taiyi's pronouncements on celestial matters were beyond counting; they touched on secrets none could hear at the time.

sentences.zh: 後數歲，卒于雒陽。

translations.literal: Several years later he died at Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Several years later he died at Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 耿詢，字敦信，丹楊人也。

translations.literal: Geng Xun, styled Dunxin, was a native of Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: Geng Xun, styled Dunxin, was a native of Danyang.

sentences.zh: 滑稽辯給，伎巧絕人。

translations.literal: Witty, glib, and clever in speech, his skill and ingenuity were unmatched.
translations.idiomatic: Witty, glib, and endlessly clever, his ingenuity was unmatched.

sentences.zh: 陳後主時，以客從東衡州刺史王勇於嶺南。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Houzhu of Chen, as a guest he followed Wang Yong, Governor of East Hengzhou, to Lingnan.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Houzhu of Chen he followed Wang Yong, Governor of East Hengzhou, to Lingnan as a guest.

sentences.zh: 勇卒，詢不歸。

translations.literal: When Yong died, Xun did not return.
translations.idiomatic: When Yong died, Xun did not return north.

sentences.zh: 會群俚反叛，推詢為主，柱國王世積討禽之。

translations.literal: When the various Li tribes rebelled, they made Xun their leader; Pillar of State Wang Shiji campaigned against them and captured him.
translations.idiomatic: When the Li tribes rebelled, they made Xun their leader; Pillar of State Wang Shiji campaigned against them and captured him.

sentences.zh: 罪當誅，自言有巧思，世積釋之，以為家奴。

translations.literal: His crime merited death; he himself said he had clever ideas, and Shiji released him and made him a household slave.
translations.idiomatic: His crime merited death; claiming clever ingenuity, he was released by Shiji and made a household slave.

sentences.zh: 久之，見其故人高智寶以玄象直太史，詢從之受天文算術。

translations.literal: After a long time he saw his old acquaintance Gao Zhibao serving as Grand Astrologer on account of celestial signs, and from him Xun received instruction in astronomy and calculation.
translations.idiomatic: Long afterward he saw his old acquaintance Gao Zhibao serving as Grand Astrologer for his knowledge of the heavens, and studied astronomy and calculation under him.

sentences.zh: 詢創意造渾天儀，不假人力，以水轉之，施於暗室中，使智寶外候天時，動合符契。

translations.literal: Xun devised and built a armillary sphere that turned by water without human labor; placed in a dark room, Zhibao observed the heavens outside and the motions matched in proof.
translations.idiomatic: Xun devised an armillary sphere turned by water without human labor; placed in a dark room, Zhibao watched the sky outside and the motions matched perfectly.

sentences.zh: 世積知而奏之，文帝配詢為官奴，給太史局。

translations.literal: When Shiji learned of it and memorialized, Emperor Wen sentenced Xun to government slavery and assigned him to the Grand Astrologer's office.
translations.idiomatic: When Shiji learned of it and memorialized, Emperor Wen sentenced Xun to government slavery and assigned him to the Grand Astrologer's office.

sentences.zh: 後賜蜀王秀，從往益州，秀甚信之。

translations.literal: Later he was granted to Prince of Shu Yang Xiu and followed him to Yizhou; Xiu greatly trusted him.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was granted to Prince of Shu Yang Xiu and followed him to Yizhou; Xiu trusted him deeply.

sentences.zh: 及秀廢，復當誅。

translations.literal: When Xiu was deposed, he again should have been executed.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiu was deposed, he again faced execution.

sentences.zh: 何稠言耿詢之巧，思若有神，上於是特原其罪。

translations.literal: He Chou spoke of Geng Xun's ingenuity, saying his thinking was like that of a spirit; the emperor thereupon specially pardoned his crime.
translations.idiomatic: He Chou praised Geng Xun's ingenuity, saying his mind worked like a spirit's; the emperor thereupon specially pardoned him.

sentences.zh: 詢作馬上刻漏，世稱其妙。

translations.literal: Xun made a clepsydra for use on horseback; the age called it marvelous.
translations.idiomatic: Xun made a clepsydra for use on horseback; his age called it marvelous.

sentences.zh: 煬帝即位，進欹器。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang succeeded to the throne, he presented a tipping vessel.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang succeeded to the throne, he presented a tipping vessel.

sentences.zh: 帝善之，免其奴。

translations.literal: The emperor approved and freed him from slavery.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved and freed him from slavery.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，授右尚方署監事。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was appointed Supervisor of the Right Palace Workshops.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a year he was appointed Supervisor of the Right Palace Workshops.

sentences.zh: 七年，車駕東征，詢上言曰：「遼東不可討，師必無功。」

translations.literal: In the seventh year, when the imperial carriage campaigned east, Xun submitted: 'Liaodong cannot be attacked; the army will surely achieve nothing.'
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, when the emperor campaigned east, Xun submitted, 'Liaodong cannot be attacked; the army will surely fail.'

sentences.zh: 帝大怒，命左右斬之。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly angered and ordered his attendants to behead him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious and ordered his attendants to behead him.

sentences.zh: 何稠苦諫得免。

translations.literal: He Chou pleaded hard and secured his pardon.
translations.idiomatic: He Chou pleaded hard and secured his pardon.

sentences.zh: 及平壤之敗，帝以詢言為中，以詢守太史丞。

translations.literal: When Pyongyang was defeated, the emperor considered Xun's words correct and had Xun hold the post of Vice Grand Astrologer.
translations.idiomatic: After the defeat at Pyongyang, the emperor judged Xun's words correct and made him Vice Grand Astrologer.

sentences.zh: 宇文化及弑逆之後，從至黎陽，謂其妻曰：「近觀人事，遠察天文，宇文必敗，李氏當王，吾知所歸矣。」

translations.literal: After Yuwen Huaji's regicide he followed him to Liyang and said to his wife: 'Observing human affairs near at hand and celestial signs far off, Yuwen will surely fall and the Li house will reign—I know where to go.'
translations.idiomatic: After Yuwen Huaji's regicide he followed him to Liyang and told his wife, 'Observing affairs near at hand and the heavens far off, Yuwen will surely fall and the Li house will reign—I know where to go.'

sentences.zh: 謀欲去之，為化及所殺。

translations.literal: He planned to leave, but Huaji killed him.
translations.idiomatic: He planned to leave, but Huaji killed him.

sentences.zh: 著《鳥情占》一卷，行於世。

translations.literal: He wrote Bird-Disposition Divination in one scroll, which circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote Bird-Disposition Divination in one scroll, which circulated in his day.

sentences.zh: 來和，字弘順，京兆長安人也。

translations.literal: Lai He, styled Hongshun, was a native of Chang'an in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Lai He, styled Hongshun, was a native of Chang'an in Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 少好相術，所言多驗。

translations.literal: From youth he loved physiognomy; what he said often proved true.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he loved physiognomy; what he said often came true.

sentences.zh: 周大塚宰宇文護引之左右，累遷畿伯下大夫，封洹水縣男。

translations.literal: Grand Minister Yuwen Hu of Zhou summoned him to his side; he was promoted in succession to Grand Master of the Jiji District and enfeoffed as Baron of Huanshui.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Minister Yuwen Hu of Zhou summoned him to his side; he rose in turn to Grand Master of the Jiji District and was enfeoffed Baron of Huanshui.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝微時，詣和。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen of Sui was still obscure, he went to see He.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen of Sui was still obscure, he went to see He.

sentences.zh: 曰：「公當王有四海。」

translations.literal: He said: 'You will reign and possess all within the four seas.'
translations.idiomatic: He said, 'You will reign and possess all within the four seas.'

sentences.zh: 及為丞相，拜儀同。

translations.literal: When he became chief minister, He was appointed Same Precedence.
translations.idiomatic: When he became chief minister, He was appointed Same Precedence.

sentences.zh: 既受禪，進爵為子。

translations.literal: After receiving the abdication, he was advanced in rank to viscount.
translations.idiomatic: After receiving the abdication, he was raised to viscount.

sentences.zh: 開皇末，和上表自陳龍潛所言曰：「昔陛下在周，與永富公竇榮定語，臣曰：'我聞有行聲，即識其人。

translations.literal: At the end of Kaihuang, He submitted a memorial recounting what he had said while the emperor was still in obscurity: 'Formerly, when Your Majesty was still under Zhou, you spoke with Duke Yongfu Dou Rongding, and I said: 'I hear a man's gait and know the man.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of Kaihuang, He submitted a memorial recounting what he had said while the emperor was still obscure: 'Formerly, when Your Majesty was still under Zhou, you spoke with Duke Yongfu Dou Rongding, and I said, 'I hear a man's gait and know the man.

sentences.zh: 臣當時即言：'公眼如曙星，無所不照，當王有天下，願忍誅殺。

translations.literal: I then said at once: 'Your eyes are like dawn stars, seeing all without omission; you will reign and possess the realm—may you restrain killing.
translations.idiomatic: I then said at once, 'Your eyes are like dawn stars, missing nothing; you will reign over the realm—may you restrain killing.

sentences.zh: 建德四年五月，周武帝在雲陽宮謂臣曰：'諸公皆汝所識，隋公相祿何如？'

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the fourth year of Jiande, Emperor Wu of Zhou at Yunyang Palace said to me: 'The lords are all men you know—how is Duke Sui's fortune and emolument?'
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the fourth year of Jiande, Emperor Wu of Zhou at Yunyang Palace said to me, 'The lords are all men you know—how is Duke Sui's fortune and emolument?'

sentences.zh: 臣報武帝曰：'隋公止是守節人，可鎮一方，若為將領，陣無不破。'

translations.literal: I replied to Emperor Wu: 'Duke Sui is only a man who keeps his integrity; he can secure one region. If made a general, no battle line will not be broken.'
translations.idiomatic: I replied to Emperor Wu, 'Duke Sui is only a man of integrity; he can hold one region. As a general, no battle line will stand against him.'

sentences.zh: 臣即于宮東南奏聞，陛下謂臣：'此語不忘。'

translations.literal: I then reported this at the southeast of the palace; Your Majesty told me: 'Do not forget these words.'
translations.idiomatic: I then reported this at the southeast of the palace; Your Majesty told me, 'Do not forget these words.'

sentences.zh: 明年，烏丸軌言于武帝曰：'隋公非人臣。'

translations.literal: The next year Wuhuan Gui said to Emperor Wu: 'Duke Sui is no ordinary subject.'
translations.idiomatic: The next year Wuhuan Gui said to Emperor Wu, 'Duke Sui is no ordinary subject.'

sentences.zh: '帝尋以問臣。

translations.literal: The emperor soon asked me.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor soon asked me.

sentences.zh: 臣知帝有疑，臣詭報曰：'是節臣，更無異相。

translations.literal: Knowing the emperor had doubts, I falsely replied: 'He is a minister of integrity; there is no other unusual sign.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing the emperor had doubts, I falsely replied, 'He is a loyal minister; there is no other unusual sign.

sentences.zh: '于時王誼、梁彥光等知臣此語。

translations.literal: At that time Wang Yi, Liang Yanguang, and others knew I had said this.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Wang Yi, Liang Yanguang, and others knew I had said this.

sentences.zh: 大象二年五月，至尊從永巷東門入，臣在永巷門東，北面立，陛下問臣曰：'我得無災鄣不？

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the second year of Daxiang, the Supreme One entered through the east gate of the Everlasting Lane; I stood north of the east gate of the Everlasting Lane, and Your Majesty asked me: 'Will I be free of calamity?
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the second year of Daxiang, the Supreme One entered through the east gate of the Everlasting Lane; I stood north of the east gate of the Everlasting Lane, and Your Majesty asked me, 'Will I be free of calamity?

sentences.zh: 臣奏陛下曰：'公骨法氣色相應，天命已有付屬。

translations.literal: I reported to Your Majesty: 'Your bone structure and vital aura correspond; heaven's mandate has already been entrusted.
translations.idiomatic: I reported to Your Majesty, 'Your bone structure and vital aura correspond; heaven's mandate has already been entrusted to you.

sentences.zh: '未幾，遂總百揆。」

translations.literal: Before long, he came to direct all ministerial affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, he was put in charge of all the ministries.

sentences.zh: 上覽之大悅，進位開府。

translations.literal: The Emperor read it and was greatly pleased, and promoted him to Establishment Grand Master.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor read the memorial and was greatly pleased, promoting Lai He to Establishment Grand Master.

sentences.zh: 和同郡韓則嘗詣和相，和謂之：「後四五當得大官。」

translations.literal: Han Ze of Tonghe commandery once came to Lai He for a physiognomic reading. Lai He told him: 'In four or five [units of time] you will obtain a great office.
translations.idiomatic: Han Ze of Tonghe commandery once had Lai He read his fortune. Lai He told him, "In four or five you will obtain a great office.

sentences.zh: 人初不知所謂。

translations.literal: At first people did not understand what he meant.
translations.idiomatic: At first no one understood what he meant.

sentences.zh: 則至開皇十五年五月終。

translations.literal: Han Ze died in the fifth month of the fifteenth year of Kaihuang.
translations.idiomatic: Han Ze died in the fifth month of Kaihuang 15.

sentences.zh: 人問其故，和曰：「十五年為三五，加以五月為四五。

translations.literal: When people asked the reason, Lai He said: 'Fifteen years is "three-five," and adding the fifth month makes "four-five.
translations.idiomatic: When people asked how he had known, Lai He said, "Fifteen years is 'three-five,' and with the fifth month added that makes 'four-five.

sentences.zh: 大官，槨也。」

translations.literal: Great office means a coffin."
translations.idiomatic: A great office meant a coffin."

sentences.zh: 和言多此類。

translations.literal: Lai He's remarks were often of this sort.
translations.idiomatic: Lai He's predictions were often of this kind.

sentences.zh: 著《相經》三十卷。

translations.literal: He authored the Physiognomy Classic in thirty scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote the Physiognomy Classic in thirty scrolls.

sentences.zh: 道士張賓、焦子順、應門人董子華等，此三人當文帝龍潛時，並私謂帝曰：「公當為天子，善自愛。」

translations.literal: The Daoists Zhang Bin, Jiao Zishun, and Dong Zihua, a disciple from Ying Gate — when Emperor Wen was still in obscurity before enthronement, all three privately told him: 'You are destined to become Son of Heaven. Take good care of yourself.
translations.idiomatic: The Daoists Zhang Bin and Jiao Zishun, together with Dong Zihua, a disciple from Ying Gate — while Emperor Wen was still in obscurity before taking the throne, all three privately told him, "You are destined to become emperor. Guard yourself well.

sentences.zh: 及踐位，以賓為華州刺史，子順為開府，子華為上儀同。

translations.literal: When he ascended the throne, he appointed Zhang Bin governor of Huazhou, Jiao Zishun Establishment Grand Master, and Dong Zihua Superlative Companion of the First Rank.
translations.idiomatic: When he took the throne, he made Zhang Bin governor of Huazhou, Jiao Zishun Establishment Grand Master, and Dong Zihua Superlative Companion of the First Rank.

sentences.zh: 蕭吉，字文休，梁武帝兄長沙宣武王懿之孫也。

translations.literal: Xiao Ji, courtesy name Wenxiu, was a grandson of Xiao Yi, Prince Xuanwu of Changsha, elder brother of Emperor Wu of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Ji, courtesy name Wenxiu, was a grandson of Xiao Yi, Prince Xuanwu of Changsha and elder brother of Emperor Wu of Liang.

sentences.zh: 博學多通，尤精陰陽、算術。

translations.literal: Learned and broadly skilled, he was especially expert in yin-yang theory and mathematics.
translations.idiomatic: He was learned and widely accomplished, and especially skilled in yin-yang lore and mathematical arts.

sentences.zh: 江陵覆亡，歸於魏，為儀同。

translations.literal: When Jiangling fell, he submitted to Wei and was made Companion of the Imperial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: After the fall of Jiangling he submitted to Northern Wei and was made a Companion of the Imperial Guard.

sentences.zh: 周宣帝時，吉以朝政日亂，上書切諫，帝不納。

translations.literal: During the reign of Emperor Xuan of Zhou, Xiao Ji, seeing court affairs daily falling into disorder, submitted a memorial of sharp remonstrance, but the emperor did not accept it.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Xuan of Northern Zhou, seeing the court daily sink into disorder, Xiao Ji submitted a forceful memorial of remonstrance, but the emperor would not heed it.

sentences.zh: 及隋受禪，進上儀同，以本官太常，考定古今陰陽書。

translations.literal: When Sui received the abdication, he was promoted to Superlative Companion of the First Rank and, retaining his post as Minister of Ceremonies, was assigned to examine and establish yin-yang texts ancient and modern.
translations.idiomatic: When Sui received the abdication, he was promoted to Superlative Companion of the First Rank and, while continuing as Minister of Ceremonies, was charged with collating yin-yang texts old and new.

sentences.zh: 吉性孤峭，不與公卿相浮沈，又與楊素不協，由是擯落，鬱鬱不得志。

translations.literal: Xiao Ji was by nature aloof and austere; he did not mingle with the great officials, and he also did not get along with Yang Su. Because of this he was pushed aside and sank into dejection without achieving his ambitions.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Ji was by nature solitary and stern; he would not rise and fall with the high ministers, and he also fell out with Yang Su. Pushed aside for this, he languished in frustration.

sentences.zh: 見上好徵祥之說，欲乾沒自進，遂矯其跡為悅媚焉。

translations.literal: Seeing that the emperor favored omens of good fortune, he wished to scheme his way to advancement and so altered his bearing to one of flattery and sycophancy.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing that the emperor delighted in auspicious portents, he sought to advance himself by scheming and so reshaped his manner into one of fawning compliance.

sentences.zh: 開皇十四年，上書曰：「今年歲在甲寅，十一月朔旦，以辛酉為冬至。

translations.literal: In Kaihuang 14 he submitted a memorial saying: 'This year the year-stem is jiayin. On the first day of the eleventh month, xinyou will be the winter solstice.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaihuang 14 he submitted a memorial saying, "This year is jiayin. On the first day of the eleventh month, xinyou falls on the winter solstice.

sentences.zh: 來年乙卯，正月朔旦，以庚申為元日。

translations.literal: Next year, yimao, on the first day of the first month, gengshen will be New Year's Day.
translations.idiomatic: Next year, yimao, on the first day of the first month, gengshen will be New Year's Day.

sentences.zh: 冬至之日，即在朔旦。

translations.literal: The day of the winter solstice falls precisely on the first day of the month.
translations.idiomatic: The winter solstice falls on the very first day of the month.

sentences.zh: 《樂汁圖征》云：'天元十二月朔旦冬至，聖王受享祚。

translations.literal: The Music Juice Chart Prognostications says: 'When in the first month of Heaven's origin the first day of the month is also the winter solstice, the sage king receives the mandate and enjoys the throne.'
translations.idiomatic: The Music Juice Chart Prognostications says, "When Heaven's origin month has its new moon on the winter solstice, the sage king receives the mandate and enjoys long reign."

sentences.zh: '今聖主在位，居天元之首，而朔旦冬至，此慶一也。

translations.literal: Now the sacred sovereign holds the throne, standing at the head of Heaven's origin, and the first day of the month coincides with the winter solstice. This is the first felicity.
translations.idiomatic: Now the sacred sovereign reigns at the head of Heaven's origin, and the new moon coincides with the winter solstice — this is the first blessing.

sentences.zh: 辛酉之日，即至尊本命。

translations.literal: The day xinyou is precisely Your Majesty's natal day.
translations.idiomatic: The day xinyou is precisely Your Majesty's birth day.

sentences.zh: 辛德在丙，此十一月建丙子，酉德在寅，正月建寅，為本命與月合德，而居元朔之首，此慶二也。

translations.literal: The virtue of xin rests in bing; this eleventh month is established at bingzi; the virtue of you rests in yin; the first month is established at yin — the natal day and the month join in virtue and stand at the head of the year's new moon. This is the second felicity.
translations.idiomatic: Xin's virtue lies in bing, and the eleventh month is established at bingzi; you's virtue lies in yin, and the first month is established at yin — so the natal day and the month unite in virtue and stand at the year's new moon. This is the second blessing.

sentences.zh: 庚申之日，即是行年。

translations.literal: The day gengshen is precisely the year of personal fortune.
translations.idiomatic: The day gengshen is precisely the year of personal fortune.

sentences.zh: 乙德在庚，卯德在申，來年乙卯，是行年與歲合德，而在元旦之朝，此慶三也。

translations.literal: The virtue of yi rests in geng; the virtue of mao rests in shen; next year yimao is the year of personal fortune joining in virtue with the year, and it falls on the morning of New Year's Day. This is the third felicity.
translations.idiomatic: Yi's virtue lies in geng, and mao's in shen; next year yimao is the year when personal fortune joins the year's virtue on the morning of New Year's Day. This is the third blessing.

sentences.zh: 《陰陽書》云：'年命與歲月合德者，必有福慶。

translations.literal: The Book of Yin and Yang says: 'When the year of destiny joins in virtue with the year and month, there must be blessing and felicity.'
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Yin and Yang says, "When the year of destiny joins in virtue with the year and month, blessing must follow."

sentences.zh: '《洪範傳》云：'歲之朝，月之朝，日之朝，主王者。

translations.literal: The Tradition of the Great Plan says: 'When the year, the month, and the day all begin together, the ruler is a true king.'
translations.idiomatic: The Tradition of the Great Plan says, "When year, month, and day all begin together, the ruler is a true king."

sentences.zh: '經書並謂三長，應之者，延年福吉。

translations.literal: The classics all call these the Three Beginnings; he who meets them enjoys prolonged life and auspicious fortune.
translations.idiomatic: The classics all call these the Three Beginnings; whoever meets them gains long life and good fortune.

sentences.zh: 況乃甲寅，蔀首；

translations.literal: Moreover, jiayin is the head of a sexagenary cycle section;
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, jiayin is the head of a sexagenary cycle;

sentences.zh: 十一月，陽之始；

translations.literal: the eleventh month is the beginning of yang;
translations.idiomatic: the eleventh month is where yang begins;

sentences.zh: 朔旦冬至，是聖王上元。

translations.literal: the new moon on the winter solstice is the Upper Origin of the sage king.
translations.idiomatic: a new moon on the winter solstice is the sage king's Upper Origin.

sentences.zh: 正月，是正陽之月，歲之首，月之先；

translations.literal: The first month is the month of true yang, the head of the year and the foremost of months;
translations.idiomatic: The first month is the month of true yang, the head of the year and first among months;

sentences.zh: 朔旦是歲之元，月之朝，日之先，嘉辰之會。

translations.literal: the new moon is the origin of the year, the beginning of the month, and the first of days — a meeting of auspicious seasons.
translations.idiomatic: its new moon is the origin of the year, the beginning of the month, and the first of days — a convergence of auspicious seasons.

sentences.zh: 而本命為九元之先，行年為三長之首，並與歲月合德。

translations.literal: The natal day is foremost among the Nine Origins, and the year of personal fortune is head among the Three Beginnings; both join in virtue with the year and month.
translations.idiomatic: The natal day stands first among the Nine Origins, and the year of personal fortune heads the Three Beginnings; both unite in virtue with the year and month.

sentences.zh: 所以《靈寶經》云：'角音龍精，其祚曰強。

translations.literal: Therefore the Scripture of the Numinous Treasure says: 'The jiao pitch is dragon essence; its reign is called strong.'
translations.idiomatic: Thus the Scripture of the Numinous Treasure says, "The jiao pitch is dragon essence; its reign is called strong."

sentences.zh: '來歲年命，納音俱角，曆之與經，如合符契。

translations.literal: Next year's year of destiny and received pitch are both jiao; the calendar and the classic accord like matching tally halves.
translations.idiomatic: Next year's year of destiny and received pitch are both jiao; calendar and classic align like matching tally halves.

sentences.zh: 又甲寅、乙卯，天地合也。

translations.literal: Moreover, jiayin and yimao are Heaven-and-Earth union.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, jiayin and yimao form Heaven-and-Earth union.

sentences.zh: 甲寅之年，以辛酉冬至；

translations.literal: In the jiayin year, xinyou is the winter solstice;
translations.idiomatic: In the jiayin year, the winter solstice falls on xinyou;

sentences.zh: 來年乙卯，以甲子夏至。

translations.literal: next year yimao has jiazi as the summer solstice.
translations.idiomatic: next year yimao has jiazi as the summer solstice.

sentences.zh: 冬至陽始，郊天之日，即是至尊本命，此慶四也。

translations.literal: The winter solstice is where yang begins and the day of suburban sacrifice to Heaven — it is precisely Your Majesty's natal day. This is the fourth felicity.
translations.idiomatic: The winter solstice, when yang begins and Heaven is sacrificed to at the suburbs, falls on Your Majesty's natal day — this is the fourth blessing.

sentences.zh: 夏至陰始，祀地之辰，即是皇后本命，此慶五也。

translations.literal: The summer solstice is where yin begins and the time of sacrifice to Earth — it is precisely the empress's natal day. This is the fifth felicity.
translations.idiomatic: The summer solstice, when yin begins and Earth is sacrificed to, falls on the empress's natal day — this is the fifth blessing.

sentences.zh: 至尊德並乾之覆育，皇后仁同地之載養，所以二儀元氣，並會本辰。」

translations.literal: Your Majesty's virtue matches Heaven's nurturing canopy, and the empress's benevolence equals Earth's sustaining burden; thus the primordial qi of the Two Powers both meet at their natal days.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty's virtue matches Heaven's sheltering canopy, and the empress's benevolence equals Earth's sustaining load; thus the primordial qi of the Two Powers both converge on their natal days.

sentences.zh: 上覽之悅，賜物五百段。

translations.literal: The emperor read it with pleasure and bestowed five hundred bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor read the memorial with pleasure and rewarded him with five hundred bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 房陵王時為太子，言東宮多鬼魅，鼠妖數見。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Fangling was heir apparent, he said the Eastern Palace was full of ghosts and demons, and rat apparitions appeared repeatedly.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Fangling was crown prince, he reported that the Eastern Palace swarmed with ghosts and demons and that rat omens appeared again and again.

sentences.zh: 上令吉詣東宮禳邪氣。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Xiao Ji to go to the Eastern Palace to exorcise evil qi.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Xiao Ji to the Eastern Palace to drive out evil influences.

sentences.zh: 于宣慈殿設神坐，有回風從艮地鬼門來，掃太子坐。

translations.literal: At Xuanci Hall he set up spirit seats, and a returning wind came from the ghost gate in the gen direction, sweeping across the heir's seat.
translations.idiomatic: At Xuanci Hall he set up spirit seats, and a returning wind came from the ghost gate in the northeast, sweeping across the crown prince's seat.

sentences.zh: 吉以桃湯葦火驅逐之，風出宮門而止。

translations.literal: Xiao Ji used peach broth and reed fire to drive it away; the wind went out through the palace gate and stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Ji drove it off with peach broth and reed fire; the wind passed out the palace gate and ceased.

sentences.zh: 謝土於未地，設壇為四門，置五帝坐。

translations.literal: He performed the rite of thanking the earth at the wei direction, setting up an altar with four gates and placing seats for the Five Emperors.
translations.idiomatic: He performed the rite of thanking the earth in the southwest, setting up an altar with four gates and placing seats for the Five Emperors.

sentences.zh: 于時寒，有蝦蟆從西南來，入人門，升赤帝坐，還從人門而出，行數步，忽然不見。

translations.literal: It was then cold, yet a toad came from the southwest, entered the human gate, climbed the seat of the Red Emperor, then went back out through the human gate; after several paces it suddenly vanished.
translations.idiomatic: Though it was cold, a toad came from the southwest, entered the human gate, climbed the Red Emperor's seat, then went back out through the human gate; after a few steps it suddenly vanished.

sentences.zh: 上大異之，賞賜優洽。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly astonished and rewarded him generously.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was deeply astonished and rewarded him with exceptional generosity.

sentences.zh: 又上言：太子當不安位。

translations.literal: He also submitted that the heir apparent would not long keep his position.
translations.idiomatic: He also submitted that the crown prince would not long retain his position.

sentences.zh: 時上陰欲廢立，得其言，是之。

translations.literal: At the time the emperor secretly wished to depose and replace him; obtaining this statement, he approved it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor already secretly wished to depose and replace him; hearing this, he took it as confirmation.

sentences.zh: 由此，每被顧問。

translations.literal: From this he was frequently consulted.
translations.idiomatic: After this he was frequently summoned for counsel.

sentences.zh: 及獻皇后崩，上令吉卜擇葬所。

translations.literal: When Empress Xian died, the emperor ordered Xiao Ji to divinely select a burial site.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Xian died, the emperor ordered Xiao Ji to choose a burial site by divination.

sentences.zh: 吉曆筮山原，至一處，云：「卜年二千，卜世二百。」

translations.literal: Xiao Ji surveyed hills and plains by calendar and milfoil, and at one place said: 'A divination of two thousand years, a divination of two hundred reigns.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Ji surveyed hills and plains by calendar and milfoil, and at one spot said, "I divined two thousand years and two hundred reigns.

sentences.zh: 具圖而奏之。

translations.literal: He drew a map and submitted it.
translations.idiomatic: He drew a map and presented it to the throne.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「吉凶由人，不在於地。

translations.literal: The emperor said: 'Fortune and misfortune depend on men, not on the ground.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Good and ill fortune depend on men, not on the ground.

sentences.zh: 高緯父葬，豈不卜乎？

translations.literal: When Gao Wei's father was buried, did he not divinely select a site?
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Wei's father was buried, did they not choose the site by divination?

sentences.zh: 國尋滅亡。

translations.literal: Yet the state was soon destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the state was soon destroyed.

sentences.zh: 正如我家墓田，若雲不吉，朕不當為天子；

translations.literal: It is just like the tomb fields of my own house: if one says they are inauspicious, I ought not to have become emperor;
translations.idiomatic: It is like the tomb fields of my own clan: if they were inauspicious, I ought not to have become emperor;

sentences.zh: 若雲不凶，我弟不當戰沒。」

translations.literal: if one says they are not inauspicious, my younger brother ought not to have died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: if they were not inauspicious, my younger brother ought not to have fallen in battle.

sentences.zh: 然竟從吉言。

translations.literal: Yet in the end he followed Xiao Ji's words.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in the end he followed Xiao Ji's recommendation.

sentences.zh: 表曰：「去月十六日，皇后山陵西北，雞未鳴前，有黑雲方圓五六百步，從地屬天；

translations.literal: In a memorial he said: 'On the sixteenth of last month, before the cock crow at the empress's mausoleum in the northwest, a black cloud four or five hundred paces square rose from earth to heaven;
translations.idiomatic: In a memorial he said, "On the sixteenth of last month, before cockcrow at the empress's mausoleum in the northwest, a black cloud four or five hundred paces square rose from earth to heaven;

sentences.zh: 東南又有旌旗、車馬、帳幕，佈滿七八里，並有人往來檢校，部伍甚整。

translations.literal: to the southeast there were also banners, chariots, horses, and tents spread over seven or eight li, with people going back and forth inspecting them in very orderly ranks.
translations.idiomatic: to the southeast there were also banners, chariots, horses, and tents spread over seven or eight li, with people going back and forth to inspect them in very orderly ranks.

sentences.zh: 日出乃滅。

translations.literal: At sunrise it vanished.
translations.idiomatic: At sunrise it vanished.

sentences.zh: 同見者十餘人。

translations.literal: More than ten people saw it together.
translations.idiomatic: More than ten people witnessed it together.

sentences.zh: 謹案《葬書》云'氣王與姓相生，大吉，今黑氣當冬王，與姓相生，是大吉利，子孫無疆之候也。」

translations.literal: According to the Book of Burial, 'When the qi is strong and joins in generation with the surname, it is greatly auspicious.' Now the black qi corresponds to winter's strength and joins in generation with the surname — this is a sign of great fortune and boundless posterity.
translations.idiomatic: According to the Book of Burial, 'When the qi is strong and generates with the surname, the omen is greatly auspicious.' Now the black qi corresponds to winter's strength and generates with the surname — a sign of great fortune and boundless posterity.

sentences.zh: 上大悅。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was greatly pleased.

sentences.zh: 其後上將親臨發殯，吉復奏曰：「至尊本命辛酉，今歲斗魁及天岡臨卯酉，謹案《陰陽書》，不得臨喪。」

translations.literal: Later, when the emperor was about to attend the empress's funeral procession in person, Xiao Ji again submitted: 'Your Majesty's natal day is xinyou. This year the Dipper's head and the celestial ridge stand over mao and you. According to the Book of Yin and Yang, one must not attend a funeral.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when the emperor was about to attend the empress's funeral in person, Xiao Ji submitted again, "Your Majesty's natal day is xinyou. This year the Dipper's head and the celestial ridge stand over mao and you. According to the Book of Yin and Yang, you must not attend a funeral.

sentences.zh: 上不納。

translations.literal: The emperor did not accept it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor would not heed him.

sentences.zh: 退而告族人蕭平仲曰：「皇太子遣宇文左率深謝餘云：'公前稱我當為太子，竟有驗，終不忘也。

translations.literal: Withdrawn, he told his clansman Xiao Pingzhong: 'The heir apparent sent the Left Leader of the Palace Guard Yuwen to express deep thanks on his behalf, saying: "You previously said I would become heir apparent, and it has indeed come true — I shall never forget it.
translations.idiomatic: Withdrawn, he told his clansman Xiao Pingzhong, "The crown prince sent the Left Leader of the Palace Guard Yuwen to express deep thanks on his behalf, saying, 'You once said I would become crown prince, and it has indeed come true — I shall never forget it.

sentences.zh: 今卜山陵，務令我早立。

translations.literal: Now in choosing the mausoleum site, see that I am established early.
translations.idiomatic: Now in choosing the mausoleum site, see that I am established soon.

sentences.zh: 我立之後，當以富貴相報。

translations.literal: After I am established, I shall repay you with wealth and honor.
translations.idiomatic: After I am established, I shall repay you with wealth and honor.

sentences.zh: '吾記之曰：'後四載，太子禦天下。

translations.literal: I noted in reply: 'Four years hence the heir apparent will rule All Under Heaven.'
translations.idiomatic: I noted in reply, 'Four years hence the crown prince will rule All Under Heaven.

sentences.zh: '今山陵氣應，上又臨喪，兆益見矣。

translations.literal: Now the mausoleum qi has responded, and the emperor again attends the funeral — the omen is clearer still.
translations.idiomatic: Now the mausoleum qi has responded, and the emperor again attends the funeral — the omen is clearer still.

sentences.zh: 且太子得政，隋其亡乎！

translations.literal: And if the heir apparent takes power, will Sui not perish?
translations.idiomatic: And if the crown prince takes power, will Sui not perish?

sentences.zh: 當有真人出矣。

translations.literal: A true lord will appear.
translations.idiomatic: A true lord will appear.

sentences.zh: 吾前紿雲'卜年二千'者，是三十字也；

translations.literal: What I previously deceived you by saying, 'a divination of two thousand years,' means the characters 'three' and 'ten' — thirty;
translations.idiomatic: What I previously deceived you by saying 'a divination of two thousand years' meant was the characters 'three' and 'ten' — thirty;

sentences.zh: '卜世二百者'，取世二運也。

translations.literal: a divination of two hundred reigns' takes 'reign' and 'two cycles.
translations.idiomatic: a divination of two hundred reigns' took 'reign' and 'two cycles.

sentences.zh: 吾言信矣，汝其志之。」

translations.literal: My words are trustworthy — keep them in mind.'
translations.idiomatic: My words are trustworthy — remember them."

sentences.zh: 及煬帝嗣位，拜太府少卿，加位開府。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang succeeded to the throne, Xiao Ji was appointed Vice Minister of the Palace Storehouse and additionally given the rank of Establishment Grand Master.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang succeeded to the throne, Xiao Ji was made Vice Minister of the Palace Storehouse with the additional rank of Establishment Grand Master.

sentences.zh: 嘗行經華陰，見楊素塚上有白氣屬天，密言於帝。

translations.literal: Once, passing Huayin, he saw white qi above Yang Su's tomb reaching to heaven, and secretly told the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Once, passing Huayin, he saw white qi above Yang Su's tomb reaching to heaven and secretly reported it to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 帝問其故，吉曰：「其候，素家當有兵禍，滅門之象。

translations.literal: The emperor asked the reason. Xiao Ji said: 'The omen is that Yang Su's house will suffer military calamity — the sign of extermination of the clan.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked what it meant. Xiao Ji said, "The omen is that Yang Su's house will suffer military calamity — the sign of clan extermination.

sentences.zh: 改葬者，庶可免乎！」

translations.literal: By reburial one might perhaps escape it!
translations.idiomatic: By reburial one might perhaps escape it!

sentences.zh: 帝后從容謂楊玄感曰：「公宜早改葬。」

translations.literal: The emperor later told Yang Xuangan at leisure: 'You ought to move the tomb early.'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor later told Yang Xuangan privately, "You ought to move the tomb soon."

sentences.zh: 玄感亦微知其故，以為吉祥，托以遼東未滅，不遑私門之事。

translations.literal: Xuangan also faintly knew the reason and, taking it as an auspicious sign, pleaded that Liaodong was not yet pacified and he had no leisure for private family affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Xuangan also had some inkling of the reason and, taking it as a good omen, pleaded that Liaodong was not yet pacified and he had no time for private family matters.

sentences.zh: 未幾而玄感以反族滅，帝彌信之。

translations.literal: Before long Xuangan rebelled and his clan was exterminated; the emperor believed Xiao Ji all the more.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Xuangan rebelled and his clan was exterminated; the emperor believed in Xiao Ji all the more.

sentences.zh: 後歲餘卒官。

translations.literal: More than a year later he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: A little over a year later he died in office.

sentences.zh: 著《金海》三十卷，《相經要錄》一卷，《宅經》八卷，《葬經》六卷，《樂譜》二十卷，及《帝王養生方》二卷，《相手版要決》一卷，《太一立成》一卷，並行于時。

translations.literal: He authored Golden Sea in thirty scrolls, Essentials of the Physiognomy Classic in one scroll, Classic of Dwellings in eight scrolls, Classic of Burial in six scrolls, Music Scores in twenty scrolls, and also Prescriptions for Nourishing the Life of Emperors in two scrolls, Essential Decisions on Reading Palm Plates in one scroll, and Establishment of the Grand Unity in one scroll — all circulated in his time.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote Golden Sea in thirty scrolls, Essentials of the Physiognomy Classic in one scroll, Classic of Dwellings in eight scrolls, Classic of Burial in six scrolls, Music Scores in twenty scrolls, Prescriptions for Nourishing the Life of Emperors in two scrolls, Essential Decisions on Reading Palm Plates in one scroll, and Establishment of the Grand Unity in one scroll — all of which circulated in his day.

sentences.zh: 楊伯醜，馮翊武鄉人也。

translations.literal: Yang Bochou was a native of Wuxiang in Fengyi.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Bochou was a native of Wuxiang in Fengyi.

sentences.zh: 好讀《易》，隱于華山。

translations.literal: He loved to read the Changes and lived in seclusion on Mount Hua.
translations.idiomatic: He loved to read the Changes and lived in seclusion on Mount Hua.

sentences.zh: 隋開皇初，征入朝，見公卿不為禮，無貴賤皆汝之，人不能測也。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaihuang in Sui he was summoned to court; seeing the great officials he made no courtesy, and addressed all without distinction of rank with 'you' — no one could fathom him.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Sui's Kaihuang era he was summoned to court; he showed no courtesy to the great officials and addressed everyone, high or low, as "you" — no one could fathom him.

sentences.zh: 文帝召與語，竟無所答。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen summoned him to converse, but he answered nothing at all.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen summoned him to talk, but he answered not a word.

sentences.zh: 賜衣服，至朝堂舍之而去。

translations.literal: Given clothes, he cast them off in the court hall and left.
translations.idiomatic: Given clothes, he cast them off in the court hall and walked away.

sentences.zh: 於是被髮陽狂，遊行市里，形體垢穢，未嘗櫛沐。

translations.literal: Thereafter he let his hair hang loose in feigned madness and wandered through the market streets, his body filthy, never combing or bathing.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter he let his hair hang loose in feigned madness and wandered the market streets, filthy and never combing or bathing.

sentences.zh: 時有張永樂者，賣卜京師，伯醜每從之遊。

translations.literal: At the time there was a Zhang Yongle who sold divinations in the capital; Bochou often accompanied him.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Zhang Yongle sold divinations in the capital, and Bochou often kept company with him.

sentences.zh: 永樂為卦有不能決者，伯醜輒為分析爻象，尋幽入微，永樂嗟服，自以為非所及也。

translations.literal: When Yongle cast hexagrams he sometimes could not decide; Bochou would analyze the lines and images, probing hidden depths to the finest point, and Yongle sighed in admiration, acknowledging he could not match him.
translations.idiomatic: When Yongle cast hexagrams he sometimes could not decide; Bochou would analyze the lines and images, probing hidden depths to the finest point. Yongle sighed in admiration and acknowledged he could not match him.

sentences.zh: 伯醜亦開肆賣卜。

translations.literal: Bochou also opened a shop selling divinations.
translations.idiomatic: Bochou also opened a shop selling divinations.

sentences.zh: 有人嘗失子就伯醜筮者。

translations.literal: Once a man who had lost his child came to Bochou for divination.
translations.idiomatic: Once a man who had lost his child came to Bochou for divination.

sentences.zh: 卦成，伯醜曰：「汝子在懷遠坊南門東，道北壁上有青裙女子抱之，可往取也。」

translations.literal: When the hexagram was complete, Bochou said: 'Your child is east of the south gate of Huaiyuan Ward, on the north side of the road, in the arms of a woman in a blue skirt — you may go and fetch him.
translations.idiomatic: When the hexagram was complete, Bochou said, "Your child is east of the south gate of Huaiyuan Ward, on the north side of the road, in the arms of a woman in a blue skirt — go and fetch him.

sentences.zh: 如言，果得。

translations.literal: As he said, the child was indeed recovered.
translations.idiomatic: It was exactly as he said, and the child was recovered.

sentences.zh: 或有金數兩，夫妻共藏之，于後失金，其夫意妻有異志，將逐之。

translations.literal: Once a couple had several taels of gold which they hid together; afterward the gold was lost, and the husband suspected his wife of unfaithful intent and was about to drive her away.
translations.idiomatic: Once a couple had several taels of gold which they hid together; later the gold was lost, and the husband suspected his wife of unfaithful intent and was about to drive her away.

sentences.zh: 其妻稱冤，以詣伯醜。

translations.literal: His wife proclaimed her innocence and went to Bochou.
translations.idiomatic: His wife proclaimed her innocence and went to Bochou.

sentences.zh: 伯醜為之筮：「金在矣。」

translations.literal: Bochou divined for her: 'The gold is still here.
translations.idiomatic: Bochou divined for her: "The gold is still here.

sentences.zh: 悉呼其家人，指一人曰：「可就取。」

translations.literal: He called in all the members of the household, pointed to one, and said: 'You may go and take it.'
translations.idiomatic: He called in all the members of the household, pointed to one, and said, "You may go and take it."

sentences.zh: 果得之。

translations.literal: The gold was indeed recovered.
translations.idiomatic: The gold was indeed recovered.

sentences.zh: 又將軍許知常問吉凶，伯醜曰：「汝勿東北行。

translations.literal: Again, the general Xu Zhichang asked about fortune and misfortune. Bochou said: 'Do not go northeast.
translations.idiomatic: Again, the general Xu Zhichang asked about fortune and misfortune. Bochou said, "Do not go northeast.

sentences.zh: 必不得已，當速還。

translations.literal: If you cannot avoid it, return quickly.
translations.idiomatic: If you cannot avoid it, return quickly.

sentences.zh: 不然者，楊素斬汝頭。」

translations.literal: Otherwise Yang Su will cut off your head.
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise Yang Su will cut off your head.

sentences.zh: 未幾，上令知常事漢王諒。

translations.literal: Before long the emperor ordered Zhichang to serve Prince Han Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the emperor ordered Zhichang to serve Prince Han Liang.

sentences.zh: 俄而上崩，諒舉兵反，知常逃歸京師。

translations.literal: Soon the emperor died; Liang raised troops in rebellion, and Zhichang fled back to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the emperor died; Liang raised troops in rebellion, and Zhichang fled back to the capital.

sentences.zh: 知常先與楊素有隙，及素平并州，先訪知常，將斬之，賴此獲免。

translations.literal: Zhichang had earlier been at odds with Yang Su; when Su pacified Bingzhou he sought out Zhichang and was about to behead him — only because of this did he escape.
translations.idiomatic: Zhichang had earlier been at odds with Yang Su; when Su pacified Bingzhou he sought out Zhichang and was about to behead him — only because of this warning did he escape.

sentences.zh: 又有人失馬來詣伯醜卜者，時伯醜為皇太子所召，在途遇之，立為作卦。

translations.literal: Again, a man who had lost a horse came to Bochou for divination. At the time Bochou had been summoned by the crown prince and, meeting the man on the road, stopped to cast a hexagram for him.
translations.idiomatic: Again, a man who had lost a horse came to Bochou for divination. Bochou had been summoned by the crown prince and, meeting the man on the road, stopped to cast a hexagram for him.

sentences.zh: 卦成，曰：「我不遑為卿說，且向西市東壁門南第三店，為我買魚作鱠，當得馬矣。」

translations.literal: When the hexagram was complete he said: 'I have no leisure to explain to you. Go to the third shop south of the east wall gate in the western market and buy fish to make sliced raw fish for me — then you will recover your horse.
translations.idiomatic: When the hexagram was complete he said, "I have no leisure to explain. Go to the third shop south of the east wall gate in the western market and buy fish to make sliced raw fish for me — then you will recover your horse.

sentences.zh: 其人如教，須臾，有一人牽所失馬而至，遂禽之。

translations.literal: The man did as instructed; before long someone leading the lost horse came along, and he seized it.
translations.idiomatic: The man did as instructed; before long someone leading the lost horse came along, and he seized it.

sentences.zh: 崖州嘗獻徑寸珠，其使者陰易之，上心疑焉，召伯醜令筮。

translations.literal: Ya Prefecture once presented a large pearl; its envoy secretly substituted another, and the emperor's heart was suspicious. He summoned Bochou to divination.
translations.idiomatic: Ya Prefecture once presented a large pearl; its envoy secretly substituted another, and the emperor grew suspicious. He summoned Bochou to divine the matter.

sentences.zh: 伯醜曰：「有物出自水中，質圓而色光，是大珠也。

translations.literal: Bochou said: 'There is an object that came from the water, round in substance and bright in color — it is a great pearl.
translations.idiomatic: Bochou said, "There is an object that came from the water, round in substance and bright in color — it is a great pearl.

sentences.zh: 今為人所隱。」

translations.literal: Now it is hidden by someone.
translations.idiomatic: Now it is hidden by someone.

sentences.zh: 且言隱者姓名、容狀。

translations.literal: He also gave the name and appearance of the person hiding it.
translations.idiomatic: He also gave the name and appearance of the person hiding it.

sentences.zh: 上如言簿責之，果得本珠，上奇之，賜帛二十匹。

translations.literal: The emperor questioned the man as described and indeed recovered the original pearl; astonished, he bestowed twenty bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor questioned the man as described and indeed recovered the original pearl; astonished, he bestowed twenty bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 國子祭酒何妥嘗詣之論《易》。

translations.literal: He Tuo, Director of the Imperial Academy, once came to discuss the Changes with him.
translations.idiomatic: He Tuo, Director of the Imperial Academy, once came to discuss the Changes with him.

sentences.zh: 聞妥之言，悠爾而笑曰：「何用鄭玄、王弼之言乎？」

translations.literal: Hearing Tuo's words, he smiled leisurely and said: 'What use are the words of Zheng Xuan and Wang Bi?
translations.idiomatic: Hearing Tuo's words, he smiled leisurely and said, "What use are the words of Zheng Xuan and Wang Bi?

sentences.zh: 久之，微有辯答，所說辭義，皆異先儒之旨，而思理玄妙。

translations.literal: After a long while he offered a slight reply; what he said in meaning differed from earlier Confucians, yet the reasoning was abstruse and subtle.
translations.idiomatic: After a long while he offered a slight reply; what he said differed from earlier Confucians in meaning, yet the reasoning was abstruse and subtle.

sentences.zh: 故論者以為天然獨得，非常人所及也。

translations.literal: Therefore critics held that he had attained understanding by natural endowment alone, beyond what ordinary men could reach.
translations.idiomatic: Critics therefore held that he had attained understanding by natural endowment alone, beyond what ordinary men could reach.

sentences.zh: 竟以壽終。

translations.literal: In the end he died at a full span of years.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he died at a full span of years.

sentences.zh: 臨孝恭，京兆人也。

translations.literal: Lin Xiaogong was a native of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Lin Xiaogong was a native of Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 明天文、算術，隋文帝甚親遇之。

translations.literal: He understood astronomy and mathematics; Emperor Wen of Sui treated him with great familiarity.
translations.idiomatic: He understood astronomy and mathematics; Emperor Wen treated him with great familiarity.

sentences.zh: 每言災祥之事，未嘗不中。

translations.literal: Whenever he spoke of omens of disaster and blessing, he was never wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he spoke of omens of disaster and blessing, he was never wrong.

sentences.zh: 上因令考定陰陽書，官至上儀同。

translations.literal: The emperor therefore ordered him to examine and establish yin-yang texts; he reached the office of Superlative Companion of the First Rank.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor therefore ordered him to examine and establish yin-yang texts; he rose to Superlative Companion of the First Rank.

sentences.zh: 著《欹器圖》三卷，《地動銅儀經》一卷，《九宮五墓》一卷，《遁甲錄》十卷，《元辰經》十卷，《元辰厄》百九卷，《百怪書》十八卷，《祿命書》二十卷，《九宮龜經》一百一十卷，《太一式經》三十卷，《孔子馬頭易卜書》一卷，並行於世。

translations.literal: He authored Tilted-Vessel Diagrams in three scrolls, Classic of the Earthquake Bronze Instrument in one scroll, Nine Palaces and Five Tombs in one scroll, Records of Dunjia in ten scrolls, Classic of the Origin Hour in ten scrolls, Calamities of the Origin Hour in one hundred nine scrolls, Book of a Hundred Marvels in eighteen scrolls, Book of Official Salary and Destiny in twenty scrolls, Classic of the Nine Palaces Tortoise in one hundred ten scrolls, Classic of the Grand Unity Style in thirty scrolls, and Confucius's Horse-Head Changes Divination Book in one scroll — all circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote Tilted-Vessel Diagrams in three scrolls, Classic of the Earthquake Bronze Instrument in one scroll, Nine Palaces and Five Tombs in one scroll, Records of Dunjia in ten scrolls, Classic of the Origin Hour in ten scrolls, Calamities of the Origin Hour in one hundred nine scrolls, Book of a Hundred Marvels in eighteen scrolls, Book of Official Salary and Destiny in twenty scrolls, Classic of the Nine Palaces Tortoise in one hundred ten scrolls, Classic of the Grand Unity Style in thirty scrolls, and Confucius's Horse-Head Changes Divination Book in one scroll — all circulated in the world.

sentences.zh: 劉祐，滎陽人也。

translations.literal: Liu You was a native of Xingyang.
translations.idiomatic: Liu You was a native of Xingyang.

sentences.zh: 隋開皇初，為大都督，封索盧縣公。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaihuang in Sui he was made Grand Commander and enfeoffed as Duke of Suolu County.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Sui's Kaihuang era he was made Grand Commander and enfeoffed as Duke of Suolu County.

sentences.zh: 其所占候，合如符契，文帝甚親之。

translations.literal: His prognostications accorded like matching tally halves; Emperor Wen treated him with great familiarity.
translations.idiomatic: His prognostications matched like tally halves; Emperor Wen treated him with great familiarity.

sentences.zh: 初與張賓、劉暉、馬顯定曆。

translations.literal: At first, together with Zhang Bin, Liu Hui, and Ma Xian, he fixed the calendar.
translations.idiomatic: At first, together with Zhang Bin, Liu Hui, and Ma Xian, he fixed the calendar.

sentences.zh: 後奉詔撰兵書十卷，名曰《金韜》，上善之。

translations.literal: Later, by imperial order he compiled a military book in ten scrolls entitled Golden Strategies; the emperor approved it.
translations.idiomatic: Later, by imperial order he compiled a military book in ten scrolls entitled Golden Strategies; the emperor approved it.

sentences.zh: 復著《陰策》二十卷，《觀台飛候》六卷，《玄象要記》五卷，《律曆術文》一卷，《婚姻志》三卷，《產乳志》二卷，《式經》四卷，《四時立成法》一卷，《安曆志》十二卷，《歸正易》十卷，並行於世。

translations.literal: He also authored Secret Strategies in twenty scrolls, Observing the Platform and Flying Omens in six scrolls, Essential Records of Mysterious Phenomena in five scrolls, Text on Calendrical and Mathematical Arts in one scroll, Records of Marriage in three scrolls, Records of Childbirth in two scrolls, Classic of Forms in four scrolls, Method of Establishing the Four Seasons in one scroll, Classic of Secure Calendars in twelve scrolls, and Returning to the Correct Changes in ten scrolls — all circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote Secret Strategies in twenty scrolls, Observing the Platform and Flying Omens in six scrolls, Essential Records of Mysterious Phenomena in five scrolls, Text on Calendrical and Mathematical Arts in one scroll, Records of Marriage in three scrolls, Records of Childbirth in two scrolls, Classic of Forms in four scrolls, Method of Establishing the Four Seasons in one scroll, Classic of Secure Calendars in twelve scrolls, and Returning to the Correct Changes in ten scrolls — all circulated in the world.

sentences.zh: 張胄玄，勃海蓚人也。

translations.literal: Zhang Zhouxuan was a native of Liu in Bohai.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhouxuan was a native of Liu in Bohai.

sentences.zh: 博學多通，尤精術數。

translations.literal: Learned and broadly skilled, he was especially expert in numerical arts.
translations.idiomatic: He was learned and widely accomplished, and especially skilled in numerical arts.

sentences.zh: 冀州刺史趙煚薦之，隋文帝征授雲騎尉，直太史，參議律曆事。

translations.literal: Governor Zhao Shuang of Jizhou recommended him; Emperor Wen of Sui summoned and appointed him Cloud Cavalry Commandant, serving in the Directorate of Astronomy to discuss calendrical and mathematical affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Zhao Shuang of Jizhou recommended him; Emperor Wen summoned him and appointed him Cloud Cavalry Commandant, serving in the Directorate of Astronomy on calendrical and mathematical affairs.

sentences.zh: 時輩多出其下，由是太史令劉暉等甚忌之。

translations.literal: Most contemporaries ranked below him; for this Director of Astronomy Liu Hui and the others greatly resented him.
translations.idiomatic: Most of his contemporaries ranked below him; for this Director Liu Hui and the others greatly resented him.

sentences.zh: 然暉言多不中，胄玄所推步甚精密。

translations.literal: Yet Hui's pronouncements often missed, while Zhouxuan's calculations were very precise.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Hui's pronouncements often missed, while Zhouxuan's calculations were very precise.

sentences.zh: 上異之，令楊素與術士數人，立議六十一事，皆舊法久難通者，令暉與胄玄等辯析之。

translations.literal: The emperor was astonished and ordered Yang Su and several technicians to set up debate on sixty-one matters — all old methods long difficult to apply — and had Hui and Zhouxuan and others analyze them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was astonished and ordered Yang Su and several technicians to set up debate on sixty-one points — all old methods long difficult to apply — and had Hui and Zhouxuan and others analyze them.

sentences.zh: 暉杜口一無所答，胄玄通者五十四焉。

translations.literal: Hui shut his mouth and answered not one; Zhouxuan mastered fifty-four.
translations.idiomatic: Hui shut his mouth and answered not one; Zhouxuan mastered fifty-four.

sentences.zh: 由是擢拜員外散騎侍郎，兼太史令，賜物千段。

translations.literal: For this he was promoted to Supernumerary Palace Attendant and concurrently Director of Astronomy, and bestowed one thousand bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: For this he was promoted to Supernumerary Palace Attendant and concurrently Director of Astronomy, and bestowed one thousand bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 暉及黨與八人，皆斥逐之。

translations.literal: Hui and his faction of eight were all dismissed and driven away.
translations.idiomatic: Hui and his faction of eight were all dismissed and driven away.

sentences.zh: 改定新曆，言前曆差一日。

translations.literal: He revised and fixed the new calendar, saying the previous calendar was off by one day.
translations.idiomatic: He revised and fixed the new calendar, saying the previous calendar was off by one day.

sentences.zh: 內史通事顏慜楚上言曰：「漢時落下閎改《顓頊曆》，作《太初曆》，云：'後當差一日，八百年當有聖者定之。

translations.literal: Yan Mintu, Master of Documents for General Affairs, submitted saying: 'In Han times Luoxia Hong revised the Zhuanxu Calendar and made the Taichu Calendar, saying: "Later there will be an error of one day; after eight hundred years a sage will fix it.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Mintu, Master of Documents for General Affairs, submitted saying, "In Han times Luoxia Hong revised the Zhuanxu Calendar and made the Taichu Calendar, saying, 'Later there will be an error of one day; after eight hundred years a sage will fix it.

sentences.zh: '計今相去七百一十年，術者舉其成數，聖者之謂，其在今乎！」

translations.literal: Calculating from now, seven hundred ten years have passed; the technicians cite the round number, and 'the sage' — does it not refer to the present?"
translations.idiomatic: Calculating from now, seven hundred ten years have passed; the technicians cite the round number — does 'the sage' not refer to the present?'

sentences.zh: 上大悅，漸見親用。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased and gradually came to employ him with familiarity.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was greatly pleased and gradually came to employ him with familiarity.

sentences.zh: 胄玄所謂曆法，與古不同者三事：其一，宋祖沖之于歲周之末，創設差分，冬至漸移，不循舊軌，每四十六年，卻差一度。

translations.literal: Zhouxuan's calendrical methods differed from antiquity in three matters: First, Song ancestor Zu Chongzhi, at the end of the year's circuit, created differential correction; the winter solstice gradually shifted and no longer followed the old track — every forty-six years it retreated one degree.
translations.idiomatic: Zhouxuan's calendrical methods differed from antiquity in three matters. First: Song ancestor Zu Chongzhi, at the end of the year's circuit, created differential correction; the winter solstice gradually shifted and no longer followed the old track — every forty-six years it retreated one degree.

sentences.zh: 至梁虞廣刂曆法，嫌沖之所差太多，因以一百八十六年，冬至移一度。

translations.literal: When Liang's Yu Kuai revised the calendar method, finding Zu Chongzhi's correction too great, he therefore used one hundred eighty-six years for the winter solstice to shift one degree.
translations.idiomatic: When Liang's Yu Kuai revised the calendar method, finding Zu Chongzhi's correction too great, he used one hundred eighty-six years for the winter solstice to shift one degree.

sentences.zh: 胄玄以此二術，年限縣隔，追檢古注，所失極多。

translations.literal: Zhouxuan, because these two methods were far apart in their year-counts, traced and examined ancient commentaries and found extremely many errors.
translations.idiomatic: Zhouxuan, because these two methods were far apart in their year-counts, traced and examined ancient commentaries and found extremely many errors.

sentences.zh: 遂折中兩家，以為度法，冬至所宿，歲別漸移，八十三年，卻行一度。

translations.literal: He then split the difference between the two schools to make a degree method: the winter solstice's lodge gradually shifts, and every eighty-three years it retreats one degree.
translations.idiomatic: He then split the difference between the two schools to make a degree method: the winter solstice's lodge gradually shifts, and every eighty-three years it retreats one degree.

sentences.zh: 則上合堯時，日永星火；

translations.literal: Then it matched above with the time of Yao, when days were longest and the Fire Star stood at its culmination;
translations.idiomatic: Then it matched above with the time of Yao, when days were longest and the Fire Star stood at its culmination;

sentences.zh: 次符漢曆，宿起牛初。

translations.literal: next it accorded with the Han calendar, with lodges beginning at the start of Ox.
translations.idiomatic: next it accorded with the Han calendar, with lodges beginning at the start of Ox.

sentences.zh: 明其前後，並皆密當。

translations.literal: Before and after, all were closely fitting.
translations.idiomatic: Before and after, all were closely fitting.

sentences.zh: 其二，周馬顯造《丙寅元曆》，有陰陽轉法，加減章分，進退蝕餘，乃推定日，創開此數。

translations.literal: Second, Zhou's Ma Xian created the Jiyin Origin Calendar, with yin-yang conversion methods, adding and subtracting cycle parts, advancing and retreating eclipse remainders — thus calculating the fixed day and opening this reckoning.
translations.idiomatic: Second: Northern Zhou's Ma Xian created the Jiyin Origin Calendar, with yin-yang conversion methods, adding and subtracting cycle parts, advancing and retreating eclipse remainders — thus calculating the fixed day and opening this reckoning.

sentences.zh: 當時術者，多不能曉。

translations.literal: Technicians of the time mostly could not understand it.
translations.idiomatic: Technicians of the time mostly could not understand it.

sentences.zh: 張賓因而用之，莫能考正。

translations.literal: Zhang Bin therefore used it but could not examine and correct it.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Bin therefore used it but could not examine and correct it.

sentences.zh: 胄玄以為加時先後，逐氣參差，就月為斷，於理未可。

translations.literal: Zhouxuan held that the sequence of added hours, following qi in succession, taking the month as the cut-off, was not acceptable in principle.
translations.idiomatic: Zhouxuan held that the sequence of added hours, following qi in succession and taking the month as the cut-off, was not acceptable in principle.

sentences.zh: 乃因二十四氣，列其盈縮所出。

translations.literal: He therefore arranged the twenty-four qi and listed their excess and deficit as they arose.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore arranged the twenty-four qi and listed their excess and deficit as they arose.

sentences.zh: 實由日行遲，則月逐日易及，令合朔加時早；

translations.literal: In truth, when the sun's motion is slow, the moon day by day easily catches up, making the added hour of conjunction early;
translations.idiomatic: In truth, when the sun's motion is slow, the moon day by day easily catches up, making the added hour of conjunction early;

sentences.zh: 日行速，則月逐日少遲，令合朔加時晚。

translations.literal: when the sun's motion is fast, the moon day by day falls somewhat behind, making the added hour of conjunction late.
translations.idiomatic: when the sun's motion is fast, the moon day by day falls somewhat behind, making the added hour of conjunction late.

sentences.zh: 檢前代加時早晚，以為損益之率。

translations.literal: Examining added hours early and late in previous dynasties, he took them as rates of increase and decrease.
translations.idiomatic: Examining added hours early and late in previous dynasties, he took them as rates of increase and decrease.

sentences.zh: 日行，自秋分已後至春分，其勢速，計一百八十二日而行一百八十度；

translations.literal: The sun's motion, from after the autumn equinox until the spring equinox, is rapid — in one hundred eighty-two days it travels one hundred eighty degrees;
translations.idiomatic: The sun's motion, from after the autumn equinox until the spring equinox, is rapid — in one hundred eighty-two days it travels one hundred eighty degrees;

sentences.zh: 自春分已後至秋分，日行遲，計一百八十二日而行一百七十六度。

translations.literal: from after the spring equinox until the autumn equinox, the sun's motion is slow — in one hundred eighty-two days it travels one hundred seventy-six degrees.
translations.idiomatic: from after the spring equinox until the autumn equinox, the sun's motion is slow — in one hundred eighty-two days it travels one hundred seventy-six degrees.

sentences.zh: 每氣之下，即其率也。

translations.literal: Below each qi lies its rate.
translations.idiomatic: Below each qi lies its rate.

sentences.zh: 其三，自古諸曆，朔望逢交，不問內外，入限便蝕。

translations.literal: Third, in calendars of antiquity, when new and full moon met crossing, regardless of inner or outer limit, upon entering the limit there was eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: Third: in calendars of antiquity, when new and full moon met crossing, regardless of inner or outer limit, upon entering the limit there was eclipse.

sentences.zh: 張賓立法，創有外限，應蝕不蝕，猶未能明。

translations.literal: Zhang Bin's law created an outer limit; eclipses that should occur did not occur — yet this was still not clear.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Bin's law created an outer limit; eclipses that should occur did not occur — yet this was still not clear.

sentences.zh: 胄玄以日行黃道，歲一周天；

translations.literal: Zhouxuan held that the sun travels the yellow path and completes one circuit of heaven in a year;
translations.idiomatic: Zhouxuan held that the sun travels the yellow path and completes one circuit of heaven in a year;

sentences.zh: 月行月道，二十七日有餘一周天。

translations.literal: the moon travels the lunar path and completes one circuit in twenty-seven-plus days.
translations.idiomatic: the moon travels the lunar path and completes one circuit in twenty-seven-plus days.

sentences.zh: 月道交絡黃道，每行黃道內十三日有奇而出，又行道外十三日有奇而入，終而復始。

translations.literal: The lunar path intersects the yellow path; each time it travels thirteen-plus days within the yellow path and emerges, then travels thirteen-plus days outside and enters again — ending and beginning anew.
translations.idiomatic: The lunar path intersects the yellow path; each time it travels thirteen-plus days within the yellow path and emerges, then travels thirteen-plus days outside and enters again — ending and beginning anew.

sentences.zh: 月經黃道，謂之交。

translations.literal: When the moon crosses the yellow path, it is called crossing.
translations.idiomatic: When the moon crosses the yellow path, it is called crossing.

sentences.zh: 朔望去交前後各五度以下，即為當蝕。

translations.literal: If new or full moon departs from crossing by five degrees or less before or after, there will be eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: If new or full moon departs from crossing by five degrees or less before or after, there will be eclipse.

sentences.zh: 若月行內道，則在黃道之北，蝕多有驗；

translations.literal: If the moon travels the inner path, it is north of the yellow path, and eclipses mostly verify;
translations.idiomatic: If the moon travels the inner path, it is north of the yellow path, and eclipses mostly verify;

sentences.zh: 月行外道，在黃道之南也，雖遇正人，無由掩映，蝕多不驗。

translations.literal: if the moon travels the outer path, south of the yellow path, even if it meets the sun directly there is no covering and shadowing — eclipses mostly do not verify.
translations.idiomatic: if the moon travels the outer path, south of the yellow path, even if it meets the sun directly there is no covering and shadowing — eclipses mostly do not verify.

sentences.zh: 遂因前法，別立定限，隨交遠近，逐氣求差，損益蝕分，事皆明著。

translations.literal: He therefore followed the previous method, separately establishing fixed limits, following crossing distance near and far, seeking difference according to qi, increasing and decreasing eclipse parts — the matter all clearly shown.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore followed the previous method, separately establishing fixed limits, following crossing distance near and far, seeking difference according to qi, increasing and decreasing eclipse parts — the matter all clearly shown.

sentences.zh: 其超古獨異者有七事：其一，古曆五星行度，皆守恆率，見伏盈縮，悉無格准。

translations.literal: His surpassing antiquity and standing alone had seven matters: First, in ancient calendars the five planets' degrees of motion all kept constant rates; appearance, hiding, excess, and deficit all had no standard measure.
translations.idiomatic: His surpassing antiquity and standing alone had seven matters. First: in ancient calendars the five planets' degrees of motion all kept constant rates; appearance, hiding, excess, and deficit all had no standard measure.

sentences.zh: 胄玄候之，各得真率，合見之數，與古不同。

translations.literal: Zhouxuan observed them and obtained each true rate; the numbers of conjunction differed from antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Zhouxuan observed them and obtained each true rate; the numbers of conjunction differed from antiquity.

sentences.zh: 其差多者，至加減三十許日。

translations.literal: Where the difference was greatest, it reached adding or subtracting about thirty days.
translations.idiomatic: Where the difference was greatest, it reached adding or subtracting about thirty days.

sentences.zh: 即如熒惑，平見在雨水氣，即均加二十九日；

translations.literal: Take Mars: its mean appearance is in the Rain Water qi — uniformly add twenty-nine days;
translations.idiomatic: Take Mars: its mean appearance is in the Rain Water qi — uniformly add twenty-nine days;

sentences.zh: 見在小雪氣，則均減二十五日。
